questions.q: Which of the following techniques is most suitable for separating a solid mixture of ammonium chloride and sodium chloride?
questions.e: Ammonium chloride sublimes on heating, changing directly from solid to gas, while sodium chloride does not. Therefore, heating the mixture will cause ammonium chloride to vaporize and re-deposit on a cooler surface, leaving sodium chloride behind.
questions.p: Na ammonium chloride dey sublime when you heat am, e dey turn straight from solid to gas, but sodium chloride no dey do like that. So if you heat the mix, ammonium chloride go turn gas and go jam cold place, leave sodium chloride for down.

questions.q: During the laboratory preparation of dry oxygen gas using potassium chlorate, manganese(IV) oxide is added and the gas is collected over water. Which separation method is primarily used to remove water vapor from the collected oxygen?
o: Filtering the gas through filter paper
Freezing the gas mixture to -20° C
Passing the gas through concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
questions.e: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is a powerful drying agent that absorbs moisture from gases bubbled through it. It is commonly used to dry gases that do not react with acid, such as oxygen.
questions.p: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid na strong drying agent wey dey suck water commot from gas when you pass am inside. Na him people dey use dry gas like oxygen wey no dey react with acid.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the correct procedure to obtain pure water from a sample of muddy well water containing dissolved table salt?
o: Filtration followed by evaporation to dryness
Using a separating funnel followed by chromatography
questions.e: Filtration removes insoluble mud particles, leaving a clear solution of salt water. Simple distillation is then used to boil off the water and condense its vapor into pure water, leaving the salt behind.
questions.p: Filtration go remove mud wey no dey dissolve, then salt water remain. Na simple distillation you go come use boil the water make e turn gas, then cool am back to pure water, while salt stay for pot.

questions.q: During paper chromatography of a black ink sample using ethanol as the solvent, component X travels 6.0 cm from the baseline while the solvent front travels 8.0 cm. What is the retardation factor (Rf) of component X?
questions.e: The Rf value is calculated as the distance moved by the substance divided by the distance moved by the solvent front. Thus, Rf = 6.0 / 8.0 = 0.75.
questions.p: Rf value na distance wey substance travel divide by distance wey solvent front travel. So na 6.0 divide by 8.0, wey give us 0.75.

questions.q: In an experiment to determine if a colourless liquid sample of borehole water is pure, which of the following physical criteria is the most reliable?
o: It has a neutral pH of exactly 7.0 at room temperature
It boils completely and constantly at exactly 100° C at 1 atm pressure
It leaves no residue when evaporated on a watch glass
It has no smell or visible particles
questions.e: A pure liquid has a fixed and sharp boiling point at a given pressure. Pure water boils constantly at 100° C under standard atmospheric pressure, whereas impure liquids boil over a temperature range.
questions.p: Pure liquid must get fixed boiling point. Na only pure water dey boil straight at 100° C under normal pressure; if dirt or salt dey inside, temperature go dey rise as e dey boil.

questions.q: A solid mixture contains iron filings, sand, and sodium chloride. A student added excess water, stirred, and filtered the mixture. What is present in the filtrate?
questions.e: Iron filings are magnetic and insoluble, sand is insoluble, but sodium chloride dissolves completely in water. When filtered, the sand and iron remain on the filter paper as residue, while the dissolved salt passes through as the filtrate.
questions.p: Iron na magnet and no dey dissolve, sand no dey dissolve too, but sodium chloride dey dissolve inside water. When you filter am, sand and iron go stay for filter paper as residue, while salt water go pass go down as filtrate.

questions.q: According to the kinetic theory of gases, which of the following best describes the collisions between gas molecules in a closed container?
o: Perfectly elastic collisions where no overall loss of kinetic energy occurs
Inelastic collisions that result in a gradual loss of total kinetic energy
Collisions that cause molecules to permanently stick together upon impact
Collisions with the container walls only, without colliding with each other
questions.e: The kinetic theory assumes that all collisions between gas molecules, as well as between molecules and the container walls, are perfectly elastic. This means there is no net loss of total kinetic energy during these collisions.
questions.p: Kinetic theory talk say as gas molecules dey jam themselves and the container wall, those collision dey perfectly elastic. E mean say energy no dey lost for the collision at all.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about real gases compared to ideal gases is correct at very high pressures?
o: The actual pressure exerted is much lower than expected due to zero particle interaction
Real gases always obey Boyle's law perfectly under extreme pressure conditions
Intermolecular forces become completely negligible because molecules move faster
The volume occupied by the gas molecules themselves becomes significant compared to the container volume
questions.e: At very high pressures, gas molecules are squeezed close together. The actual volume of the gas particles themselves is no longer negligible compared to the total volume of the container.
questions.p: When pressure high gidigba, the gas molecules go pack themselves tight. That time, the space wey the molecules themselves take up no be small thing again when you compare am to the whole container.

questions.q: A gas X diffuses through a porous partition twice as fast as gas Y under the same conditions of temperature and pressure. If the molar mass of gas X is 16 g/mol, what is the molar mass of gas Y?
questions.e: According to Graham's law of diffusion, RateX / RateY = √(My / Mx). Given RateX = 2RateY, so 2 = √(My / 16). Squaring both sides gives 4 = My / 16, hence My = 64 g/mol.
questions.p: Apply Graham law: RateX over RateY equal to square root of My over Mx. Put the numbers inside, make you square both sides, and you go find say My na 64 g/mol.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions favors the liquefaction of a real gas?
questions.e: Gases liquefy when intermolecular forces hold molecules close together. Low temperatures reduce kinetic energy so molecules do not fly apart, and high pressures force molecules closer together.
questions.p: To turn gas to liquid, you need cold weather (low temperature) to slow down the molecules, and strong squeeze (high pressure) make dem pack close together.

questions.q: What is the pressure exerted by 0.5 mole of an ideal gas confined in a 10 dm³ container at 27 °C? (Take R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: Using the ideal gas equation PV = nRT. P = (nRT) / V = (0.5 × 0.0821 × 300) / 10 = 1.2315 atm, which rounds to 1.23 atm.
questions.p: Use PV = nRT. Make you multiply mole (0.5) times R (0.0821) times temperature in Kelvin (300 K), then divide everything by volume (10). Your answer na 1.23 atm.

questions.q: A sample of nitrogen gas is collected over water at 23 °C and a total barometric pressure of 745 mmHg. If the aqueous tension (vapor pressure of water) at 23 °C is 21 mmHg, what is the partial pressure of the dry nitrogen gas?
questions.e: According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, total pressure is the sum of the gas pressure and water vapor pressure. P(nitrogen) = P(total) - P(water vapor) = 745 - 21 = 724 mmHg.
questions.p: Dalton law talk say total pressure na the addition of gas pressure and water vapor pressure. Just minus 21 from 745, you go get 724 mmHg for the dry nitrogen.

questions.q: An element Z has two naturally occurring isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37, existing in the ratio 3:1 respectively. What is the relative atomic mass of element Z?
questions.e: The relative atomic mass is calculated as (35 x 3 + 37 x 1) / (3 + 1), which gives (105 + 37) / 4 = 142 / 4 = 35.5. This accounts for the weighted average of the isotopic masses based on their abundance ratio.
questions.p: To find the relative atomic mass, multiply each mass number by its ratio part, add dem together, and divide by the total ratio. Dat na (35 x 3 + 37 x 1) / 4, wey give 142 / 4 = 35.5.

questions.q: Which of the following electronic configurations represents an atom in an excited state?
questions.e: In the configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁵ 3s¹, one electron from the 2p orbital has been promoted to the higher 3s orbital. This absorption of energy characterizes an unstable excited state before dropping back to ground state.
questions.p: For dis configuration, one electron don jump leave 2p go enter 3s before 2p even full finish. E mean say energy don enter the atom and e dey excited state.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a shell with principal quantum number n = 3?
questions.e: The maximum capacity of electrons in any shell is given by the formula 2n². For n = 3, the maximum number of electrons is 2(3)² = 2 x 9 = 18.
questions.p: The formula to find maximum electron for any shell na 2n squared. When you put n = 3 inside, you get 2 times 9, wey be 18 electrons.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in a neutral nitrogen atom (atomic number 7)?
questions.e: Nitrogen has an electronic configuration of 1s² 2s² 2p³. According to Hund's rule, the three 2p electrons will occupy three separate degenerate orbitals singly, resulting in 3 unpaired electrons.
questions.p: Nitrogen get 7 electrons with configuration 1s² 2s² 2p³. When you arrange the three electrons for the 2p box, each one go stay alone for different box, so dem be 3 unpaired electrons.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is NOT permissible for an electron in an atom?
questions.e: The azimuthal quantum number (l) must range from 0 to n - 1. For n = 2, the maximum value of l is 1, so l = 2 is invalid and not permissible.
questions.p: The value of l must always dey less than n. If n na 2, l fit only be 0 or 1. Na why l = 2 no correct at all.

questions.q: An atom X has 18 electrons and 20 neutrons. What is the correct representation of this nuclide?
questions.e: The atomic number of X is equal to the number of electrons for a neutral atom, which is 18. The mass number is protons plus neutrons, 18 + 20 = 38, written as a superscript before the chemical symbol.
questions.p: For neutral atom, the number of electrons na same as proton number (18). Mass number na proton plus neutron (18 + 20 = 38). Na why e be 38 over 18 X.

questions.q: Which statement best describes isotopes of the same element?
o: They have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
They have the same chemical properties due to the same number of electrons
They have different numbers of valence electrons
They have different numbers of protons and neutrons
questions.e: Isotopes have the same atomic number and number of electrons, leading to identical chemical properties, but differ in the number of neutrons and hence mass numbers.
questions.p: Isotopes na same element wey get same number of electrons, na why their chemical behavior dey same. Na only their number of neutrons dey different.

questions.q: What is the total number of s-electrons present in a neutral atom of magnesium (atomic number 12)?
questions.e: The electronic configuration of magnesium is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s². Counting the electrons in all the s orbitals (1s², 2s², 3s²) gives 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 s-electrons.
questions.p: Magnesium configuration na 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s². Just count all the electrons wey dey inside s orbitals (2 for 1s, 2 for 2s, 2 for 3s), e go give you 6.

questions.q: The phenomenon where an element exists in two or more different physical forms in the same physical state is called:
questions.e: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different forms in the same physical state, such as graphite and diamond for carbon.
questions.p: When one element dey exist in different physical forms for the same state like carbon as diamond or graphite, we dey call am allotropy.

questions.q: An element X belongs to Group 3 and Period 3 of the Periodic Table. What is the formula of its stable oxide?
questions.e: Group 3 elements exhibit a valency of 3, meaning X forms an ion with a +3 charge (X₃+). Oxygen always forms an ion with a -2 charge (O₂-). Balancing the charges gives the formula X₂O₃.
questions.p: Group 3 elements dey carry +3 valency, and oxygen dey carry -2. When you cross them, you go get X₂O₃.

questions.q: Consider four elements represented by their atomic numbers: P (9), Q (11), R (17), and S (19). Which of these elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.e: Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right and decreases down a group. Among the given elements, P (Fluorine, atomic number 9) is at the top right of the halogen group, making it the most electronegative.
questions.p: Electronegativity dey increase as you go up and right for periodic table. Na P (Fluorine) dey top for halogen group, so naim electronegativity pass the rest.

questions.q: Moving from sodium to chlorine across the third period of the periodic table, which of the following properties decreases steadily?
questions.e: Across a period from left to right, nuclear charge increases, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus. This causes the atomic radius to decrease steadily across the period.
questions.p: As you dey move from left to right for period table, nuclear charge dey increase and draw electrons near. Naim make atomic radius dey reduce.

questions.q: Which of the following electronic configurations represents an element in the p-block of the periodic table?
questions.e: The block of an element is determined by the subshell that receives the last electron. Option B ends with 3p⁴, placing it in the p-block.
questions.p: The block of any element na the subshell wey last electron enter. Option B finish with 3p⁴, meaning say na p-block element.

questions.q: The elements in Group 0 (or 18) of the periodic table are chemically inert because they
o: are all gases at room temperature
questions.e: Group 0 elements have a stable duplet (for helium) or octet (for others) configuration in their outermost shell. This makes them chemically stable and unreactive.
questions.p: Group 0 elements get full outer shell, either two electrons for helium or eight for others. Because their house don complete, dem no dey react with anybody.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of elements shows diagonal relationship in the periodic table?
questions.e: Diagonal relationship occurs between certain adjacent elements in neighboring groups and periods, such as Lithium in Group 1 and Magnesium in Group 2, due to similar charge-to-radius ratios.
questions.p: Diagonal relationship dey happen between elements wey dey diagonal face-to-face for periodic table, like Lithium and Magnesium, because their properties resemble each other well well.

questions.q: The first ionization energy of magnesium is greater than that of sodium because magnesium has
questions.e: Magnesium has a higher nuclear charge (atomic number 12) than sodium (atomic number 11) in the same period. This stronger nuclear pull makes it harder to remove an electron from magnesium.
questions.p: Magnesium nuclear charge pass sodium own because e get atomic number 12 instead of 11. Dat strong pull make am harder to remove electron from magnesium.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric in nature?
questions.e: Aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) is amphoteric, meaning it can react with both acids and bases to form salt and water. Sodium oxide is basic, magnesium oxide is basic, and sulfur trioxide is acidic.
questions.p: Aluminium oxide na amphoteric oxide, meaning say e fit react with acid and also react with base. Na₂O and MgO na basic, while SO₃ na acidic.

questions.q: An atom M has an atomic number of 14. What is the nature of the oxide formed by M?
questions.e: An element with atomic number 14 is Silicon, which is a metalloid located in Group 4. Its oxide (silicon dioxide, SiO₂) is acidic in nature and reacts with strong alkalis.
questions.p: Atomic number 14 na Silicon, wey be metalloid for Group 4. E oxide (SiO₂) na acidic oxide, e dey react with strong base.

questions.q: Which of the following substances possesses both electrovalent and covalent bonds in its crystal lattice?
questions.e: Ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) contains an electrovalent bond between the ammonium ion and chloride ion, and covalent bonds (as well as a coordinate covalent bond) within the ammonium ion itself. The other options contain only one specific type of bond.
questions.p: Ammonium chloride get ionic bond between ammonium and chloride ions, and covalent bond inside the ammonium ion itself. E dey carry both types.

questions.q: The type of chemical bond formed by the complete transfer of one or more valence electrons from a metal to a non-metal is called
questions.e: Electrovalent or ionic bonding involves the complete transfer of electrons from electropositive metallic atoms to electronegative non-metallic atoms. This creates oppositely charged ions held by strong electrostatic forces.
questions.p: Electrovalent bond na when metal give non-metal electrons completely make both of them become ions wey attract each other.

questions.q: What is the primary factor that accounts for the exceptionally high boiling point of water compared to other hydrides of group 16 elements?
questions.e: Water molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds due to the high electronegativity of oxygen attached to hydrogen. These extra forces require more thermal energy to break, raising the boiling point.
questions.p: Na hydrogen bonding make water boiling point high reach like dat because oxygen dey pull electron well well, make water molecules hold body tight.

questions.q: Consider element X with atomic number 12 and element Y with atomic number 9. What is the standard chemical formula of the compound formed between X and Y?
questions.e: Element X is magnesium (group 2, valency 2) and Y is fluorine (group 17, valency 1). Combining them requires one X ion to two Y ions to balance charges, yielding XY₂.
questions.p: Magnesium get valency 2, fluorine get valency 1. To balance the charge, you need one magnesium and two fluorine atoms, na why e be XY₂.

questions.q: Which of the following molecules has a linear molecular geometry according to the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory?
questions.e: Beryllium chloride (BeCl₂) has two bond pairs around the central beryllium atom with no lone pairs, resulting in a linear geometry with a bond angle of 180 degrees. The others are bent, trigonal pyramidal, and tetrahedral respectively.
questions.p: BeCl₂ get two bond pairs and zero lone pair for center, na why e straight like ruler (linear) with 180 degrees angle.

questions.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity while diamond does not, even though both are allotropes of carbon?
o: Graphite has higher density than diamond
Diamond is gaseous at room temperature
Graphite contains free delocalized electrons in its layers
Diamond has ionic bonds instead of covalent bonds
questions.e: In graphite, each carbon atom uses three of its four valence electrons for bonding, leaving one electron per atom free and delocalized along the layers to carry current. Diamond uses all four valence electrons in rigid tetrahedral covalent bonds.
questions.p: Graphite get one free electron per carbon wey dey move about to carry current, but diamond use all im electrons tight for covalent bond.

questions.q: The attractive force that holds atoms together in a metallic crystal is best described as an electrostatic attraction between positive metal kernels and
o: mobile delocalized sea of valence electrons
shared pairs of inner shell electrons
questions.e: Metallic bonding involves positive metal ions (kernels) immersed in a sea of delocalized valence electrons that move freely throughout the crystal lattice, providing strength and conductivity.
questions.p: Metallic bond na like positive metal ions wey dey swim inside one sea of free electrons wey dey carry current up and down.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of elements will combine to form a compound with the most pronounced ionic character?
questions.e: Ionic character increases with a greater difference in electronegativity between the combining atoms. Sodium (Group 1) and fluorine (Group 17) have the largest electronegativity difference among the given pairs.
questions.p: Na sodium and fluorine go get the highest ionic character because their electronegativity difference wide pass all the other pairs.

questions.q: What type of intermolecular force is primarily responsible for holding liquid argon atoms together at very low temperatures?
questions.e: Argon is a noble gas made of single atoms. The only attractive forces possible between non-polar monoatomic particles are weak instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces, known as London dispersion forces.
questions.p: Argon na noble gas, e no get permanent pole. Na only small small London dispersion forces dey hold them together when temperature cold.

questions.q: A chemical bond in which both electrons of the shared pair originate from only one of the participating atoms is known as a
questions.e: A coordinate covalent bond, or dative bond, occurs when the shared pair of electrons comes entirely from a single donor atom possessing a lone pair. Once formed, it is identical to a normal covalent bond.
questions.p: Coordinate bond (dative bond) happen when na only one atom bring the two electrons wey dem dey share together.

questions.q: How many water molecules are contained in 0.5 moles of water, H₂O? [Avogadro's constant = 6.02 x 10²³]
questions.e: The number of particles is found by multiplying the number of moles by Avogadro's constant. Therefore, 0.5 moles x 6.02 x 10²³ = 3.01 x 10²³ molecules.
questions.p: To get number of molecules, multiply moles by Avogadro constant. So, 0.5 times 6.02 x 10²³ give us 3.01 x 10²³ molecules.

questions.q: What volume does 2.2 g of carbon dioxide gas, CO₂, occupy at standard temperature and pressure (STP)? [Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.e: Molar mass of CO₂ is 12 + (16 x 2) = 44 g/mol. Number of moles = 2.2 g / 44 g/mol = 0.05 mol. Volume = 0.05 mol x 22.4 dm³/mol = 1.12 dm³.
questions.p: First find mole of CO₂ by dividing mass 2.2 by molar mass 44, e give 0.05 mol. Then multiply by molar volume 22.4 to get 1.12 dm³.

questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in copper(II) oxide, CuO. [Cu = 64, O = 16]
questions.e: The molar mass of CuO is 64 + 16 = 80 g/mol. The percentage of oxygen is (Mass of O / Molar mass of CuO) x 100%, which is (16 / 80) x 100% = 20.0%.
questions.p: Total mass of CuO na 80 g/mol. Mass of oxygen na 16. Divide 16 by 80 and multiply by 100 to get 20.0 percent.

questions.q: An organic compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen, and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.e: Divide percentage by atomic masses: C = 40/12 = 3.33; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Dividing by the smallest (3.33) gives a mole ratio of C:H:O = 1:2:1, hence CH₂O.
questions.p: Divide each percentage by their atomic mass to get moles: C = 3.33, H = 6.7, O = 3.33. Divide all by the smallest one, you go get ratio 1 to 2 to 1, wey be CH₂O.

questions.q: What is the concentration of a sodium hydroxide solution in mol/dm³ if 20.0 cm³ of it is completely neutralized by 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid?
questions.e: Using (CaVa)/(CbVb) = Na/Nb for NaOH + HCl -> NaCl + H₂O, Ca = 0.1, Va = 25, Vb = 20, Na=1, Nb=1. Solving for Cb gives (0.1 x 25) / 20 = 0.125 mol/dm³.
questions.p: Use titration formula CaVa over CbVb equal to Na over Nb. Put the numbers inside: (0.1 x 25) divide by (20 x Cb) = 1/1, so Cb na 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.q: Consider the reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) -> 2NH₃(g). What volume of ammonia gas is produced when 50 cm³ of nitrogen gas reacts completely with excess hydrogen at room temperature and pressure?
questions.e: By Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes, 1 mole (or volume) of N₂ produces 2 moles (or volumes) of NH₃. Therefore, 50 cm³ of N₂ will produce 50 x 2 = 100 cm³ of NH₃.
questions.p: From the balanced equation, 1 volume of N₂ dey give 2 volumes of NH₃. So 50 cm³ of N₂ go produce 50 times 2, wey be 100 cm³.

questions.q: What is the mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃, present in 250 cm³ of a 0.2 mol/dm³ solution? [Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.e: Molar mass of Na₂CO₃ = (23 x 2) + 12 + (16 x 3) = 106 g/mol. Moles = concentration x volume in dm³ = 0.2 x (250/1000) = 0.05 mol. Mass = 0.05 x 106 = 5.30 g.
questions.p: Molar mass of Na₂CO₃ na 106 g/mol. Find moles by multiplying concentration with volume in dm³ (0.2 x 0.25 = 0.05 mol). Multiply moles by molar mass to get 5.30 g.

questions.q: If 10.0 g of calcium carbonate is strongly heated until no further change occurs, what mass of calcium oxide is obtained? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.e: Equation: CaCO₃ -> CaO + CO₂. 100 g of CaCO₃ gives 56 g of CaO. By proportion, 10.0 g of CaCO₃ will yield (56 / 100) x 10.0 = 5.60 g of CaO.
questions.p: From equation CaCO₃ give CaO + CO₂, 100 g of CaCO₃ dey produce 56 g of CaO. So, 10.0 g go produce (56 divide by 100) times 10, wey be 5.60 g.

questions.q: Which of the following contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.e: He has 1 atom/molecule (1 mole atoms). Cl₂ has 2 atoms/molecule x 2 moles = 4 moles of atoms. H₂O has 3 atoms/molecule x 1 mole = 3 moles of atoms. CH₄ has 5 atoms/molecule x 1.5 moles = 7.5 moles of atoms, making it the highest.
questions.p: Check total atoms for each: He get 1 mole atoms. Cl₂ get 4 moles atoms. H₂O get 3 moles atoms. CH₄ get 5 atoms per molecule, so 1.5 moles give 7.5 moles of atoms, highest be that!

questions.q: What is the conjugate base of the hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) ion, HCO₃-?
questions.e: A conjugate base is formed when an acid donates a proton (H+). Removing a proton from HCO₃- leaves CO₃²⁻ with a 2- charge.
questions.p: Conjugate base na wetin remain when acid throw away one hydrogen ion (H+). If you collect H+ from HCO₃-, na CO₃²⁻ go remain.

questions.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.005 mol/dm³ solution of sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄), assuming complete dissociation.
questions.e: H₂SO₄ is a strong dibasic acid, so [H+] = 2 x 0.005 = 0.01 mol/dm³. The pH is -log10(0.01), which equals 2.00.
questions.p: H₂SO₄ na strong dibasic acid, so concentration of hydrogen ion be 2 times 0.005, wey be 0.01. When you find -log of 0.01, e go give you 2.00.

questions.q: Which of the following salts undergoes cationic hydrolysis in aqueous solution to give an acidic solution?
questions.e: Ammonium chloride is formed from a weak base (NH₃) and a strong acid (HCl). Its cation (NH₄+) reacts with water to produce H+ ions, making the solution acidic.
questions.p: Na only ammonium chloride wey come from weak base and strong acid dey undergo hydrolysis to make water acidic because of the NH₄+ ion.

questions.q: What volume of 0.1 mol/dm³ NaOH solution is required to completely neutralize 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid?
questions.e: Using (CaVa)/(CbVb) = nA/nB where nA=1 and nB=1, (0.2 x 25.0)/(0.1 x Vb) = 1/1. Solving for Vb gives (0.2 x 25.0)/0.1 = 50.0 cm³.
questions.p: Use formula (CaVa)/(CbVb) = na/nb. Multiply 0.2 by 25 and divide by 0.1 to get 50 cm³.

questions.q: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating weak ethanoic acid against strong sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.e: Phenolphthalein changes colour in the alkaline pH range (8.3 to 10.0), which matches the pH at the equivalence point of a weak acid and strong base titration.
questions.p: For weak acid and strong base titration, the endpoint dey alkaline side, na why phenolphthalein wey dey change colour for high pH be the best.

questions.q: An oxide which reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water only is described as:
questions.e: Amphoteric oxides, such as zinc oxide and aluminium oxide, show both acidic and basic properties when reacting with acids and alkalis.
questions.p: Amphoteric oxide na bad guy wey fit pack with both acid and base to make salt and water. Examples na zinc oxide and aluminium oxide.

questions.q: Which of the following substances does not behave as an electrolyte when dissolved in pure water?
questions.e: Ethanol is a covalent organic compound that does not ionize or dissociate into ions in water, hence it is a non-electrolyte.
questions.p: Ethanol na organic compound wey no dey break down to form ions inside water, naim make am non-electrolyte.

questions.q: If 20.0 cm³ of a dibasic acid neutralizes 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH, what is the molar concentration of the acid?
questions.e: Mole of NaOH = (0.2 x 25)/1000 = 0.005 mol. Since acid is dibasic, mole of acid = 0.005 / 2 = 0.0025 mol. Concentration = 0.0025 / 0.020 = 0.125 mol/dm³.
questions.p: Find mole of NaOH first, then divide by 2 because the acid na dibasic. Divide that mole by volume of acid in dm³ to get 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.q: What happens to the pH of a 1.0 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid solution when it is diluted 100 times with distilled water?
questions.e: Diluting a strong acid 100 times increases the volume by a factor of 10², decreasing [H+] by 100 and thus increasing the pH by 2 units (from 0 to 2).
questions.p: If you dilute acid 100 times, concentration of H+ go reduce by 100 times, meaning pH go go up by 2 steps because of log scale.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII), KMnO₄?
questions.e: Potassium has an oxidation number of +1 and oxygen has -2. Let the oxidation number of Mn be x. Therefore, (+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0, which gives 1 + x - 8 = 0, leading to x = +7.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds, when present in water bodies via agricultural runoff, is the primary driver of eutrophication leading to aquatic pollution?
questions.e: Nitrates and phosphates from fertilizers wash into water bodies, causing rapid algal blooms that deplete dissolved oxygen and pollute the ecosystem.
questions.p: Nitrates and phosphates from fertilizer wey rain wash enter river dey make algae grow too much, and this one dey kill fish by reducing oxygen.

questions.q: Catalytic converters are installed in modern automobile exhaust systems primarily to reduce the emission of which combination of pollutants?
o: Carbon(IV) oxide, water vapour and nitrogen
Particulate matter, ammonia and hydrogen sulphide
Carbon(II) oxide, unburnt hydrocarbons and oxides of nitrogen
questions.e: Catalytic converters use redox catalysts to convert harmful carbon(II) oxide, unburnt hydrocarbons, and nitrogen oxides into harmless carbon(IV) oxide, water, and nitrogen gas.
questions.p: Catalytic converter dey help motor change bad gases like CO, hydrocarbons and NOx into harmless nitrogen, water and CO(2) before e commot for exhaust.

questions.q: Which of the following drying agents is most suitable for drying ammonia gas?
questions.e: Ammonia is a basic gas and will react with acidic drying agents like H₂SO₄ and P₂O₅. Anhydrous CaCl₂ forms a coordination complex with ammonia, leaving calcium oxide (quicklime) as the only suitable basic drying agent.
questions.p: Ammonia na basic gas, so e dey react with acid drying agents like H₂SO₄. Calcium chloride dey form complex with am, na only calcium oxide remain wey be basic enough to dry am well.

questions.q: In the industrial preparation of nitric acid by the Ostwald process, the catalytic oxidation of ammonia is achieved using which of the following catalysts?
questions.e: The Ostwald process involves the catalytic oxidation of ammonia to nitrogen(II) oxide using a heated platinum-rhodium catalyst at about 900° C.
questions.p: For Ostwald process to make nitric acid, dem dey use hot platinum-rhodium gauze as catalyst to oxidize ammonia make e turn to nitrogen(II) oxide.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is bubbled into an aqueous solution of potassium iodide. What observation is made?
o: Effervescence of a pungent gas occurs
questions.e: Chlorine is a stronger halogen than iodine and displaces it from potassium iodide solution. The liberated iodine dissolves in the solution, turning it a characteristic red-brown colour.
questions.p: Chlorine strong pass iodine, so e go push iodine comot from potassium iodide. As the iodine free, the water go turn red-brown colour.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in sodium tetrathionate, Na₂S₄O₆?
questions.e: Let the oxidation number of sulphur be x. For Na₂S₄O₆: 2(+1) + 4(x) + 6(-2) = 0, which gives 2 + 4x - 12 = 0, so 4x = 10, and x = +2.5.
questions.p: Make sulphur oxidation number be x. Do sodium (+1) times 2 plus 4x plus oxygen (-2) times 6 equal to zero. Solve am, you go get 4x = 10, so x = +2.5.

questions.q: Which of the following allotropes of sulphur is stable at room temperature and exists as octahedral crystals?
questions.e: Rhombic sulphur (or alpha-sulphur) is the stable allotrope of sulphur below 95.6° C and forms bright yellow octahedral crystals.
questions.p: Na rhombic sulphur be the stable one for normal room temperature, and e dey form fine yellow octahedral crystals.

questions.q: Hydrogen gas can be prepared in the laboratory by the action of dilute hydrochloric acid on which of the following metals?
questions.e: Zinc is above hydrogen in the electrochemical series and reacts readily with dilute non-oxidising acids like HCl to liberate hydrogen gas. Copper, silver, and gold are below hydrogen and do not react.
questions.p: Zinc dey up for electrochemical series pass hydrogen, so e fit react with dilute HCl to release hydrogen gas. Copper, silver and gold no fit do am.

questions.q: During the industrial manufacture of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid by the Contact process, sulphur(VI) oxide is dissolved in concentrated H₂SO₄ to form an intermediate product known as:
questions.e: In the Contact process, SO₃ is not dissolved directly in water (which causes a dangerous mist) but absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to produce pyrosulphuric acid, commonly called oleum (H₂S₂O₇).
questions.p: For Contact process, dem no dey put SO₃ straight inside water because e go cause dangerous mist. Dem dey dissolve am inside concentrated H₂SO₄ to form oleum first.

questions.q: Which of the following ores is primarily used for the industrial extraction of aluminium?
questions.e: Bauxite, which is hydrated aluminium oxide, is the principal and most economic ore used for extracting aluminium via the Hall-Héroult process. Haematite is for iron, malachite for copper, and galena for lead.
questions.p: Na bauxite dem dey use take extract aluminium for industry, because na hin get plenty aluminium oxide inside. Haematite na for iron, malachite na for copper.

questions.q: During the extraction of iron in the blast furnace, what is the primary role of limestone (calcium carbonate)?
o: To remove acidic impurities by forming slag
To act as a catalyst for the combustion of coke
To provide the carbon monoxide needed for reduction
To reduce iron(III) oxide to iron metal
questions.e: Limestone decomposes to calcium oxide, which reacts with acidic silicon dioxide impurities in the ore to form molten calcium silicate, known as slag. This slag floats on the molten iron and helps purify it.
questions.p: Limestone dey decompose to calcium oxide, wey come join sand impurity to form slag. Na dat slag dey float for top make dem remove am easily.

questions.q: Which of the following metals is extracted commercially by the electrolytic reduction of its fused chloride or oxide, rather than by chemical reduction with carbon?
questions.e: Aluminium is a very reactive metal high up in the electrochemical series; its oxide cannot be reduced by carbon because it has a very high affinity for oxygen. Hence, it requires electrolysis.
questions.p: Aluminium dey too reactive, so carbon no fit collect oxygen from am. Na electrolytic reduction dem dey use am.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy consisting primarily of which of the following pairs of metals?
questions.e: Brass is a well-known alloy made mainly of copper and zinc, which gives it a bright golden appearance. Copper and tin make bronze, while iron and carbon make steel.
questions.p: Brass na alloy of copper and zinc. If na copper and tin, na bronze be dat.

questions.q: In the purification of impure copper by electrolysis, what material is used as the cathode?
questions.e: In electrolytic refining of copper, the impure copper serves as the anode, while a thin strip of pure copper serves as the cathode where pure copper ions are deposited.
questions.p: For copper purification, pure copper strip na hin be cathode, while the dirty impure copper na hin be anode.

questions.q: Alnico, an important alloy used for making permanent magnets, contains aluminium, nickel, cobalt, and which other metal?
questions.e: Alnico is an acronym derived from its main metallic components: Aluminium (Al), Nickel (Ni), Cobalt (Co), and Iron (Fe). It is widely used for strong permanent magnets.
questions.p: Alnico name come from Aluminium, Nickel, Cobalt, and Iron. Dem dey use am make strong magnet.

questions.q: What is the main chemical agent that actually reduces iron(III) oxide to iron in the lower and middle sections of a blast furnace?
questions.e: Although coke (carbon) is burnt to produce heat and carbon dioxide, the actual reducing agent that strips oxygen from iron(III) oxide in the furnace is carbon monoxide gas.
questions.p: Even though coke dey burn, na carbon monoxide gas be the actual reducing agent wey dey collect oxygen from iron ore inside furnace.

questions.q: Which of the following alloys is specifically chosen for making electric fuse wires due to its low melting point?
questions.e: Solder, an alloy usually made of lead and tin, has a relatively low melting point, making it ideal for electrical connections and fuse wires that must melt when current exceeds safe limits.
questions.p: Solder wey contain lead and tin get low melting point, na hin make am good for fuse wire make e melt quick when current pass normal limit.

questions.q: Calculate the mass of aluminium deposited in grams when a current of 5.0 A is passed through molten aluminium oxide for 965 seconds. (Faraday constant = 96500 C/mol, Al = 27)
questions.p: Use Faraday formula m = (I × t × M) / (z × F). Put current = 5, time = 965, molar mass = 27, valency z = 3, Faraday = 96500. Multiply and divide well, you go get 0.45 g.

questions.q: Which property makes aluminium extremely resistant to atmospheric corrosion despite being a very reactive metal?
o: It is alloyed naturally with unreactive trace elements
It has a very high density that prevents oxygen penetration
It dissolves readily in rainwater to form a protective solution
It forms a stable, protective oxide film on its surface
questions.e: Aluminium reacts quickly with oxygen in the air to form a thin, tough, and impermeable layer of aluminium oxide that passivates the metal and prevents further oxidation.
questions.p: Aluminium dey form thin layer of strong oxide coat for body when air touch am. Dis coat dey protect the metal make air no rust am again.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of the branched alkane with the molecular formula C₆H₁₄ that possesses a continuous chain of four carbon atoms and two methyl groups at carbon-2 and carbon-3?
questions.e: The longest carbon chain has four carbon atoms (butane). There are two methyl groups attached to carbon-2 and carbon-3, giving 2,3-dimethylbutane.
questions.p: Di longest carbon chain na four carbon, wey bi butane. Two methyl group dey for carbon-2 and carbon-3, so di name na 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.q: What volume of carbon(IV) oxide at Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) is produced when 0.1 mol of propane is completely burned in excess oxygen?
questions.e: One mole of propane burns to give 3 moles of CO₂. Therefore, 0.1 mol of propane yields 0.3 mol of CO₂, which occupies 0.3 × 22.4 dm³ = 6.72 dm³ at STP.
questions.p: One mole of propane dey give 3 moles of CO₂. So, 0.1 mol go give 0.3 mol of CO₂, and 0.3 times 22.4 dm³ na 6.72 dm³ at STP.

questions.q: Which of the following reagents is specifically used to distinguish between a terminal alkyne like pent-1-yne and a non-terminal alkyne like pent-2-yne?
questions.e: Terminal alkynes contain an acidic hydrogen atom on the triple-bonded carbon, which reacts with ammoniacal silver nitrate to form a white precipitate. Non-terminal alkynes do not react.
questions.p: Terminal alkyne get acidic hydrogen wey dey react with ammoniacal silver nitrate to form white precipitate, but non-terminal alkyne no dey react.

questions.q: Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions rather than addition reactions primarily because it possesses:
o: two faces that repel incoming reagents
a stable delocalized π electron cloud
questions.e: The delocalized π electron system of benzene gives it special thermodynamic stability. Addition reactions would destroy this aromatic stability, whereas substitution preserves it.
questions.p: Di delocalized π electron system for benzene dey give am strong stability. If addition happen, di stability go scatter, but substitution go maintain am.

questions.q: What is the principal product formed when 2-bromobutane is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide?
questions.e: Heating a haloalkane with alcoholic KOH results in a dehydrohalogenation (elimination) reaction. According to Zaitsev's rule, the major product is the more substituted alkene, which is but-2-ene.
questions.p: If you heat haloalkane with alcoholic KOH, elimination reaction happen. Following Zaitsev rule, di major product na di more substituted alkene, wey bi but-2-ene.

questions.q: Which of the following organic compounds has the highest boiling point?
questions.e: Boiling points of alkanes increase with molecular mass due to stronger van der Waals forces. Pentane has five carbons, which is more than butane, propane, or 2-methylpropane.
questions.p: Boiling point of alkanes dey increase as mass dey increase because of strong van der Waals forces. Pentane get five carbons, so e heavy pass di rest.

questions.q: Cracking of heavy petroleum fractions in the petroleum industry is primarily carried out to produce:
o: lighter, more valuable petrol fractions and alkenes
questions.e: Cracking breaks down large, less useful hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, high-demand petrol fractions and important alkene feedstocks.
questions.p: Cracking dey break down heavy hydrocarbon into smaller, high-demand petrol and alkenes wey industries need.

questions.q: When ethene gas is bubbled through cold, dilute, acidified potassium permanganate solution, the color of the solution changes from:
questions.e: Cold dilute KMnO₄ oxidizes ethene to ethane-1,2-diol. During this redox reaction, the purple permanganate ion is reduced to colorless Mn₂+ ions.
questions.p: Cold dilute KMnO₄ dey oxidize ethene to ethane-1,2-diol, and as e dey happen, di purple colour of permanganate dey turn colorless.

questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of carbon in ethyne (C₂H₂)? (Atomic weights: C = 12, H = 1)
questions.e: Molar mass of C₂H₂ is (2 × 12) + (2 × 1) = 26 g/mol. Mass of carbon is 24 g/mol, so percentage is (24 / 26) × 100 = 92.3%.
questions.p: Molar mass of C₂H₂ na 26 g/mol, and mass of carbon inside na 24 g/mol. Percentage of carbon na (24 divide by 26) times 100, wey give 92.3 percent.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is classified as a tertiary alcohol?
questions.e: A tertiary alcohol has the hydroxyl (-OH) group attached to a carbon atom that is bonded to three other carbon atoms. In 2-methylbutan-2-ol, the central carbon carrying the -OH group is bonded to a methyl group, an ethyl group, and another methyl group, making it tertiary.
questions.p: Tertiary alcohol na when the carbon wey carry -OH group join three other carbon atoms. Na only 2-methylbutan-2-ol fit this description well well.

questions.q: When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid at a temperature of 170° C, the major organic product formed is
questions.e: Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid acts as a dehydrating agent. At 170° C, it promotes the intramolecular dehydration of ethanol to yield ethene gas.
questions.p: Concentrated H₂SO₄ na dehydrating agent. When you heat am with ethanol for 170° C, e dey remove water comot make ethene gas.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name for the organic compound with the formula CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)COOH?
questions.e: The longest carbon chain containing the carboxyl group has four carbons, making it a butane derivative (butanoic acid). Numbering starts from the carboxyl carbon as C-1, placing a methyl group at carbon 2, hence 2-methylbutanoic acid.
questions.p: The longest carbon chain wey get the acid group get four carbons, so na butanoic acid. If you start to count from the acid carbon, the methyl branch dey carbon number 2.

questions.q: An organic compound 'X' reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate solution to effervesce, producing a colourless gas that turns lime water milky. Compound 'X' most likely contains which functional group?
questions.e: Carboxylic acids react with weak bases like sodium hydrogen carbonate to release carbon dioxide gas, which turns lime water milky. This reaction is a characteristic chemical test for the carboxyl group (-COOH).
questions.p: Na carboxylic acid dey react with sodium hydrogen carbonate to produce carbon dioxide gas wey dey turn lime water milky. The functional group na carboxyl group.

questions.q: During the saponification of palm oil for soap making in a local cottage industry, which substance is added to hydrolyze the fat or oil?
questions.e: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils using a strong alkali like sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide to yield soap and glycerol.
questions.p: Saponification mean say you dey boil oil or fat with strong alkali like sodium hydroxide to make soap and glycerol.

questions.q: What is the primary role of adding sodium chloride (common salt) at the end of the soap-making process?
o: To bleach the coloured soap mixture
To precipitate the soap from solution
To act as a catalyst for esterification
questions.e: Adding sodium chloride causes salting-out, which decreases the solubility of soap in the aqueous medium and causes it to precipitate out as a solid crust on top.
questions.p: We dey add common salt so that the soap go salad out and float for top because e go reduce how soap take dissolve inside water.

questions.q: Consider the ester propyl ethanoate. What are the respective alcohol and carboxylic acid precursors used in its preparation?
questions.e: An ester's name comes from its alcohol part (alkyl group) and acid part (alkanoate). 'Propyl' comes from propan-1-ol, and 'ethanoate' comes from ethanoic acid.
questions.p: Name of ester dey show where e come from. 'Propyl' na from propan-1-ol, and 'ethanoate' na from ethanoic acid.

questions.q: What mass of sodium hydroxide, NaOH, is required to completely saponify exactly 1.0 mole of a pure fat represented as glyceryl tristearate? [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23]
questions.e: One mole of a triglyceride (fat) contains three ester linkages and requires 3 moles of NaOH for complete alkaline hydrolysis. Mass of 3 moles of NaOH = 3 x (23 + 16 + 1) = 3 x 40 = 120 g.
questions.p: One mole of fat get three ester groups, so e need 3 moles of NaOH to break am finish. Since molar mass of NaOH na 40 g/mol, 3 times 40 give you 120 g.

questions.q: A pure liquid organic compound 'Y' has a sweet fruity smell, is insoluble in water, and does not react with acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution. Compound 'Y' is most likely an
questions.e: Esters are characterized by fruity smells, insolubility in water, and resistance to oxidation by mild oxidizing agents like acidified KMnO₄ because they lack active functional groups like -OH or -CHO.
questions.p: Any compound wey get fruity smell, no soluble for water, and oxidation no touch am like ester. Ester no get active -OH or -COOH group again.

questions.q: During the fractional distillation of Nigerian light crude oil in Port Harcourt, which of the following fractions is collected at the highest temperature range?
questions.e: Bitumen has the highest boiling point range among the fractions listed and is therefore collected at the bottom of the fractionating column at the highest temperature.
questions.p: Na bitumen get the highest boiling point for inside crude oil, so naim dey settle down for bottom where temperature high pass.

questions.q: What is the primary chemical process involved in converting heavy crude oil fractions into lighter, more valuable petrol in Nigerian refineries?
questions.e: Cracking breaks down large, high-boiling hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful alkenes and alkanes suited for petrol.
questions.p: Na cracking dem dey use break big big molecules into small small ones wey motor fit use as petrol.

questions.q: Which of the following polymers is correctly classified as a condensation polymer formed from two different monomers?
questions.e: Nylon-6,6 is a polyamide formed by the condensation polymerization of a hexanediamine and a adipic acid, eliminating water.
questions.p: Na nylon-6,6 be condensation polymer because e dey combine two different monomer and water dey commot for body.

questions.q: A polymer sample is found to be made strictly by the addition reaction of gaseous ethene molecules under high pressure. What is the structural repeat unit of this polymer?
questions.e: Ethene (C₂H₄) undergoes addition polymerization by opening its double bond to form the repeat unit -CH₂-CH₂- in polyethene.
questions.p: Ethene wey double bond open up dey form polyethene, and the repeat unit na -CH₂-CH₂-.

questions.q: In the catalytic reforming unit of a Kaduna refinery, straight-chain alkanes are converted into aromatic hydrocarbons to improve fuel quality. Which catalyst is commonly employed for this purpose?
questions.e: Platinum supported on alumina is the standard catalyst used in reforming processes to convert alkanes into branched alkanes and aromatics.
questions.p: Na platinum on alumina dem dey use as catalyst for reforming plant make petrol quality beta well well.

questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon in the repeat unit of polypropene, (C₃H₆)n. [C = 12, H = 1]
questions.e: The molar mass of the repeat unit C₃H₆ is (3 x 12) + (6 x 1) = 42 g/mol. Mass percentage of carbon = (36 / 42) x 100% = 85.7%.
questions.p: Total mass of C₃H₆ na 42. Mass of carbon na 36, so percentage na (36 / 42) times 100 which give 85.7 percent.

questions.q: Which of the following substances is used as a vulcanizing agent to improve the elasticity and strength of natural rubber in Nigerian tyre industries?
questions.e: Sulphur is added during vulcanization to form cross-links between rubber polymer chains, making it stronger and more elastic.
questions.p: Na sulphur dem dey add to rubber make e strong and bounce well well when dem dey make tyre.

questions.q: A sample of crude oil contains various fractions. If the fraction containing pentane to octane is processed, how many carbon atoms are present per molecule in this petrol fraction?
questions.e: Petrol (gasoline) typically consists of hydrocarbons containing between 5 and 8 carbon atoms per molecule (pentane to octane).
questions.p: Petrol fraction dey contain hydrocarbon wey get carbon atoms from 5 to 8 inside each molecule.

questions.q: Which of the following statements concerning synthetic polymers and natural polymers is correct?
o: Starch is a polyamide formed by condensation.
Cellulose is a natural polymer made of glucose units.
Proteins are synthetic addition polymers of amino acids.
Terylene is a natural biopolymer found in plants.
questions.e: Cellulose is a naturally occurring polysaccharide composed of repeating beta-glucose units linked together.
questions.p: Cellulose na natural polymer wey glucose units join body together inside plant.

questions.q: During the cracking of a heavy alkane with molecular formula C₁₄H₃₀, one molecule of propene (C₃H₆) is produced alongside an alkane X. What is the molecular formula of alkane X?
questions.e: By conservation of atoms, C₁₄H₃₀ minus C₃H₆ leaves C₁₁H₂₄. An alkane with 11 carbons has the general formula CnH2n+2, giving C₁₁H₂₄.
questions.p: If you subtract C₃H₆ from C₁₄H₃₀, wetin remain na C₁₁H₂₄ because alkane must follow CnH2n+2 formula.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a chemical reaction and a nuclear reaction?
o: Nuclear reactions occur at room temperature without any catalyst, while chemical reactions require high pressure.
Nuclear reactions involve valence electrons, while chemical reactions involve protons and neutrons.
Nuclear reactions involve changes in the nucleus and release enormous amounts of energy, while chemical reactions involve electrons and smaller energy changes.
Chemical reactions change one element into another, whereas nuclear reactions do not.
questions.e: Chemical reactions only involve the outer valence electrons and have relatively small energy changes. Nuclear reactions involve the core particles (protons and neutrons) inside the nucleus and release millions of times more energy.
questions.p: Chemical reaction dey involve ordinary electron for outside, but nuclear reaction dey touch the center nucleus where proton and neutron dey, and e dey produce massive energy.

questions.q: During the radioactive decay of Uranium-238 to Thorium-234, which type of particle is emitted?
questions.e: Uranium-238 has a mass number of 238 and atomic number 92. When it decays to Thorium-234 (mass number 234, atomic number 90), the mass decreases by 4 and atomic number decreases by 2, which is characteristic of alpha emission.
questions.p: Uranium-238 wey turn to Thorium-234 don lose four mass number and two atomic number, na clear sign say na alpha particle dem release.

questions.q: If a radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5 days, what fraction of the original sample will remain unreacted after 20 days?
questions.e: The number of half-lives n = total time / half-life = 20 / 5 = 4. The remaining fraction is (1/2)ⁿ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16.
questions.p: Number of half-life na 20 divide by 5, wey give us 4. If you calculate (1/2) power 4, na 1 over 16 go remain.

questions.q: Which of the following radioactive emissions has the highest ionizing power and the lowest penetrating power?
questions.e: Alpha particles are heavy and doubly charged, making them extremely good at stripping electrons from atoms (high ionizing power) but easily stopped by a sheet of paper (low penetrating power).
questions.p: Alpha particle heavy and get double positive charge, so e dey ionize things quick quick, but ordinary paper fit block am because e no fit penetrate far.

questions.q: Balance the following nuclear equation representing beta decay: Carbon-14 goes to Nitrogen-14 plus X. What is particle X?
questions.e: In beta-minus decay, a neutron inside the nucleus changes into a proton and an electron (beta particle). The electron is ejected, so X is an electron (0/-1 e).
questions.p: For beta decay, neutron dey turn to proton and electron inside nucleus. Na that ejected electron wey be beta particle dey come out as X.

questions.q: An isotope of iodine has a half-life of 8 days. If 64 grams of this isotope is stored, how many grams will remain after 24 days?
questions.e: Number of half-lives = 24 / 8 = 3. Remaining mass = Initial mass / (2³) = 64 / 8 = 8 grams.
questions.p: Time wey pass na 3 half-life (24 divide by 8). Just divide 64 grams by 2 three times, you go get 8 grams.

questions.q: Which device is commonly used in laboratories to detect and measure ionizing radiation by producing an electrical pulse for each particle or ray detected?
questions.e: The Geiger-Muller counter contains a gas-filled tube that ionizes when radiation enters, creating an electrical click or pulse that is easily measured.
questions.p: Na Geiger-Muller counter dem dey use for lab to detect radiation because anytime radiation enter the tube, e go produce sharp sound or electrical pulse.

questions.q: What is the primary application of Cobalt-60 in medicine and industry?
o: As a tracer to monitor underground water flow in the Niger Delta
As fuel rods in nuclear power plants
As a radiation source for radiotherapy in cancer treatment and sterilization
As a catalyst for cracking petroleum in refineries
questions.e: Cobalt-60 emits powerful gamma rays used extensively in treating cancer tumors and sterilizing medical equipment.
questions.p: Dem dey use Cobalt-60 produce gamma rays wey dey help kill cancer cells for hospital and also use am sterilize instrument.

questions.q: Calculate the decay constant (in day⁻¹) for a radioactive nuclide whose half-life is 6.93 days. (Use ln(2) = 0.693)
questions.e: The decay constant lambda = 0.693 / half-life = 0.693 / 6.93 = 0.1 day⁻¹.
questions.p: Formula for decay constant na 0.693 divide by half-life. If you divide 0.693 by 6.93, answer na 0.1.

questions.q: Which nuclear process is responsible for the massive energy output and generation of light from the sun and other stars?
questions.e: Nuclear fusion involves combining light nuclei (like hydrogen isotopes) under extreme temperature and pressure to form heavier nuclei, releasing immense amounts of energy.
questions.p: Na nuclear fusion, where small hydrogen atoms join together to form helium under hot sun condition, dey produce all that massive energy for sun.

questions.q: Hauwa mixes palm oil with water in a container and notices the oil floats as a separate layer above the water, with no visible mixing at the boundary. Which laboratory technique is most suitable for separating the palm oil from the water?
questions.e: Palm oil and water are immiscible liquids that form two distinct layers because of different densities. A separating funnel allows the denser liquid (water) to be run off from the bottom tap, leaving the oil behind. Filtration and sublimation are for solid-liquid or solid-solid mixtures, not immiscible liquids.
questions.p: Palm oil and water no dey mix, dem go dey settle as two layers because dem get different density. Separating funnel go help you drain the water wey dey below first, leave the oil. Filtration and sublimation no fit work here because na liquid mixture.

questions.q: A student has a solid mixture of iodine crystals and common salt (sodium chloride). Iodine changes directly from solid to vapour on gentle heating and then solidifies again on a cold surface, while sodium chloride does not. Which technique is most appropriate for separating the iodine from the mixture?
questions.e: Sublimation is used when one component of a solid mixture turns directly into vapour on heating without melting, while the other does not. Iodine sublimes easily, so heating the mixture lets iodine vapour escape and condense on a cold surface, leaving the salt behind. Distillation and decantation are for liquid mixtures, and crystallization needs dissolving in a solvent first.
questions.p: Sublimation na the method wey dem dey use when one part of solid mixture fit turn to gas straight without melting, but the other one no fit. Iodine dey sublime easily, so if you heat the mixture, iodine go turn vapour and later condense for cold surface, salt go remain. Distillation and decantation na for liquid mixtures, crystallization need solvent first.

questions.q: A sample of impure common salt contaminated with sand weighs 20.0 g. The sample is dissolved in water, filtered to remove the insoluble sand, and the filtrate is evaporated to dryness, yielding 15.0 g of pure sodium chloride crystals. What is the percentage purity of the original salt sample?
questions.e: Percentage purity equals the mass of pure substance recovered divided by the mass of the original impure sample, multiplied by 100. Here, (15.0 g / 20.0 g) x 100 = 75%. This shows that only 75% of the original 20.0 g sample was actually sodium chloride, the rest being sand.
questions.p: Percentage purity na the mass of the pure substance wey you recover divide by the mass of the original impure sample, multiply by 100. So (15.0 g / 20.0 g) x 100 = 75%. Na so we know say na 75% of the 20.0 g be real sodium chloride, the remaining na sand.

questions.q: A student stirs a mixture of fine sand and common salt in water until the salt dissolves completely, then filters the mixture. The sand is retained on the filter paper as residue, while the filtrate contains dissolved salt in water. Which process should the student carry out next to recover solid salt from the filtrate?
questions.e: The filtrate is a solution of salt dissolved in water, so heating it until all the water evaporates leaves behind the solid salt crystals. Decantation only separates liquids from settled solids without dissolving, sublimation is for substances that vaporise directly from solid, and chromatography separates components based on different movement rates on paper, not for recovering a dissolved solid.
questions.p: The filtrate na solution wey salt dissolve inside water, so if you heat am make water evaporate finish, the solid salt go remain as crystals. Decantation na just to pour out liquid from settled solid, sublimation na for substance wey dey change from solid to gas direct, and chromatography na for separate components wey dey move different speed, e no fit recover dissolved solid.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases?
o: Collisions between gas molecules and with the walls of the container are perfectly elastic
The actual volume occupied by the gas molecules is negligible compared to the volume of the container

questions.q: A sample of gas occupies 450 cm³ at a temperature of 17°C and a pressure of 760 mmHg. What volume will the same sample of gas occupy at 47°C and 950 mmHg?
questions.e: Using the combined gas law, V₂ = V₁ x (P₁/P₂) x (T₂/T₁). First convert temperatures to Kelvin: T₁ = 290 K, T₂ = 320 K. So V₂ = 450 x (760/950) x (320/290) = 450 x 0.8 x 1.1034 = 397 cm3 (to 3 s.f.).
questions.p: We go use combined gas law: V₂ = V₁ x (P₁/P₂) x (T₂/T₁). First change the temperature to Kelvin: 290K and 320K. Calculate am, you go see say V₂ na 397 cm3.

questions.q: Under the same temperature and pressure, gas Q diffuses through a small hole in 20 seconds while gas P, with the same volume, takes 40 seconds to diffuse through the same hole. If the molar mass of gas Q is 16 g/mol, calculate the molar mass of gas P.
questions.e: Rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to time taken, so rateP/rateQ = tQ/tP = 20/40 = 0.5. By Graham's law, rateP/rateQ = √(MQ/MP), so 0.5 = √(16/MP). Squaring gives 0.25 = 16/MP, so MP = 16/0.25 = 64 g/mol.
questions.p: Rate of diffusion dey inverse to the time wey e take, so rateP/rateQ = 20/40 = 0.5. Graham law talk say rateP/rateQ = √(MQ/MP). If you square 0.5 you go get 0.25 = 16/MP, so MP = 64 g/mol.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 4.0 dm3 at a temperature of 350 K and a pressure of 2.0 atm. The gas is then compressed so that it occupies 1.0 dm3 at a pressure of 5.0 atm. What is the final temperature of the gas?
questions.e: Using the combined gas law, P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂, so T₂ = T₁ x (P₂V₂)/(P₁V₁). Substituting values: T₂ = 350 x (5 x 1)/(2 x 4) = 350 x 5/8 = 218.75 K, which rounds to about 219 K.
questions.p: We go use combined gas law: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂, so T₂ = T₁ x (P₂V₂)/(P₁V₁). Put the numbers: T₂ = 350 x (5x1)/(2x4) = 350 x 5/8 = 218.75 K, wey be like 219 K.

questions.q: An atom of element Q has a mass number of 31 and contains 16 neutrons. How many electrons are present in a neutral atom of Q?
questions.e: Number of protons = mass number - neutrons = 31 - 16 = 15. In a neutral atom, electrons equal protons, so there are 15 electrons.
questions.p: Protons = mass number minus neutrons = 31 - 16 = 15. Since the atom no get charge, electrons go equal protons, na 15.

questions.q: Chlorine has atomic number 17. Which of the following electron configurations correctly represents a chlorine atom in its ground state?
questions.e: Chlorine has 17 electrons. Filling in order: 1s2(2) + 2s2(2) + 2p6(6) + 3s2(2) + 3p5(5) = 17 electrons, matching the aufbau order with no d-electrons needed yet.
questions.p: Chlorine get 17 electrons. If you fill am well-well: 1s2 + 2s2 + 2p6 + 3s2 + 3p5 go give you 2+2+6+2+5 = 17. Na dis one dey correct, no need for 3d yet.

questions.q: An element M has two naturally occurring isotopes: one with mass number 69 and the other with mass number 71, present in the ratio 3:2 respectively. Calculate the relative atomic mass of M to one decimal place.
questions.e: Relative atomic mass = (69x3 + 71x2)/(3+2) = (207+142)/5 = 349/5 = 69.8. This weighted average accounts for the different abundances of each isotope.
questions.p: You go multiply each mass number by im ratio, add dem together, then divide by total ratio: (69x3 + 71x2)/5 = 349/5 = 69.8. Na dis weighted average be the relative atomic mass.

questions.q: A calcium atom (atomic number 20) has the ground-state electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2. How many electrons occupy the principal shell with n = 3?
questions.e: The n=3 shell contains the 3s and 3p subshells only, since 3d is empty in calcium's ground state (the 4s fills first). So electrons in n=3 are 3s2 + 3p6 = 2+6 = 8.
questions.p: Na only 3s and 3p dey inside n=3 shell for calcium, 3d still empty because 4s fill first. So electrons wey dey n=3 na 3s2 + 3p6 = 2+6 = 8.

questions.q: As you move down Group 1 of the periodic table from lithium to caesium, what happens to the atomic radius of the elements?
o: It remains the same for all elements
questions.e: Going down a group, more electron shells are added to each successive element. More shells mean the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, so atomic radius increases steadily from lithium to caesium.
questions.p: As you dey go down Group 1 from lithium reach caesium, each element dey add one more shell of electron. More shell mean say the outer electron dey far from nucleus, so the atomic size dey increase steadily.

questions.q: An element X has atomic number 19. Using the electronic configuration of X, determine its correct position (period and group) in the periodic table.
questions.e: Atomic number 19 gives the configuration 2,8,8,1. The number of shells (4) gives the period, and the 1 electron in the outermost shell gives the group number, so X is in Period 4, Group 1.
questions.p: Atomic number 19 na 2,8,8,1. Di shells wey dey (4) na di period, and di 1 electron wey dey di last shell na di group, so X dey Period 4, Group 1.

questions.q: The ions Na+, Mg₂+, Al₃+ and F- all have exactly 10 electrons, the same arrangement as neon. Which of these ions has the smallest ionic radius?
questions.e: All four ions have the same number of electrons (10), but their nuclear charges differ: F- has 9 protons, Na+ has 11, Mg₂+ has 12, and Al₃+ has 13. The higher the nuclear charge for the same number of electrons, the stronger the pull on the electron cloud, so Al₃+ has the smallest radius.
questions.p: All di ions get 10 electrons, but di protons (nuclear charge) dey different: F- (9), Na+ (11), Mg₂+ (12), Al₃+ (13). Di one wey get di most protons go pull im electrons close pass, so Al₃+ get di smallest size.

questions.q: An element Z is located in Group 15 of the periodic table. How many valence (outermost shell) electrons does Z have?
questions.e: For main group elements, the group number (using the old or simplified numbering 1 to 18 minus 10 for groups 13-18) tells you the number of valence electrons. Group 15 elements, like nitrogen and phosphorus, have 5 electrons in their outermost shell.
questions.p: For main group elements, di group number dey show how many electron dey di outer shell. Group 15 elements like nitrogen and phosphorus get 5 electrons for dia last shell.

questions.q: Which type of chemical bond is formed when two non-metal atoms share a pair of electrons, with each atom contributing one electron to the shared pair?
questions.e: A covalent bond forms when two non-metal atoms each contribute one electron to a shared pair, so the pair is mutually owned. Ionic bonds involve electron transfer, metallic bonds involve a sea of delocalised electrons, and hydrogen bonds are weak intermolecular attractions, not true chemical bonds between atoms within a molecule.
questions.p: Covalent bond na when two non-metal atoms share electron pair, each one give one electron. Ionic bond na when electron dey transfer, metallic bond na sea of free electrons, hydrogen bond na weak force between molecules, no be real bond inside one molecule.

questions.q: The electronegativity values of hydrogen and chlorine are 2.1 and 3.0 respectively. Given that a difference greater than 1.7 usually indicates an ionic bond while a smaller difference indicates a covalent bond, what type of bond exists in hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
questions.e: The electronegativity difference is 3.0 minus 2.1, which equals 0.9. Since 0.9 is less than 1.7, the bond is covalent, but because the difference is not zero, the electron pair is unequally shared, making it a polar covalent bond.
questions.p: The difference na 3.0 minus 2.1 wey give 0.9. Since 0.9 dey less pass 1.7, e no be ionic bond, na covalent. But because the difference no be zero, electron no dey share equally, so na polar covalent bond.

questions.q: Xenon tetrafluoride (XeF₄) has a central xenon atom bonded to four fluorine atoms. Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Using the formula: total electron pairs around the central atom = (valence electrons of central atom + number of bonded atoms) / 2, and subtracting the number of bonding pairs, how many lone pairs of electrons are on the central xenon atom?
questions.e: Total electron pairs around Xe = (8 + 4) / 2 = 6. Since 4 of these pairs are used in bonding to the 4 fluorine atoms, the remaining lone pairs = 6 - 4 = 2. These 2 lone pairs give XeF₄ its square planar shape.
questions.p: Total electron pairs around Xe na (8 + 4) / 2 = 6. Since 4 out of the 6 dey used for bonding to the 4 fluorine atoms, the remaining lone pairs na 6 - 4 = 2. Na these 2 lone pairs make XeF₄ take square planar shape.

questions.q: During the formation of the ammonium ion (NH₄+), the nitrogen atom in ammonia uses its lone pair of electrons to bond with an incoming hydrogen ion (H+), which has no electron of its own to contribute. What type of bond is formed between the nitrogen atom and this particular hydrogen atom?
questions.e: A coordinate (dative) covalent bond forms when only one atom supplies both electrons of the shared pair. Here, nitrogen alone donates its lone pair to the empty orbital of H+, so this specific N-H bond is dative, even though it becomes identical to the other N-H bonds afterward.
questions.p: Coordinate (dative) covalent bond na when one atom alone give both electrons wey dem go share. Here, nitrogen alone donate im lone pair give the empty orbital of H+, so dis particular N-H bond na dative bond, even though e go later be like the other N-H bonds.

questions.q: Calculate the number of moles of magnesium atoms present in 6.0 g of magnesium metal. [Mg = 24]

questions.p: Moles = mass divide molar mass = 6.0/24 = 0.25 mol. Na straight formula work be dis.

questions.q: 100 cm3 of 0.4 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid solution is mixed with 300 cm3 of distilled water. Assuming the volumes are additive, what is the concentration of the resulting solution?
questions.e: Moles of HCl = 0.4 mol/dm3 x 0.1 dm3 = 0.04 mol. Total volume after mixing = 0.1 + 0.3 = 0.4 dm3. New concentration = 0.04/0.4 = 0.1 mol/dm3.
questions.p: Moles of HCl wey dey inside = 0.4 x 0.1 = 0.04 mol. Total volume don become 0.4 dm3. So new concentration = 0.04/0.4 = 0.1 mol/dm3.

questions.q: Propane gas burns completely in oxygen according to the equation: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) -> 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(g). If 0.2 mol of propane is completely burnt, how many moles of oxygen gas are required?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mol C₃H₈ reacts with 5 mol O₂. So 0.2 mol C₃H₈ needs 0.2 x 5 = 1.0 mol O₂.
questions.p: For the equation, 1 mol propane dey react with 5 mol O₂. So 0.2 mol propane go need 0.2 x 5 = 1.0 mol O₂.

questions.q: Aluminium reacts with chlorine gas according to: 2Al(s) + 3Cl₂(g) -> 2AlCl₃(s). A chemist, Mr. Danjuma, mixes 5.4 g of aluminium with 7.1 g of chlorine gas in a sealed container and allows the reaction to go to completion. What mass of aluminium chloride, AlCl₃, is formed? [Al = 27, Cl = 35.5]
questions.e: Moles Al = 5.4/27 = 0.2 mol, moles Cl₂ = 7.1/71 = 0.1 mol. Required ratio Cl₂:Al is 3:2 = 1.5, but available ratio is 0.1/0.2 = 0.5, so Cl₂ is the limiting reagent. From 3 mol Cl₂ giving 2 mol AlCl₃, 0.1 mol Cl₂ gives (2/3) x 0.1 = 0.0667 mol AlCl₃, mass = 0.0667 x 133.5 = 8.9 g.
questions.p: Moles Al = 5.4/27 = 0.2 mol, moles Cl₂ = 7.1/71 = 0.1 mol. The ratio wey dem need na 3:2 = 1.5, but wetin dem get na 0.5, so Cl₂ na di limiting reagent. 0.1 mol Cl₂ go produce (2/3) x 0.1 = 0.0667 mol AlCl₃, wey be 8.9 g.

questions.q: What is the pH of a 0.01 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid, assuming complete dissociation in water?
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid, so it dissociates completely: [H+] = 0.01 = 1 x 10⁻² mol/dm3. pH = -log10(1 x 10⁻²) = 2.
questions.p: HCl na strong acid so e go dissociate well-well: [H+] = 0.01 = 1 x 10⁻² mol/dm3. pH = -log10(1 x 10⁻²) = 2.

questions.q: Potassium trioxocarbonate(IV), K₂CO₃, is formed from the reaction of a strong base (KOH) and a weak acid (H₂CO₃). What is the expected nature of an aqueous solution of this salt?
questions.e: When a salt comes from a strong base and a weak acid, the anion (CO₃²⁻) hydrolyses in water to produce OH- ions, making the solution basic. This is called anionic hydrolysis.

questions.q: A school laboratory technician wants to neutralize 50.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid completely using solid sodium hydroxide, NaOH. Calculate the minimum mass of NaOH required. (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.e: Moles of HCl = 0.0500 dm3 x 0.20 mol/dm3 = 0.01 mol. Since HCl and NaOH react 1:1, moles of NaOH needed = 0.01 mol. Mass = 0.01 x 40 = 0.40 g.
questions.p: Moles of HCl = 0.0500 dm3 x 0.20 mol/dm3 = 0.01 mol. Since HCl and NaOH dey react 1:1, moles of NaOH wey dem need = 0.01 mol. Mass = 0.01 x 40 = 0.40 g.

questions.q: Ammonium trioxonitrate(V), NH₄NO₃, contains two nitrogen atoms in different chemical environments: one in the NH₄+ ion (oxidation number -3) and one in the NO₃- ion (oxidation number +5). What is the AVERAGE oxidation number of nitrogen in the whole compound?

questions.q: According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis, the mass of a substance liberated or deposited at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the:

questions.q: Calculate the mass of aluminium deposited at the cathode when a steady current of 10.0 A is passed through molten aluminium oxide for 2 hours. [Al = 27, F = 96500 C/mol]
questions.e: Charge Q = It = 10 x 7200 = 72000 C. Moles of electrons = 72000/96500 = 0.746 mol. Since Al₃+ + 3e- gives Al, moles of Al = 0.746/3 = 0.249 mol, so mass = 0.249 x 27 = 6.72 g.

questions.q: Two electrolytic cells, one containing molten aluminium chloride and the other containing aqueous copper(II) sulphate, are connected in series using inert electrodes. If 0.09 mole of aluminium is deposited in the first cell, calculate the mass of copper deposited in the second cell during the same period. [Cu = 64]
questions.e: Same charge passes through both cells. Al₃+ + 3e- -> Al, so 0.09 mol Al needs 0.09 x 3 = 0.27 mol electrons. Cu₂+ + 2e- -> Cu, so moles of Cu = 0.27/2 = 0.135 mol, mass = 0.135 x 64 = 8.64 g.
questions.p: Na the same charge dey pass through both cell. Al₃+ + 3e- -> Al, so 0.09 mol Al go need 0.27 mol electron. Cu₂+ + 2e- -> Cu, so mol of Cu = 0.27/2 = 0.135 mol, mass = 0.135 x 64 = 8.64 g.

questions.q: The Faraday constant (F) is the quantity of electric charge carried by one mole of electrons. If the charge on a single electron is 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ C and the Avogadro number is 6.0 x 10²³ per mole, calculate the value of the Faraday constant.
questions.e: Faraday constant F = Avogadro number x charge on one electron = 6.0 x 10²³ x 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.6 x 10⁴ C/mol = 96000 C/mol, which is close to the standard value of 96500 C/mol.
questions.p: Faraday constant F = Avogadro number x charge for one electron = 6.0 x 10²³ x 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.6 x 10⁴ C/mol = 96000 C/mol, wey close to the standard 96500 C/mol.

questions.q: During a chemical reaction, bonds in the reactants are broken (which requires energy) and new bonds form in the products (which releases energy). If the energy released when new bonds form is greater than the energy needed to break the old bonds, the reaction is classified as:
questions.e: When bond-forming releases more energy than bond-breaking absorbs, the overall reaction gives out energy to the surroundings. This makes the reaction exothermic, with a negative enthalpy change (delta H).
questions.p: If the energy wey dem release when new bond form pass the one wey dem use break old bond, na extra energy dey comot go environment. That one na exothermic reaction, delta H go negative.

questions.q: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) -> 2NH₃(g), the bond energies are: N≡N = 945 kJ/mol, H-H = 436 kJ/mol, and N-H = 391 kJ/mol. Using bond energy data, calculate the enthalpy change of the reaction.
questions.e: Energy to break bonds (reactants) = 945 + 3(436) = 2253 kJ/mol. Energy released forming bonds (products, 6 N-H bonds) = 6(391) = 2346 kJ/mol. Enthalpy change = bonds broken minus bonds formed = 2253 - 2346 = -93 kJ/mol, showing the reaction is exothermic.
questions.p: Energy wey go break the bond for reactant side = 945 + 3(436) = 2253 kJ/mol. Energy wey go release when the 6 N-H bond form = 6(391) = 2346 kJ/mol. Delta H = 2253 - 2346 = -93 kJ/mol, na exothermic reaction.
