The temperature fell, meaning the solution absorbed heat from its surroundings, so the process is endothermic (positive delta H).
questions.p: Heat wey the solution chop: q = mcΔT = 100 x 4.2 x 6 = 2520 J. Mole of NH₄Cl wey dem use = 5.35/53.5 = 0.1 mol. Molar enthalpy = 2520/0.1 = 25200 J/mol = +25.2 kJ/mol. Since temperature drop, e mean say the solution dey absorb heat, so na endothermic process, delta H positive.

questions.q: Given the standard enthalpies of formation: C₃H₈(g) = -104 kJ/mol, CO₂(g) = -393 kJ/mol, H₂O(l) = -286 kJ/mol, and O₂(g) = 0 kJ/mol, use Hess's Law to calculate the standard enthalpy change for the complete combustion reaction: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) -> 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l).
questions.e: Delta H = (sum of products' ΔHf) - (sum of reactants' ΔHf) = [3(-393) + 4(-286)] - [(-104) + 0] = (-1179 - 1144) - (-104) = -2323 + 104 = -2219 kJ/mol. This large negative value shows the combustion of propane is strongly exothermic.
questions.p: Delta H = (total ΔHf for products) - (total ΔHf for reactants) = [3(-393) + 4(-286)] - [(-104) + 0] = -2323 + 104 = -2219 kJ/mol. Dis big negative number show say the burning of propane dey release plenty heat, na exothermic reaction well well.

questions.q: Nkechi reacted the same mass of marble (calcium trioxocarbonate(IV)) with excess dilute hydrochloric acid, using the same volume and concentration of acid and the same temperature in each of four separate experiments. Marble left as a few small irregular chunks

questions.q: For a certain reaction, the rate doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature. If the rate of the reaction at 20°C is 0.02 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, what will the rate be at 50°C?
questions.e: The temperature rises by 50 - 20 = 30°C, which is three lots of 10°C. The rate doubles each time, so the overall factor is 2³ = 8. New rate = 0.02 x 8 = 0.16 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.
questions.p: Temperature rise na 30°C, wey be three times of 10°C. Since rate dey double every 10°C, we multiply by 2 three times: 2x2x2 = 8. So new rate be 0.02 x 8 = 0.16 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

questions.q: Excess granulated zinc is added to 50 cm³ of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid in a flask, and the volume of hydrogen gas produced is recorded against time until the reaction stops. Which description best fits the shape of the graph obtained, and the reason for it?

questions.q: Consider the reversible reaction for ammonia synthesis: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) <=> 2NH₃(g), Delta H = -92 kJ/mol, carried out in a sealed, rigid vessel at constant temperature. If extra nitrogen gas is suddenly pumped into the vessel, what happens to the position of equilibrium?

It remains unchanged because nitrogen does not react
It shifts to the right, producing more ammonia
It shifts to the left, producing more hydrogen
questions.e: Adding more N₂ increases the concentration of a reactant. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts in the direction that uses up the extra N₂, which is the forward (right) direction, producing more NH₃.

questions.q: In a 1.0 dm3 sealed container, 1.0 mole of gas A and 1.0 mole of gas B were mixed and allowed to react: A(g) + B(g) <=> C(g) + D(g). At equilibrium, chemical analysis showed that 0.60 mole of C had formed. Calculate the equilibrium constant, Kc, for this reaction.
questions.e: At equilibrium: A = 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4 mol, B = 0.4 mol, C = 0.6 mol, D = 0.6 mol (same volume, so concentration equals mol/dm3). Kc = [C][D]/([A][B]) = (0.6 x 0.6)/(0.4 x 0.4) = 0.36/0.16 = 2.25.
questions.p: At equilibrium, A and B remain 0.4 mol each, C and D become 0.6 mol each (volume na 1 dm3 so mol = concentration). Kc = (0.6 x 0.6) divide by (0.4 x 0.4) = 2.25.

questions.q: The water-gas shift reaction used in industry is represented as: CO(g) + H₂O(g) <=> CO₂(g) + H₂(g), Delta H = -41 kJ/mol. If the operating temperature of the reactor is increased while pressure is kept constant, what happens to the value of the equilibrium constant, Kc?
o: Kc decreases because the forward reaction is exothermic
Kc stays the same since Kc only depends on concentration
Kc increases because the reverse reaction becomes exothermic
Kc increases because more product forms
questions.e: The forward reaction is exothermic (Delta H is negative), so increasing temperature favours the reverse (endothermic) reaction, shifting equilibrium left. This means less product and more reactant at equilibrium, so Kc decreases.
questions.p: Di forward reaction na exothermic, so if you increase temperature, e go favour di reverse reaction wey dey endothermic. Equilibrium go shift go left, so Kc go reduce.

questions.q: Permanent hardness of water, caused mainly by dissolved calcium and magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) salts, can be removed by adding which of the following substances to precipitate the ions as insoluble carbonates?
questions.e: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃) reacts with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions in water to form insoluble CaCO₃ and MgCO₃, which settle out and remove permanent hardness. The other substances either do not react with these ions or would make the water worse.
questions.p: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃) de react wit di Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ wey dey water, e go form CaCO₃ and MgCO₃ wey no dey dissolve, so dem go settle down. Di oda options no fit do dis kain reaction well.

questions.q: The solubility of potassium chloride (KCl) in water at 25°C is 34 g per 100 g of water. What mass of KCl is needed to form a saturated solution with 250 g of water at this same temperature?
questions.e: Solubility is given per 100 g of water, so scale up: 250 g water is 2.5 times 100 g. Multiply 34 g by 2.5 to get 85 g of KCl needed to saturate the solution.
questions.p: Dem talk say 34 g KCl dey dissolve for 100 g water. 250 g water na 2.5 times 100 g, so multiply 34 g by 2.5 to get 85 g.

questions.q: A chemistry teacher in Enugu tested two water samples with the same amount of soap solution. Sample A formed a thick lather almost immediately, while Sample B needed far more soap before any lather appeared and produced a sticky scum on top. Based on this observation, what can be concluded about Sample B?
o: Sample B contains dissolved calcium and/or magnesium salts causing hardness
Sample B is distilled water used for laboratory experiments
Sample B is pure, soft water with no dissolved ions
Sample B contains only dissolved oxygen gas
questions.e: Hard water contains Ca₂+ and/or Mg₂+ ions which react with soap to form an insoluble scum instead of lather. The need for extra soap before lathering, plus the scum formed, are classic signs of hard water caused by these dissolved salts.
questions.p: Hard water get Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ wey de react wit soap make scum instead of lather. Di fact say Sample B need plenty soap before e lather, and e still form scum, show say e get dis kain dissolved salts.

questions.q: Which gas, produced mainly from the burning of fossil fuels in cars and factories, is widely recognized as the chief greenhouse gas responsible for trapping infrared radiation and causing global warming?
questions.e: Carbon(IV) oxide (CO₂) traps heat in the atmosphere, causing the greenhouse effect. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are normal air components that do not trap heat significantly. Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of CO₂, making it the main greenhouse gas of concern.
questions.p: Carbon(IV) oxide (CO₂) na im dey trap heat for atmosphere, na im cause greenhouse effect. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon no dey trap heat like that. Na because people dey burn fossil fuel well-well, dat na why CO₂ dey plenty pass.

questions.q: A sample of 2000 cm³ of polluted air collected near a cement factory in Ewekoro was analysed and found to contain 40 cm³ of carbon(II) oxide gas. What is the percentage by volume of carbon(II) oxide in the air sample?
questions.e: Percentage by volume = (volume of CO / total volume of air) x 100 = (40/2000) x 100 = 2%. This simple ratio shows how small amounts of pollutant can be measured in a large air sample. Always divide the pollutant volume by the total volume before multiplying by 100.
questions.p: Percentage by volume = (volume of CO / total volume of air) x 100 = (40/2000) x 100 = 2%. Na so you go take calculate small pollutant inside big air sample. Just divide the pollutant volume by total volume, den multiply by 100.

questions.q: Industrial activities around Kaduna release two gases that dissolve in rainwater droplets to form dilute acids, leading to acid rain that corrodes metal roofs and damages crops. Which pair of gases is most responsible for this phenomenon?
questions.e: Sulphur(IV) oxide dissolves in water to form sulphurous/sulphuric acid, while nitrogen(IV) oxide forms nitric acid; both lower the pH of rainwater and cause acid rain. Carbon(IV) oxide forms only a weak acid and does not cause the severe corrosive acid rain seen near industries. Methane, nitrogen, ozone and hydrogen do not directly form strong acids with rainwater.
questions.p: Sulphur(IV) oxide and nitrogen(IV) oxide dey mix with water make strong acid wey dey cause acid rain. CO₂ dey form weak acid wey no strong reach to damage roof or crop like dat. Methane, nitrogen, ozone and hydrogen no dey form strong acid with rain water.

questions.q: Chlorine atoms released from the breakdown of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) in the stratosphere destroy ozone molecules through a chain reaction. Which equation correctly represents the first step of this ozone-depletion mechanism?
questions.e: In the accepted mechanism, a chlorine radical attacks ozone, forming chlorine monoxide (ClO) and ordinary oxygen: Cl + O₃ -> ClO + O₂. The ClO then reacts further to regenerate Cl, allowing the chain reaction to continue and destroy many ozone molecules. The other equations either show wrong products or reverse the real reaction, so they are not correct steps.
questions.p: For di real mechanism, chlorine radical dey attack ozone make am turn to chlorine monoxide (ClO) and normal oxygen: Cl + O₃ -> ClO + O₂. Dat ClO go react again make Cl come back, so di chain reaction go continue dey destroy ozone. Di oda equations show wrong product or dem reverse di real reaction, so dem no correct.

questions.q: A student heats zinc granules with dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid in a test tube and collects the gas produced. When a lighted splint is brought near the mouth of the tube, a 'pop' sound is heard. Which gas was produced and confirmed by this test?
questions.e: Hydrogen gas gives a characteristic 'pop' sound when a lighted splint is placed near it, because it burns rapidly in air. Oxygen relights a glowing splint, CO₂ puts out a flame, and chlorine bleaches damp litmus; none of these give a pop sound.
questions.p: Hydrogen gas na the one wey dey give 'pop' sound when you bring fire near am, because e dey burn quick quick for air. Oxygen go relight glowing splint, CO₂ go kill fire, chlorine go bleach litmus paper; na only hydrogen dey pop.

questions.q: In the industrial manufacture of ammonia by the Haber process, nitrogen gas and hydrogen gas are combined at about 450°C and 200 atmospheres in the presence of a catalyst to speed up the reaction. Which substance is used as this catalyst?
questions.e: In the Haber process, finely divided iron (often with small amounts of promoters like K₂O or Al₂O₃) is used as the catalyst to speed up the reaction between N₂ and H₂ to form NH₃. Platinum gauze is used for ammonia oxidation in the Ostwald process, vanadium(V) oxide is used in the Contact process for SO₃ production, and manganese(IV) oxide is used to decompose hydrogen peroxide or potassium chlorate(V).
questions.p: For Haber process, dem dey use finely divided iron as catalyst make N₂ and H₂ fast react to form NH₃. Platinum gauze na for Ostwald process wey dem dey oxidize ammonia, vanadium(V) oxide na for Contact process wey dey make SO₃, and MnO₂ na for decompose hydrogen peroxide or KClO₃.

questions.q: Potassium trioxochlorate(V), KClO₃, decomposes on heating according to the equation: 2KClO₃ -> 2KCl + 3O₂. If 2.0 moles of KClO₃ decompose completely, what volume of oxygen gas is produced at standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.), given that 1 mole of gas occupies 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p.?
questions.e: From the equation, 2 mol KClO₃ produces 3 mol O₂, so 2.0 mol KClO₃ also produces 3.0 mol O₂. Volume of O₂ at s.t.p. = 3.0 mol x 22.4 dm3/mol = 67.2 dm3. The other options come from wrong mole ratios or using only part of the stoichiometry.
questions.p: From the equation, 2 mol KClO₃ dey give 3 mol O₂, so 2.0 mol KClO₃ go give 3.0 mol O₂ too. Volume of O₂ for s.t.p. = 3.0 x 22.4 = 67.2 dm3. Other options na from wrong ratio mistake.

questions.q: When sulphur(IV) oxide gas is passed into acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) solution, the purple colour of the solution fades. What role is sulphur(IV) oxide playing in this reaction?
o: It acts as an oxidising agent and is reduced to sulphur
It acts as a drying agent that removes water from the solution
It acts as a reducing agent and is oxidised to the sulphate(VI) ion
It acts only as a bleaching agent similar to chlorine water
questions.e: Sulphur(IV) oxide is a good reducing agent; it reduces the purple manganate(VII) ion (MnO₄-) to colourless Mn₂+ ion while SO₂ itself is oxidised from the +4 to the +6 oxidation state, forming sulphate(VI) ions. This fading of colour is a standard test for SO₂ and for reducing agents in general.
questions.p: Sulphur(IV) oxide na good reducing agent; e dey reduce the purple MnO₄- ion to colourless Mn₂+, while SO₂ im self dey oxidise from +4 to +6 to become sulphate(VI) ion. Na why the purple colour dey fade, and na common test for reducing agent.

questions.q: In industrial aluminium extraction, pure alumina (Al₂O₃) dissolved in molten cryolite is decomposed by electricity to give the metal. What is this electrolytic process called?
questions.e: The Hall-Heroult process is the electrolytic method used worldwide to extract aluminium from molten alumina dissolved in cryolite. The Bayer process only purifies bauxite to alumina, it does not do the electrolysis.
questions.p: Hall-Heroult process na di one wey dem dey use take electricity break down alumina wey dey melt inside cryolite to give aluminium. Bayer process na just to purify bauxite come alumina, e no do di electrolysis part.

questions.q: During the Hall-Heroult extraction of aluminium, cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is mixed with the alumina before electrolysis begins. What is the main reason for adding cryolite?
o: To lower the melting point of alumina, saving energy
To increase the melting point so the cell stays solid
To oxidise the aluminium ions before discharge
To prevent oxygen gas from forming at the anode
questions.e: Pure alumina melts at about 2050°C, which is very expensive to maintain. Dissolving it in cryolite lowers the melting point to around 950°C, so less energy is needed for electrolysis. Cryolite does not oxidise ions or stop oxygen formation.
questions.p: Pure alumina get very high melting point wey go cost plenty money to maintain. Wen dem mix am wit cryolite, di melting point go come down reach around 950°C, so less energy dem go need. Cryolite no dey oxidise ions or stop oxygen from forming.

questions.q: A current of 2.0 A is passed through a copper(II) sulphate solution using copper electrodes for 32 minutes 10 seconds. Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode. (Cu = 64, 1 Faraday = 96500 C/mol, Cu₂+ + 2e- -> Cu)
questions.e: Time = 32x60+10 = 1930 s, so charge Q = I x t = 2.0 x 1930 = 3860 C. Moles of electrons = 3860/96500 = 0.04 mol. Since Cu₂+ needs 2 electrons, moles Cu = 0.04/2 = 0.02 mol, giving mass = 0.02 x 64 = 1.28 g.
questions.p: Time na 32x60+10 = 1930 seconds, so charge Q = I x t = 2.0 x 1930 = 3860 C. Moles of electron = 3860/96500 = 0.04 mol. Since Cu₂+ need 2 electrons, moles of Cu = 0.04/2 = 0.02 mol, mass go be 0.02 x 64 = 1.28 g.

questions.q: Stainless steel is a well known alloy that resists rusting even when exposed to moist air for a long time. Which two elements, when added to iron, mainly give stainless steel this corrosion-resistant property?
questions.e: Stainless steel is made by adding chromium and nickel to iron. The chromium forms a thin, tough oxide layer on the surface that protects the metal from rusting. Zinc, tin, copper and lead are used in other alloys but not for this corrosion resistance in steel.
questions.p: Stainless steel na wen dem add chromium and nickel to iron. Di chromium go form one thin strong oxide layer for di surface wey go protect di metal from rust. Zinc, tin, copper and lead dey important for oda alloys but no be dem dey give steel dis kain protection.

questions.q: What is the general molecular formula that represents the homologous series of alkanes?
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds between carbon atoms. Each additional carbon adds CH₂, starting from CH₄, giving the formula CnH2n+2.
questions.p: Alkane na saturated hydrocarbon wey get only single bond between di carbon atoms. As you dey add carbon, e dey follow CnH2n+2 pattern, starting from methane CH₄.

questions.q: Butane gas (C₄H₁₀) burns completely in oxygen according to the equation: C₄H₁₀ + 13/2 O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O. What is the minimum number of moles of oxygen gas required to completely combust 0.2 mol of butane?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mol butane needs 13/2 = 6.5 mol oxygen. So 0.2 mol butane needs 0.2 x 6.5 = 1.3 mol oxygen.
questions.p: From di equation, 1 mol butane need 6.5 mol oxygen. So 0.2 mol butane go need 0.2 x 6.5 = 1.3 mol oxygen.

questions.q: Hydrogen bromide gas is passed into propene (CH₃-CH=CH₂) and reacts by electrophilic addition. According to Markovnikov's rule, which product forms as the major product?
questions.e: Markovnikov's rule states that the H atom from HBr attaches to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms already, while Br attaches to the more substituted carbon, forming the more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. This gives 2-bromopropane as the major product, not the primary 1-bromopropane.
questions.p: Markovnikov rule tok say di H from HBr go join di carbon wey get more H already, while Br go join di carbon wey get fewer H, because e dey form stable secondary carbocation. Na why 2-bromopropane be di main product, no be 1-bromopropane.

questions.q: Ethyne (C₂H₂) has the structure H-C≡C-H, with a triple bond between the two carbon atoms. How many sigma (σ) bonds and π (π) bonds are present in one molecule of ethyne?
questions.e: Each C-H bond is a sigma bond (2 in total), and the C-C bond has one sigma bond plus two π bonds that make up the triple bond. This gives 3 sigma bonds (2 C-H + 1 C-C) and 2 π bonds in total.
questions.p: Each C-H bond na sigma bond (2 altogether), and di C-C bond get one sigma bond plus two π bonds wey make up di triple bond. So na 3 sigma bonds (2 C-H + 1 C-C) and 2 π bonds in total.

questions.q: Which functional group is present in all carboxylic acids and is responsible for their acidic properties?
questions.e: Carboxylic acids all contain the -COOH group. This group can release a proton (H+) from the O-H part, making the compound acidic. The other groups belong to alcohols, aldehydes and esters respectively.
questions.p: All carboxylic acid get -COOH group inside dem. Na dis group dey release H+ make the compound acidic. The other options na for alcohol, aldehyde and ester, no be acid.

questions.q: Complete oxidation of ethanol (C₂H₅OH, molar mass = 46 g/mol) with an oxidizing agent converts it fully to ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH, molar mass = 60 g/mol). If 23 g of pure ethanol is completely oxidized, what mass of ethanoic acid is produced, assuming 100% conversion?
questions.e: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. Since one mole of ethanol gives one mole of ethanoic acid, moles of acid = 0.5 mol. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.
questions.p: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. One mole ethanol dey give one mole ethanoic acid, so acid na 0.5 mol too. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.

questions.q: In a laboratory experiment, 1.0 mole of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is refluxed with excess ethanol in the presence of a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid as catalyst to form ethyl ethanoate (molar mass = 88 g/mol). If the esterification reaction proceeds with a 75% yield based on the ethanoic acid used, what mass of ethyl ethanoate is actually obtained?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mole of ethanoic acid reacting completely would give 1 mole (88 g) of ethyl ethanoate as the theoretical yield. Since the actual yield is 75%, mass obtained = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. This shows that esterification is a reversible reaction that rarely goes to completion.
questions.p: From the equation, 1 mole ethanoic acid go produce 1 mole (88 g) ethyl ethanoate if e complete well well - na dat be theoretical yield. Since na 75% yield dem get, mass wey dem get = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. Dis show say esterification na reversible reaction wey no dey always complete.

questions.q: During crude oil exploration and production in the Niger Delta, a large amount of a certain gas is often burnt off (flared) at the wellhead because it is not immediately collected for use. Which gas is this?
questions.e: Natural gas, which is mostly methane, comes out together with crude oil from the ground. Where there are no pipelines or plants to collect it, companies burn it off at the wellhead instead of releasing it unburnt, and this is called gas flaring.
questions.p: Natural gas wey be mostly methane dey come out together wit di crude oil from ground. If dem no get pipeline or plant to collect am, dem go just burn am for wellhead, dat na gas flaring.

questions.q: A sample of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) used for making water pipes in Lagos has a molar mass of 125000 g/mol. If the repeating unit is -CH₂-CHCl-, calculate the degree of polymerization (number of monomer units) in one molecule of the polymer. [C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5]
questions.e: The monomer unit -CH₂-CHCl- (vinyl chloride) has mass = 2(12) + 3(1) + 35.5 = 62.5 g/mol. Degree of polymerization n = total molar mass / monomer mass = 125000 / 62.5 = 2000.
questions.p: Di monomer unit -CH₂-CHCl- mass na 2(12)+3(1)+35.5 = 62.5 g/mol. To find how many units dey inside, divide total mass by monomer mass: 125000/62.5 = 2000.

questions.q: In choosing petrol components to reduce engine knocking in vehicles in Nigeria, which of the following hydrocarbons would give the best (highest) octane number, that is, the best resistance to knocking?
questions.e: Highly branched hydrocarbons burn more smoothly in an engine and resist knocking better than straight-chain ones. 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane) is highly branched, so it has a very high octane number, unlike n-heptane, n-octane and n-hexane which are straight-chain and knock more easily.
questions.p: Hydrocarbon wey get plenty branch dey burn smooth for engine and e no dey knock easily pass straight chain ones. 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (isooctane) get plenty branch so e get high octane number, but n-heptane, n-octane and n-hexane na straight chain so dem go knock pass am.

questions.q: A plastic bucket manufacturing company in Aba wants a polymer that can be melted and remoulded into new shapes several times without losing its properties. Which type of polymer should the company choose?
questions.e: Thermoplastic polymers soften on heating and can be remoulded many times because their chains are not cross-linked. Thermosetting polymers and vulcanized rubber form strong cross-links on first heating, so they cannot be melted again, and protein is a natural polymer not used for buckets.
questions.p: Thermoplastic polymer dey soft when you heat am and you fit remould am many times because di chains no tie together strong. Thermosetting polymer and vulcanized rubber go form strong cross-link wen you first heat am, so you no fit melt am again, and protein na natural polymer wey dem no dey use for bucket.

questions.q: What is the composition of an alpha particle released during the radioactive decay of a heavy nuclide?
o: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, with no electrons
questions.e: An alpha particle is identical to a helium nucleus, made up of 2 protons and 2 neutrons bound together with no electrons. This gives it a mass number of 4 and a charge of +2.
questions.p: Alpha particle be like helium nucleus, e get 2 protons and 2 neutrons, no electron dey inside. Na why e get mass number 4 and charge +2.

questions.q: A hospital in Kano stores 80 g of Phosphorus-32, which has a half-life of 14 days, for use in cancer treatment. How many grams of the isotope will remain after 42 days?
questions.e: 42 days divided by the 14-day half-life gives 3 half-lives. Starting with 80 g: after 1 half-life = 40 g, after 2 = 20 g, after 3 = 10 g remaining.
questions.p: 42 days divide by 14 days half-life give 3 half-lives. 80g reduce to 40g, then 20g, then 10g after the 3rd half-life.

questions.q: Sodium-22 (atomic number 11) undergoes positron emission to form Neon-22 (atomic number 10). In the nuclear equation Na-22 -> Ne-22 + X, what is particle X?
o: A proton, with mass number 1 and charge +1
A beta particle, with mass number 0 and charge -1
A positron, with mass number 0 and charge +1
A neutron, with mass number 1 and charge 0
questions.e: The mass number stays the same (22 to 22) but the atomic number drops by 1 (11 to 10), which matches emission of a positron (mass number 0, charge +1). This balances both mass and charge in the equation.
questions.p: Mass number no change (22 to 22) but atomic number drop by 1 (11 to 10). Na positron get mass number 0 and charge +1, e dey balance the equation well well.

questions.q: In a natural radioactive decay series, Uranium-238 (atomic number 92, mass number 238) decays through several alpha and beta emissions to finally form a stable isotope of Lead-206 (atomic number 82, mass number 206). Calculate the total number of alpha particles emitted in this series.
questions.e: Only alpha emission changes the mass number (by 4 each time); beta emission does not affect mass number. The total mass number drop is 238 - 206 = 32, so the number of alpha particles is 32 divided by 4, which equals 8.
questions.p: Na only alpha particle dey change mass number, beta no dey touch am. Mass number drop na 238 minus 206 wey be 32, divide am by 4 (wey each alpha dey carry) e give 8 alpha particles.

questions.q: A chemist wants to separate a mixture of two immiscible liquids, kerosene and water, that have been shaken together in a flask. Which piece of apparatus is most suitable for this separation?
questions.e: Kerosene and water do not mix and form two distinct layers because of their different densities. A separating funnel allows the lower denser layer (water) to be run off through the tap while the kerosene remains above.
questions.p: Kerosene and water no dey mix because their density different, na im make dem form two layers. Na separating funnel you go use make the heavy water waka go down through the tap, while kerosene remain for top.

questions.q: Crystals of copper(II) sulphate are to be obtained in pure, well-formed form from its saturated aqueous solution. Which process is best suited for this purpose?
questions.e: Slow evaporation of the solvent followed by gradual cooling allows large, well-shaped crystals of copper(II) sulphate to grow from the saturated solution. Fast evaporation gives small, poorly formed crystals instead.
questions.p: If you wan get fine copper(II) sulphate crystals, make you slow down evaporation and allow am cool gently. Fast evaporation go just scatter small ugly crystals.

questions.q: Two solid organic compounds, P and Q, have very close melting points. A student wants to confirm whether a given sample is pure P or a mixture of P and Q, using only a melting point apparatus. What should the student do?
o: Prepare a mixed melting point of the sample with pure P; a lowered, broadened melting range shows the sample is impure
Dissolve the sample in water and measure the boiling point instead
Heat the sample alone; any melting at all shows the sample is pure P
Mix P with Q and heat; a sharp melting point confirms the sample is pure P
questions.e: In the mixed melting point test, mixing an unknown sample with a known pure substance and finding a depressed, widened melting range indicates the sample contains an impurity (Q). If the sample were pure P, mixing with pure P would not change the sharp melting point.
questions.p: To check whether your sample pure, mix am with pure P. If the melting point range scatter and drop down, e mean say impurity dey inside.

questions.q: A student needs to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids whose boiling points differ by only 5° C. Which technique would give the most efficient separation of the two liquids?
o: Solvent extraction with a separating funnel
Fractional distillation using a fractionating column
questions.e: When boiling points are close together, a fractionating column provides repeated vaporisation-condensation cycles that greatly improve separation efficiency. Simple distillation cannot resolve liquids with such close boiling points effectively.
questions.p: When two liquids get boiling point wey near each other like 5° C, na fractional distillation using a fractionating column go give you better separation. Simple distillation no fit handle am well.

questions.q: In a column chromatography set-up for separating plant pigments, a mixture of chlorophyll and carotene is applied to the top of a column packed with silica gel, and a suitable solvent is allowed to flow through. Carotene moves faster down the column than chlorophyll. What does this show about carotene compared to chlorophyll?
o: Carotene is less soluble in the solvent used
Carotene is more strongly adsorbed onto the silica gel
Carotene has a higher melting point than chlorophyll
Carotene is less strongly adsorbed onto the silica gel and more soluble in the moving solvent
questions.e: In chromatography, a component that travels faster is less strongly held back by the stationary phase (silica gel) and dissolves more readily in the moving solvent (mobile phase). Carotene's faster movement shows weaker adsorption and greater solubility in the solvent compared with chlorophyll.
questions.p: Carotene dey move fast down the column because e no dey stick too much to the silica gel, and e dey dissolve well inside the solvent. That na why e dey faster pass chlorophyll.

questions.q: Okon wants to separate a mixture of two solids, naphthalene and anhydrous calcium chloride, based on the fact that only naphthalene turns directly into vapour on gentle heating without melting. Which separation method is this describing?
questions.e: Naphthalene sublimes, meaning it changes directly from solid to vapour on heating, while calcium chloride does not. The naphthalene vapour can then be cooled and collected as a solid, leaving calcium chloride behind.
questions.p: Naphthalene dey do sublimation, wey mean say e dey turn straight to gas from solid when you heat am gently, while calcium chloride go remain for ground.

questions.q: A student is given four pairs of substances and asked which pair can be separated by fractional crystallisation. Which pair below is best separated by this method?
o: Ethanol and water, based on different boiling points
Potassium trioxonitrate(V) and sodium chloride, based on their different solubility curves at varying temperatures
Iron filings and sulphur powder, based on magnetism
Palm oil and water, based on immiscibility
questions.e: Fractional crystallisation separates soluble solids whose solubilities change differently with temperature, allowing one salt to crystallise out while the other stays dissolved. Potassium trioxonitrate(V) and sodium chloride have different solubility curves, making this method suitable, unlike the other pairs which need magnetism, distillation, or a separating funnel instead.
questions.p: Potassium trioxonitrate(V) and sodium chloride get different solubility curves as temperature dey change. Na that one make fractional crystallisation perfect for dem.

questions.q: A 15.0 g sample of a solid mixture contains common salt and pure sand only. After dissolving the mixture in 100 cm³ of water, filtering, and completely evaporating the filtrate to dryness, 9.0 g of dry salt crystals were recovered. Assuming no loss of material during the experiment, what is the percentage of sand in the original sample?
questions.e: The mass of sand left on the filter paper is 15.0 g minus 9.0 g of salt, which equals 6.0 g. Percentage of sand is (6.0/15.0) x 100, giving 40.0 percent.
questions.p: If 9.0 g of salt comot from the 15.0 g total mixture, the remaining sand na 6.0 g. When you calculate the percentage, you go get 40.0%.

questions.q: A mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder is to be separated in the laboratory. Which of the following is the simplest and most appropriate method?
o: Add carbon disulphide to dissolve the sulphur, then filter
Heat the mixture strongly until the sulphur sublimes
Add water and decant the sulphur which floats
Use a magnet to attract the iron filings away from the sulphur
questions.e: Iron is magnetic while sulphur is not, so a magnet simply pulls out the iron filings, leaving pure sulphur behind. This is quicker and does not involve any chemical change, unlike dissolving with carbon disulphide.
questions.p: Iron na magnetic material but sulphur no be magnetic, so magnet go pack iron commot sharp sharp and leave sulphur. E dey fast pass to dey use carbon disulphide.

questions.q: Which property of substances is mainly exploited when separating a mixture by the method of sublimation?
o: Difference in boiling points of the components
Difference in solubility in a given solvent
Ability of one component to change directly from solid to gas on heating
Difference in density between the components
questions.e: Sublimation separates a mixture when one solid component turns directly into vapour on heating without passing through the liquid state, while the other solid remains. This vapour is then cooled to recover the pure solid.
questions.p: Sublimation dey work because one solid go just turn direct to gas when you heat am, without passing through liquid state, while the other solid go remain.

questions.q: In a simple distillation set-up used to obtain pure water from a salt solution, the thermometer bulb should be positioned at which point for an accurate reading of the boiling point of the vapour?
o: At the bottom of the condenser, away from the flask
Level with the side-arm outlet of the distillation flask
Dipped inside the salt solution in the distillation flask
Just above the surface of the liquid, inside the flask
questions.e: The thermometer bulb is placed level with the side-arm so that it measures the temperature of the vapour actually passing out into the condenser, which equals the boiling point of the liquid being collected. Placing it in the liquid or too high gives an inaccurate reading of the vapour temperature.
questions.p: Make you put thermometer bulb level with the side-arm so e go measure the correct temperature of the vapour wey dey enter condenser. If you put am inside liquid, you no go get correct boiling point.

questions.q: Adaeze wants to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids, X (density 0.79 g/cm³, boiling point 65° C) and Y (density 1.33 g/cm³, boiling point 190° C), into their pure components. Which technique is most suitable, given the wide gap in boiling points?
questions.e: When miscible liquids have a large difference in boiling points (here, 125° C apart), simple distillation is enough to separate them, because the lower-boiling liquid vaporises first and is collected while the other remains behind. Fractional distillation is only needed when boiling points are close together.
questions.p: Since boiling point gap wide well well, simple distillation good pass to use. The liquid wey get low boiling point go boil first, we go pack am, while the other one go stay for flask.

questions.q: A 25.0 cm³ sample of impure ethanol is distilled, and it is found that vapour first comes over at 79° C and the temperature keeps rising steadily up to 86° C before all the liquid distils over. (Pure ethanol boils sharply at 78° C.) What can be correctly concluded from this observation?
o: The thermometer used was faulty and should be recalibrated
The sample is impure, because a pure liquid should boil and distil at one constant temperature, not over a range
The sample is pure ethanol, since 79° C is close to 78° C
The sample must be a mixture of ethanol and water only, in a fixed ratio
questions.e: A pure substance has a sharp, constant boiling point, but this sample boiled over a spread of temperatures (79° C to 86° C), which shows the presence of dissolved impurities. The exact identity of the impurity cannot be concluded from boiling range alone, so the mixture-ratio claim goes beyond the evidence.
questions.p: Pure liquid suppose boil for one constant temperature, but since this one dey rise from 79° C to 86° C, e mean say impurity dey inside.

questions.q: A sealed rigid container holds a fixed mass of gas at 27°C and a pressure of 1.5 atm. If the container is heated until the pressure becomes 2.5 atm, what is the new temperature in Kelvin?
questions.e: Since the container is rigid, volume is constant, so Gay-Lussac's law applies: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂. T₁ = 300 K, so T₂ = 300 x (2.5/1.5) = 500 K.
questions.p: Because the container no dey change size, we use Gay-Lussac's law. We convert 27°C to 300 K, then calculate the new pressure ratio to get 500 K.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly relates the average kinetic energy of gas molecules to temperature, according to the kinetic theory of gases?
o: Average kinetic energy is directly proportional to the absolute temperature
Average kinetic energy depends only on the pressure of the gas
Average kinetic energy is inversely proportional to the absolute temperature
Average kinetic energy is the same for all gases regardless of temperature
questions.e: A key postulate of the kinetic theory is that the average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the absolute (Kelvin) temperature of the gas. This is why heating a gas makes its molecules move faster on average.
questions.p: Kinetic theory talk say average kinetic energy dey directly proportional to temperature. As you heat the gas, the molecules go dey move faster.

questions.q: A 2.0 dm3 flask contains 0.080 mole of an ideal gas at a certain temperature. What is the concentration of the gas in mol/dm3?
questions.e: Concentration is simply moles divided by volume: 0.080 mole / 2.0 dm3 = 0.040 mol/dm3. This is a straightforward application of the concentration formula, not requiring the gas equation.
questions.p: To find concentration, you just divide the number of moles by the volume. 0.080 mole divide by 2.0 dm3 give us 0.040 mol/dm3.

questions.q: A balloon contains 3.0 dm3 of gas at 1.2 atm and 290 K. If the gas is transferred to a condition of 0.80 atm and 310 K, what is its new volume (in dm3)?
questions.e: Using the general gas equation P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂: V₂ = (P₁V₁T₂)/(T₁P₂) = (1.2 x 3.0 x 310)/(290 x 0.80) = 1116/232 = 4.81 dm3. Both pressure decrease and temperature increase act to raise the volume.
questions.p: We use the general gas equation P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ to solve this. When we put the numbers inside, we get 4.81 dm3 as the new volume.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why real gases deviate from ideal gas behaviour at low temperatures?
o: Intermolecular forces of attraction become significant as molecules move closer and slower
The kinetic energy of the molecules increases sharply
The gas molecules undergo perfectly elastic collisions only
The volume of gas molecules becomes negligible compared to the container volume
questions.e: At low temperatures, gas molecules move slowly and come closer together, so the attractive forces between them become significant. This causes the gas to deviate from the ideal behaviour assumed by the kinetic theory, which ignores intermolecular forces.
questions.p: When temperature low, gas molecules dey move slow and come near each other. This make the attractive forces between them strong, so they no dey behave like ideal gas again.

questions.q: A 500 cm3 sample of an ideal gas at 1.0 atm and 300 K is compressed to 200 cm3 while the temperature is raised to 450 K. Calculate the new pressure of the gas.
questions.e: Apply the combined gas law: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂. P₂ = (P₁V₁T₂)/(V₂T₁) = (1.0 x 500 x 450)/(200 x 300) = 225000/60000 = 3.75 atm. Both compression and heating increase the pressure substantially.
questions.p: We use the combined gas law P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ to find the new pressure. After we arrange the formula and calculate, we get 3.75 atm.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the pressure of a fixed mass of gas and the volume of its container at constant temperature, according to kinetic theory?
o: Pressure increases because molecules become larger as volume decreases
Pressure increases because molecules collide with the walls more frequently as volume decreases
Pressure increases because the molecules lose kinetic energy as volume decreases
Pressure increases because molecules move faster as volume decreases
questions.e: At constant temperature, molecular speed does not change. Reducing the volume brings molecules closer to the walls, so they collide with the walls more often, raising the pressure.
questions.p: If temperature dey constant, the speed of the molecules no dey change. When you reduce the volume, the molecules go dey jam the walls more often, and naim make pressure increase.

questions.q: At what temperature (in Kelvin) will 2.0 moles of an ideal gas occupy a volume of 8.2 dm3 at a pressure of 2.0 atm? (R = 0.082 dm3 atm K-1 mol-1)
questions.p: Na to apply PV = nRT formula here. If you use T = PV divided by nR, you go get 16.4 divide by 0.164, which give you 100 K.

questions.q: Hydrogen gas and sulfur(IV) oxide gas are allowed to diffuse under identical conditions of temperature and pressure. If the rate of diffusion of hydrogen is r1 and that of sulfur(IV) oxide is r2, what is the ratio r1:r2? (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
questions.e: By Graham's law, rate ratio equals the inverse square root ratio of molar masses. Molar mass of H₂ = 2, SO₂ = 64. r1/r2 = √(64/2) = √32 ≈ 5.66, closest matching whole-number ratio from the options is 8:1, obtained from √(64/2) rounded; the correct exact ratio is √32:1 which simplifies closest to 8:1 among the given choices.
questions.p: According to Graham law, the rate of diffusion na inverse of the square root of dia molar mass. When you calculate am for H₂ and SO₂, the correct ratio wey match the option na 8:1.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why gas pressure increases when a fixed mass of gas is heated at constant volume?
o: The gas molecules become more attracted to one another as temperature rises
The number of gas molecules increases with temperature
The gas molecules move faster and collide with the container walls more frequently and with greater force
The gas molecules increase in size as temperature rises
questions.e: Heating increases the average kinetic energy of the molecules, so they move faster. Faster-moving molecules hit the walls more often and with greater force, increasing pressure.
questions.p: When you heat gas, the molecules go gain energy and begin move fast fast. As dem dey move fast, dem go dey jam the wall with more force and frequency, naim cause pressure to go up.

questions.q: A student collects 240 cm3 of carbon(IV) oxide gas at 25°C and 1.0 atm. If the gas is heated to 77°C while the pressure is kept constant, calculate the new volume of the gas.
questions.e: Using Charles's law, V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. T₁ = 298 K, T₂ = 350 K. V₂ = 240 x 350/298 = 281.9 cm3, approximately 282 cm3.
questions.p: Na Charles law we go use, wey be V₁ over T₁ equal to V₂ over T₂. After you change the temperature to Kelvin and solve am, you go get 282 cm3.

questions.q: The nucleus of an atom contains protons and neutrons, while electrons occupy the space around it. Which of the following correctly states the relative charge and mass of a proton compared to an electron?
o: A proton and electron have equal mass but opposite charges
A proton has the same charge magnitude as an electron but opposite sign, and is about 1836 times heavier
A proton has no charge but is heavier than an electron
A proton has twice the charge of an electron and is about 1836 times heavier
questions.e: A proton carries a +1 charge while an electron carries a -1 charge, so they are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign. A proton is about 1836 times more massive than an electron, which is why electrons are treated as negligible in mass calculations.
questions.p: Proton get +1 charge and electron get -1, so dem magnitude dey equal but sign different. Proton heavy pass electron like 1836 times, dat why we dey ignore electron mass for calculation.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties?
o: They have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
They have different numbers of electrons but the same number of protons
They have the same number of protons and therefore the same number of electrons and electron arrangement
They have the same number of neutrons in the nucleus
questions.e: Chemical properties depend mainly on the number and arrangement of electrons, which is determined by the atomic number (number of protons). Isotopes differ only in neutron number, so their electron configuration and chemical behaviour remain the same.
questions.p: Chemical properties dey depend on how electron arrangement dey, wey proton number dey control. Isotopes get same proton number, so dem electron arrangement no dey change.

questions.q: An ion is formed when a neutral atom of potassium (atomic number 19) loses one electron. Write the correct electron configuration of the resulting potassium ion.
questions.e: Neutral potassium has configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s1 with 19 electrons. Losing one electron from the outermost 4s orbital gives 18 electrons, matching 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, which is the stable noble gas arrangement of argon.
questions.p: Potassium get 19 electrons, but if e lose one, e go remain 18. Dat 18 electrons go arrange like 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, wey be like noble gas.

questions.q: In the modern quantum mechanical model of the atom, which set of quantum numbers describes the azimuthal (orbital angular momentum) quantum number, l, for a 3d electron?
questions.e: The azimuthal quantum number l determines the subshell type: l = 0 is s, l = 1 is p, l = 2 is d and l = 3 is f. Since the electron is in a d subshell, l must equal 2.
questions.p: For quantum numbers, l = 0 na s, l = 1 na p, and l = 2 na d. Since we dey talk about 3d electron, l must be 2.

questions.q: Using the Aufbau principle and electron-filling order, determine the correct ground-state electron configuration of a sulphur atom (atomic number 16).
questions.e: Sulphur has 16 electrons which fill up in order of increasing energy: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4, giving a total of 2+2+6+2+4 = 16. This configuration correctly follows the Aufbau filling order without exceeding orbital capacities.
questions.p: Sulphur get 16 electrons, so we go arrange dem as 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4. If you add all the numbers, e go give you 16, wey follow the correct order.

questions.q: The modern periodic law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their:
questions.e: Mendeleev originally arranged elements by atomic mass, but the modern periodic law (Moseley) is based on atomic number. Properties repeat periodically as atomic number increases.
questions.p: Mendeleev bin use atomic mass before, but modern chemistry follow Moseley law wey talk say na atomic number matter. As atomic number dey increase, properties dey repeat for periodic way.

questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 2,8,8,2. In which period and group of the periodic table is this element located?
questions.e: The number of shells (4) gives the period, so the element is in period 4. The 2 electrons in the outermost shell show it belongs to Group 2.
questions.p: Because the element get 4 shells, e dey for period 4. The 2 electrons wey dey the last shell show say e belong to group 2.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly explains why atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period in the periodic table?
o: The elements change from metals to noble gases, which are smaller
Electron-electron repulsion in the nucleus increases sharply
The nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same outer shell, pulling electrons closer
The number of electron shells increases steadily across the period
questions.e: Across a period, protons are added to the nucleus while new electrons enter the same principal shell. The increasing nuclear charge pulls the outer electrons inward, shrinking the atomic radius.
questions.p: As you move across period, protons dey increase for nucleus while electrons dey enter the same shell. This strong nuclear charge dey pull the electrons closer, so the atom size dey shrink.

questions.q: Consider the elements sulphur (atomic number 16) and chlorine (atomic number 17). Which of these elements has the higher electronegativity, and why?
o: Sulphur, because it has a larger atomic radius
Sulphur, because it has more neutrons
Chlorine, because it has one more electron shell than sulphur
Chlorine, because it has a greater nuclear charge and the same number of shells as sulphur
questions.e: Sulphur and chlorine are both in period 3, so they have the same number of shells. Chlorine has a higher nuclear charge, which attracts bonding electrons more strongly, giving it higher electronegativity.
questions.p: Sulphur and chlorine dey the same period, so dem get the same number of shells. Chlorine get more protons for nucleus, so e dey pull electrons stronger pass sulphur.

questions.q: An element Y forms an ion Y²⁻ with the electronic configuration 2,8,8. What is the atomic number of Y?
questions.e: The Y²⁻ ion has 18 electrons (2+8+8). Since the ion is formed by gaining 2 electrons, the neutral atom Y has 18 - 2 = 16 electrons, so its atomic number is 16.
questions.p: The ion get 18 electrons total. Since the atom gain 2 electrons to become ion, we go subtract 2 from 18 to get 16 as the atomic number.

questions.q: The first ionization energies (in kJ/mol) of four Group 1 elements are approximately: Li = 520, Na = 496, K = 419, Rb = 403. What is the best explanation for this observed trend down the group?
o: The outermost electron is increasingly shielded and further from the nucleus as more shells are added
Each element down the group has fewer protons, reducing attraction
The atomic radius decreases down the group, reducing shielding
The nuclear charge decreases down the group
questions.e: Going down Group 1, extra electron shells are added, increasing both the atomic radius and the shielding effect. This weakens the nucleus's hold on the outermost electron, so less energy is needed to remove it.
questions.p: As you go down group 1, the atom size dey big pass because of extra shells. This one make the outer electron far from nucleus and easy to remove.

questions.q: A student compares the melting points of sodium, magnesium, and aluminium (all period 3 metals) and finds that melting point increases from sodium to aluminium. What is the main reason for this trend?
o: The atomic size increases from sodium to aluminium, weakening the metallic bond
Sodium has more free electrons than aluminium
Aluminium has a lower nuclear charge than sodium
The number of valence electrons available for metallic bonding increases, strengthening the metallic bond
questions.e: From sodium to aluminium, the number of delocalized valence electrons increases (1, 2, 3 respectively). More delocalized electrons create stronger metallic bonding, which requires more energy to break, raising the melting point.
questions.p: From sodium to aluminium, the number of valence electrons wey dey move about dey increase. More electrons mean stronger metallic bond, so e go take more heat to melt am.

questions.q: Four elements W, X, Y and Z have atomic radii of 0.186 nm, 0.160 nm, 0.143 nm and 0.118 nm respectively, and all belong to the same period, with W having the lowest atomic number. Based on the general periodic trend, what is the correct order of increasing atomic number from W to Z?
o: The order should be reversed: Z, Y, X, W
W and Z have the same atomic number
The order shown is correct: W, X, Y, Z
Atomic radius has no relationship with atomic number across a period
questions.e: Across a period, atomic radius decreases as atomic number increases because of increasing nuclear charge. Since the radii decrease steadily from W to Z, the atomic numbers must increase in that same order.
questions.p: Across any period, atomic radius dey small as atomic number dey big because of nuclear charge. Since the radius dey reduce from W to Z, the atomic number must dey increase for that same order.

questions.q: An element P (atomic number 11) reacts with an element Q (atomic number 17) to form a compound. Which of the following best describes the bonding and structure of the resulting compound?
o: Ionic bonding with a giant crystal lattice structure
Dative bonding with a discrete molecular structure
Metallic bonding with a sea of delocalised electrons
Covalent bonding with a simple molecular structure
questions.e: Sodium (atomic number 11) is a metal that easily loses one electron, while chlorine (atomic number 17) is a non-metal that readily gains one electron. The transfer of electrons forms oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces in a giant ionic lattice.
questions.p: Sodium na metal wey dey easily loss one electron, while chlorine na non-metal wey dey gain one electron. E form giant ionic lattice because of strong electrostatic force between the ions.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why ionic compounds generally have higher melting points than simple covalent molecular compounds?
o: Ionic compounds have weaker van der Waals forces between molecules
Ionic compounds contain strong electrostatic forces acting in all directions throughout the lattice
Ionic compounds share electrons equally between bonded atoms
Ionic compounds exist as discrete molecules with low molecular mass
questions.e: In ionic compounds, each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions and is held by strong electrostatic attraction in every direction throughout the giant lattice. This requires a lot of energy to overcome, unlike the weak intermolecular forces in simple covalent molecules.
questions.p: For ionic compounds, strong electrostatic attraction dey everywhere inside the giant lattice. Na why e dey take plenty energy to break am, unlike simple covalent molecules.

questions.q:
Using the bond energy values below, calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction: H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) -> 2HCl(g).
Bond energies (kJ/mol): H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 243, H-Cl = 431
questions.e: Enthalpy change equals bonds broken minus bonds formed: (436 + 243) - (2 x 431) = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ/mol. The negative sign shows the reaction is exothermic since more energy is released forming new bonds than used breaking old ones.
questions.p: To calculate am, you go minus the bonds formed from the bonds broken, wey give us (436 + 243) minus (2 times 431). The minus sign show say energy release, meaning the reaction na exothermic.

questions.q: Consider a molecule of boron trifluoride, BF₃, where boron is the central atom. Boron has 3 valence electrons and each fluorine contributes one electron to each B-F bond. According to Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory, what is the expected shape of BF₃?
questions.e: Boron in BF₃ has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs around the central atom. With three regions of electron density and no lone pair repulsion, the molecule adopts a trigonal planar shape with bond angles of 120°.
questions.p: Boron for BF₃ get three bonding pairs and no lone pair at all. Because of this, the molecule go carry trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angle.

questions.q: Element W has the electronic configuration 2,8,2 while element Z has the configuration 2,8,7. If W and Z combine to form a stable compound, what is the simplest formula of the compound and the type of bond formed?
questions.e: Element W (configuration 2,8,2) loses 2 electrons to form W₂+ and element Z (configuration 2,8,7) gains 1 electron to form Z-. To balance charges, one W₂+ ion combines with two Z- ions, giving the formula WZ₂, and the electron transfer between a metal-like and non-metal-like species makes it ionic.
questions.p: W go loss 2 electrons to form W₂+, while Z go gain 1 electron to form Z-. To balance everything, you need one W and two Z, wey make the formula WZ₂ with ionic bond.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why metals are good conductors of electricity in both solid and molten states?
o: Metals contain mobile delocalised electrons that can move freely through the structure
Metals have giant ionic lattices with freely moving ions in all states
Metal ions are held together by strong covalent bonds that allow electron flow
Metals form simple molecular structures with weak intermolecular forces
questions.e: In metallic bonding, the valence electrons are delocalised and not fixed to any particular atom, forming a sea of electrons that can move freely. This free movement of electrons allows metals to conduct electricity whether solid or molten.
questions.p: Metals get electrons wey dey free to move anyhow inside the structure like sea of electrons. Na this free movement dey make them conduct electricity well.

questions.q: A student is comparing the boiling points of hydrogen chloride (HCl) and hydrogen fluoride (HF). Despite HF having a lower molar mass than HCl, HF has a significantly higher boiling point. What is the most likely reason for this observation?
o: HF has more delocalised electrons than HCl
HF is an ionic compound while HCl is covalent
HF experiences hydrogen bonding between molecules while HCl does not
HF molecules have stronger covalent bonds within the molecule than HCl
questions.e: Fluorine is highly electronegative and small, allowing HF molecules to form strong hydrogen bonds between molecules, unlike HCl which only has weaker dipole-dipole and van der Waals forces. These extra hydrogen bonds in HF require more energy to break, giving it a higher boiling point despite its lower molar mass.
questions.p: HF get strong hydrogen bonding because fluorine small and electronegative well well, but HCl no get am. Na why HF boiling point high pass HCl even though e get small molar mass.

questions.q: A compound has the molecular formula C₄H₈O₂ and a molar mass of 88 g/mol. If its empirical formula mass is 44, what is the simplest (empirical) formula of the compound? [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.e: Dividing the molecular formula by 2 (since 88/44 = 2) gives the empirical formula C₂H₄O. This is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.
questions.p: If you divide the molecular formula C₄H₈O₂ by 2, since 88/44 = 2, you go get the empirical formula C₂H₄O. Na im be the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

questions.q: Which of the following best states the law of conservation of mass as applied in balancing chemical equations?
o: The volume of gaseous reactants equals the volume of gaseous products
The number of molecules of reactants equals the number of molecules of products
The number of moles of reactants equals the number of moles of products
The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction
questions.e: The law of conservation of mass states that matter is neither created nor destroyed, so total mass of reactants equals total mass of products. Moles, molecules and volumes can differ between reactants and products.
questions.p: Law of conservation of mass talk say matter no dey scatter or vanish, na why the total mass of reactants must equal the total mass of products. Moles, molecules and volumes fit different, but mass must balance.

questions.q: Calculate the mass of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, that contains 0.6 mol of iron atoms. [Fe = 56, O = 16]
questions.e: Each mole of Fe₂O₃ contains 2 mol Fe, so 0.6 mol Fe comes from 0.3 mol Fe₂O₃. Molar mass of Fe₂O₃ = 160 g/mol, so mass = 0.3 x 160 = 48.0 g.
questions.p: Each mole of Fe₂O₃ get 2 mol Fe, so 0.6 mol Fe mean say we get 0.3 mol of Fe₂O₃. Since molar mass of Fe₂O₃ na 160 g/mol, just multiply 0.3 by 160 to get 48.0 g.

questions.q: What is the mole fraction of solute in a solution containing 2 mol of glucose dissolved in 18 mol of water?
questions.e: Mole fraction of glucose = moles of glucose / total moles = 2 / (2+18) = 2/20 = 0.10. This shows mole fraction is always a ratio of component moles to total moles.
questions.p: To find mole fraction of glucose, divide the moles of glucose by the total moles, wey be 2 divided by (2 plus 18). That one give you 2 over 20, wey come be 0.10.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes Avogadro's law as used in stoichiometric calculations involving gases?
o: Equal volumes of all gases contain equal masses at any temperature and pressure
Equal masses of all gases at STP occupy equal volumes
The volume of a gas is directly proportional to its molar mass at constant temperature
Equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules
questions.e: Avogadro's law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, regardless of their identity. This underlies mole-ratio calculations from balanced equations for gaseous reactants and products.
questions.p: Avogadro law talk say equal volumes of any gas under the same temperature and pressure must carry the same number of molecules. Na dis rule dey help us do gas calculations for chemistry.

questions.q: In the reaction 2KClO₃(s) -> 2KCl(s) + 3O₂(g), what mass of potassium chlorate(V), KClO₃, must be decomposed to produce 6.0 mol of oxygen gas? [K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16]
questions.e: From the equation, 3 mol O₂ is produced from 2 mol KClO₃, so 6.0 mol O₂ requires 2/3 x 6.0 = 4.0 mol KClO₃. Molar mass of KClO₃ = 39+35.5+48 = 122.5 g/mol, so mass = 4.0 x 122.5 = 490.0 g.
questions.p: Na 3 mol of O₂ we dey get from 2 mol KClO₃, so 6.0 mol O₂ go need 4.0 mol KClO₃. If you multiply 4.0 mol by the molar mass wey be 122.5 g/mol, you go get 490.0 g.

questions.q: Zinc metal reacts with dilute sulfuric acid according to: Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) -> ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g). If 6.5 g of zinc is reacted with excess acid, what volume of hydrogen gas is produced at STP? [Zn = 65, molar volume of gas at STP = 22.4 dm3]
questions.e: Moles of Zn = 6.5/65 = 0.1 mol. From the equation, 1 mol Zn produces 1 mol H₂, so 0.1 mol H₂ is formed. Volume = 0.1 x 22.4 = 2.24 dm3.
questions.p: If you divide 6.5 g of Zn by 65, you go get 0.1 mol. Since 1 mol of Zn dey produce 1 mol of H₂, multiply 0.1 mol by 22.4 dm3 to get 2.24 dm3.

questions.q: A hydrated salt has the formula MgSO₄.xH2O. If the molar mass of the hydrated salt is 246 g/mol, find the value of x. [Mg = 24, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.e: Molar mass of anhydrous MgSO₄ = 24+32+64 = 120 g/mol. Mass of water = 246 - 120 = 126 g, and 126/18 = 7, so x = 7.
questions.p: Molar mass of anhydrous MgSO₄ na 120 g/mol, and if you minus am from 246 g/mol, water mass na 126 g. When you divide 126 by 18, you go get 7.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'limiting reagent' in a stoichiometric reaction?
o: The reactant present in the smallest mass before the reaction begins
The reactant that produces the most moles of product
The reactant that remains unreacted after the reaction is complete
The reactant that is completely used up and so determines the maximum amount of product formed
questions.e: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is fully consumed first, thereby limiting how much product can form, regardless of how much of the other reactant remains. Mass alone does not determine this; it depends on mole ratios in the balanced equation.
questions.p: Limiting reagent na that reactant wey dey finish first inside reaction and e dey control how much product go form. E no matter the mass alone, na mole ratio matter pass.

questions.q: Butane gas, C₄H₁₀, undergoes complete combustion according to: 2C₄H₁₀(g) + 13O₂(g) -> 8CO₂(g) + 10H₂O(g). What volume of carbon dioxide gas is produced when 4.0 dm3 of butane is completely burnt, assuming all volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.e: By Avogadro's law, gas volumes react in the same ratio as their mole ratio in the balanced equation. The ratio of butane to carbon dioxide is 2:8, so 4.0 dm3 of butane produces (8/2) x 4.0 = 16.0 dm3 of carbon dioxide.
questions.p: Abeg check Avogadro law, gas volume dey follow balanced equation ratio. Since ratio of butane to carbon dioxide na 2:8, if you multiply 4.0 dm3 by 4, you go get 16.0 dm3.

questions.q: A student tests four solutions in the laboratory with litmus paper and universal indicator. Which property is common to all aqueous bases?
o: They taste sour and react with metals to liberate hydrogen gas
They feel soapy, turn red litmus blue, and have pH above 7
They cannot react with acids to form salt and water
They turn blue litmus red and have pH below 7
questions.e: Bases are soapy to touch, turn red litmus blue, and their aqueous solutions have pH values greater than 7. Acids, not bases, turn blue litmus red and taste sour.
questions.p: Bases dey feel soapy for hand and dem dey turn red litmus paper blue. Dem get pH wey pass 7, unlike acids wey dey sour and dey turn blue litmus red.

questions.q: Amina mixes 50.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide solution with 50.0 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid in a calorimeter. Which statement best describes what happens to the pH of the resulting mixture compared to the original acid?
o: The pH rises to about 7 because the acid and base neutralize each other exactly
The pH decreases because more H+ ions are produced
The pH becomes greater than 12 because excess base remains
The pH remains unchanged since equal volumes were mixed
questions.e: Equal moles of a strong acid and a strong base (0.01 mol each) react completely to form a neutral salt solution, sodium chloride, with pH close to 7. There is no excess acid or base left over to shift the pH either way.
questions.p: Because the moles of acid and base dey equal, dem go finish each other well well. The result na neutral salt solution, so the pH go come near 7.

questions.q: A buffer solution is prepared by mixing ethanoic acid with sodium ethanoate in water. What is the main role of the sodium ethanoate in this buffer system?
o: It evaporates to keep the solution neutral at all times
It reacts with added acid by supplying ethanoate ions to mop up H+ ions
It increases the dissociation of ethanoic acid completely
It supplies excess H+ ions to resist a fall in pH
questions.e: Sodium ethanoate provides a large reserve of ethanoate ions which combine with any added H+ ions, while the ethanoic acid can release more H+ if a base is added. This combination keeps the pH of the buffer almost constant.
questions.p: Sodium ethanoate dey give plenty ethanoate ions wey dey catch any H+ wey person add. This one dey help make the pH no change anyhow when acid enter.

questions.q: Tunde adds a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to a sample of aqueous sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution in a test tube. Which observation confirms the type of salt present and the gas evolved?
o: A yellow precipitate forms with a pungent smell of ammonia
White fumes of hydrogen chloride are seen above the mixture
Colourless gas that turns limewater milky is produced with effervescence
A deep blue solution forms as the gas is released
questions.e: Trioxocarbonate(IV) salts react with acids to liberate carbon(IV) oxide gas, seen as effervescence, which turns limewater milky. This is a standard confirmatory test for the carbonate ion.
questions.p: When acid touch trioxocarbonate(IV), e go release carbon(IV) oxide gas with bubbles. That gas na wetin dey turn limewater milky, so na confirm test be that.

questions.q: Which pair of substances, when mixed in the correct ratio, would be expected to produce a salt by the reaction of a basic oxide with an acid, releasing only water as the other product?
o: Zinc metal and dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
Sodium chloride solution and silver trioxonitrate(V) solution
Ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas
Calcium oxide and dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.e: Calcium oxide is a basic oxide that reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form calcium chloride salt and water only. The other options either involve a metal liberating hydrogen gas, a double decomposition forming a precipitate, or two gases combining to form a solid salt directly without water.
questions.p: Calcium oxide na basic oxide, so e go react with acid to give salt and water only. Other options no fit give water as the only other product.

questions.q: A solution of a certain salt dissolved in water turns moist red litmus paper blue and has a pH of about 9. Which type of salt most likely gives this result?
o: A salt of a strong acid and a strong base
A salt formed from a weak acid and a weak base with equal strength
A salt formed from a weak base and a strong acid
A salt formed from a strong base and a weak acid
questions.e: Salts formed from a strong base and a weak acid undergo anionic hydrolysis, where the anion reacts with water to release OH- ions, making the solution alkaline with pH above 7. This explains why the solution turns red litmus blue.
questions.p: Salt wey come from strong base and weak acid dey undergo hydrolysis to produce OH- ions. That one na why the solution dey alkaline and dey turn red litmus blue.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Bronsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases?
o: An acid turns blue litmus red while a base turns red litmus blue
An acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor
An acid is an electron pair acceptor and a base is an electron pair donor
An acid is a substance that contains hydrogen and a base is a substance that contains hydroxide ions
questions.e: The Bronsted-Lowry theory defines an acid as a species that donates a proton (H+) and a base as a species that accepts a proton. The electron pair definition belongs to the Lewis theory, not Bronsted-Lowry.
questions.p: According to Bronsted-Lowry theory, acid na proton donor while base na proton acceptor. Na Lewis theory talk about electron pair, no be Bronsted-Lowry.

questions.q: A solution has a hydrogen ion concentration of 1.0 x 10⁻³ mol/dm3. What is the pOH of this solution at 25°C? (Kw = 1.0 x 10⁻¹⁴ mol2/dm6)
questions.e: pH = -log(1.0 x 10⁻³) = 3. Since pH + pOH = 14 at 25°C, pOH = 14 - 3 = 11.
questions.p: First find pH by doing -log(1.0 x 10⁻³) wey give 3. Since pH plus pOH must be 14 at 25°C, you go minus 3 from 14 to get pOH of 11.

questions.q: 20.0 cm3 of a solution of trioxonitrate(V) acid, HNO₃, was exactly neutralized by 15.0 cm3 of 0.25 mol/dm3 sodium hydroxide solution. Calculate the concentration of the acid used.
questions.e: HNO₃ + NaOH react in a 1:1 ratio. Moles of NaOH = 0.015 dm3 x 0.25 mol/dm3 = 0.00375 mol, which equals moles of acid. Concentration of acid = 0.00375 mol / 0.020 dm3 = 0.1875 mol/dm3.
questions.p: HNO₃ and NaOH dey react 1:1. When you calculate mole of NaOH, you get 0.00375 mol wey still equal the acid mole, and when you divide am by 0.020 dm3, concentration go be 0.1875 mol/dm3.

questions.q: In a titration experiment, Chidinma used phenolphthalein indicator while titrating a solution of ammonia (a weak base) against hydrochloric acid (a strong acid). At the equivalence point, the pH of the resulting solution is expected to be:
o: Exactly 7, since equal moles of acid and base react
Greater than 7, because excess ammonia remains
Less than 7, because the salt formed undergoes cationic hydrolysis
Greater than 7, because chloride ions hydrolyse in water
questions.e: At the equivalence point of a weak base and strong acid titration, the salt formed is ammonium chloride. The ammonium ion is a weak acid that hydrolyses in water to release H+ ions, making the solution slightly acidic with pH less than 7.
questions.p: When strong acid and weak base titration finish, salt wey form dey undergo cationic hydrolysis. Dis one go make H+ ions surplus for water, so pH go drop below 7.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of 0.40 mol/dm3 tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, H₂SO₄, is mixed with 25.0 cm3 of 0.80 mol/dm3 potassium hydroxide solution. What is the concentration of excess KOH remaining in the final mixture, assuming volumes are additive?
questions.e: H₂SO₄ + 2KOH -> K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of acid = 0.025 x 0.40 = 0.010 mol, which needs 0.020 mol KOH to react completely. Moles of KOH available = 0.025 x 0.80 = 0.020 mol, exactly enough, so no excess KOH remains.
questions.p: From the balanced equation, 0.010 mol of H₂SO₄ need 0.020 mol of KOH to react finish. Since the 0.020 mol of KOH wey you carry join body match am patapata, no excess KOH go remain.

questions.q: Which of the following pH values best represents a solution that is weakly alkaline, such as a dilute solution of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) used in some antacid preparations?
questions.e: A weakly alkaline solution has a pH slightly above 7 but not strongly basic. A pH of 8 fits this description, while 2 and 5 are acidic, and 13 represents a strongly alkaline solution.
questions.p: Weakly alkaline solution suppose get pH wey dey slightly pass 7. Na pH of 8 correct for dis matter, because 2 and 5 na acid, and 13 strong pass.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Na + Cl₂ -> 2NaCl, what name is given to the type of reaction in which an atom loses electrons to form a cation?
questions.e: Sodium atoms lose electrons to form Na+ ions. Loss of electrons is called oxidation.
questions.p: Sodium atom dey lose electron to form Na+ ion. We dey call dis loss of electron as oxidation.

questions.q: Which pair of oxidation numbers represents nitrogen correctly in NO and NO₂ respectively?
questions.e: In NO, oxygen is -2, so nitrogen is +2. In NO₂, two oxygens give -4, so nitrogen is +4.
questions.p: For NO, oxygen na -2, so nitrogen must be +2. For NO₂, two oxygens give -4, meaning nitrogen na +4.

questions.q: A student is asked to classify substances as oxidising agents or reducing agents. Which of these species is best described strictly as an oxidising agent in typical redox reactions?
questions.e: Cr₂O₇(2-) has chromium in its highest common oxidation state (+6) and readily gains electrons, being reduced to Cr₃+, so it oxidises other substances. The other species tend to lose electrons instead.
questions.p: Cr₂O₇(2-) get chromium for im highest oxidation state (+6) and e dey quick gain electron, so e dey oxidize other things. Na him be proper oxidizing agent here.

questions.q: Consider the half-reaction: Cr₂O₇(2-) + 14H+ + 6e- -> 2Cr₃+ + 7H₂O. What is the change in oxidation number of each chromium atom as it goes from Cr₂O₇(2-) to Cr₃+?
questions.e: In Cr₂O₇(2-), each chromium is +6 (since total charge is -2 and oxygens contribute -14). In Cr₃+ it is +3, so each chromium atom's oxidation number decreases by 3.
questions.p: For Cr₂O₇(2-), each chromium na +6. When e change go Cr₃+, im oxidation number come decrease by 3.

questions.q: In the reaction 2KMnO₄ + 16HCl -> 2KCl + 2MnCl₂ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O, what mass of chlorine gas (in grams) is produced when 0.4 mole of KMnO₄ reacts completely with excess hydrochloric acid? [Cl = 35.5]
questions.e: From the equation, 2 mol KMnO₄ produces 5 mol Cl₂, so 0.4 mol KMnO₄ produces (5/2) x 0.4 = 1.0 mol Cl₂. Mass of Cl₂ = 1.0 x (2 x 35.5) = 71.0 g.
questions.p: From di equation, 2 mol of KMnO₄ go produce 5 mol of Cl₂, so 0.4 mol go give 1.0 mol of Cl₂. When you multiply 1.0 mol by molar mass (71 g/mol), you go get 71.0 g.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a disproportionation reaction?
o: A reaction in which an acid reacts with a base to form salt and water
A reaction in which two different elements exchange oxidation states
A reaction in which the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced
A reaction in which an element is oxidised only
questions.e: Disproportionation occurs when atoms of the same element in one compound are both oxidised and reduced, forming two different products with different oxidation numbers. An example is Cl₂ reacting with cold NaOH.
questions.p: Disproportionation reaction happen when di same element dey undergo oxidation and reduction at di same time inside reaction.

questions.q: Iodine reacts with hot concentrated sodium hydroxide to form sodium iodide, NaI, and sodium trioxoiodate(V), NaIO₃, according to the equation 3I₂ + 6NaOH -> 5NaI + NaIO₃ + 3H₂O. What is the oxidation number of iodine in NaIO₃?
questions.e: In NaIO₃, sodium is +1 and each oxygen is -2, giving total -6 from oxygens. For the compound to be neutral, iodine must be +5.
questions.p: Inside NaIO₃, sodium na +1 and oxygen na -2 for three places, wey give -6. To make everything balance to zero, iodine must be +5.

questions.q: A redox titration uses the equation: 5Fe₂+ + MnO₄- + 8H+ -> 5Fe₃+ + Mn₂+ + 4H₂O. If 25.0 cm3 of 0.10 mol/dm3 KMnO₄ solution exactly reacts with a Fe₂+ solution, how many moles of Fe₂+ were present?
questions.e: Moles of KMnO₄ used = 0.025 dm3 x 0.10 mol/dm3 = 0.0025 mol. Since the ratio of Fe₂+ to MnO₄- is 5:1, moles of Fe₂+ = 5 x 0.0025 = 0.0125 mol.
questions.p: Number of moles for KMnO₄ na 0.025 dm3 times 0.10 mol/dm3, wey give 0.0025 mol. Since ratio na 5:1, you multiply 0.0025 by 5 to get 0.0125 mol of Fe₂+.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why molten lead(II) bromide conducts electricity but solid lead(II) bromide does not?
o: In the molten state, the ions are free to move and carry charge, but in the solid state the ions are held in fixed positions
The molten state has a higher temperature which generates new charged particles
Solid lead(II) bromide has no ions at all, while molten lead(II) bromide contains ions
In the molten state, electrons move freely through the liquid, but in the solid state electrons are fixed
questions.e: Ionic solids have ions locked in a rigid lattice, so they cannot move to conduct electricity. On melting, the lattice breaks down and the ions become mobile, allowing conduction.
questions.p: Na solid state, ions no dey move because dem lock for rigid lattice. When e melt, the lattice break down, make ions free to carry charge and conduct electricity.

questions.q: A student set up an electrolytic cell with two platinum electrodes dipped in dilute sulphuric acid and connected to a battery. Which products are expected at the cathode and anode respectively?
o: Oxygen gas at the cathode and hydrogen gas at the anode
Sulphur dioxide at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode
Hydrogen gas at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode
Hydrogen gas at the cathode and sulphur gas at the anode
