questions.e: In dilute sulphuric acid, hydrogen ions are discharged at the cathode to form hydrogen gas, while hydroxide ions from water are discharged at the anode to form oxygen gas. Sulphate ions are not discharged because they are more difficult to oxidise than hydroxide ions.
questions.p: For dilute sulphuric acid, hydrogen ions go cathode to produce hydrogen gas. Meanwhile, hydroxide ions go anode to produce oxygen gas because sulphate ions hard to oxidise.

questions.q: In the industrial electrolysis of brine (concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution) using a diaphragm cell, which pair of products is obtained at the cathode and anode respectively?
questions.e: At the cathode, water is preferentially discharged over sodium ions, producing hydrogen gas, while at the anode, chloride ions are discharged in preference to hydroxide ions because the solution is concentrated, producing chlorine gas.
questions.p: For brine electrolysis, water discharge for cathode to give hydrogen gas. For anode, chloride ions win hydroxide ions because the solution dey concentrated, so chlorine gas dey come out.

questions.q: Chidinma set up two electrolytic cells in series: one containing molten zinc chloride and the other containing an aqueous solution of tin(II) chloride, both using inert electrodes. If 0.20 mole of zinc was deposited in the first cell, how many moles of tin would be deposited in the second cell?
questions.e: Since the cells are in series, the same quantity of electricity (same number of faradays) passes through both. Both zinc and tin ions are discharged by gaining 2 electrons each (Zn₂+ and Sn₂+), so equal moles of electrons deposit equal moles of each metal, giving 0.20 mole of tin.
questions.p: As the cells dey series, the same current dey pass through both. Since both Zn₂+ and Sn₂+ need 2 electrons each, the same mole of electrons go deposit equal moles of zinc and tin.

questions.q: Which property of an electrolyte explains why aqueous solutions of electrolytes are good conductors of electricity while pure water is a poor conductor?
o: Pure water has a lower density than electrolyte solutions
Aqueous electrolyte solutions contain a high concentration of mobile ions, while pure water has very few ions
Electrolyte solutions contain free electrons that move through the liquid
Aqueous electrolyte solutions have a higher boiling point than pure water
questions.e: Conduction in electrolytes depends on the presence of free-moving ions, not electrons. Pure water ionises only very slightly, so it has far fewer ions than a solution of a dissolved electrolyte.
questions.p: Na mobile ions dey make electrolyte solutions conduct electricity, no be free electrons. Pure water get small, small ions inside am, so e no fit conduct current well.

questions.q: A quantity of electricity deposited 3.0 g of copper from a solution of copper(II) sulphate. If the same quantity of electricity were passed through a solution of silver nitrate, what mass of silver would be deposited? [Cu = 64, Ag = 108]
questions.e: Moles of electrons used for copper = (3.0/64) x 2 = 0.09375 mol electrons, since Cu₂+ needs 2 electrons. Silver needs only 1 electron per ion, so moles of Ag = 0.09375, mass = 0.09375 x 108 = 10.13 g.
questions.p: Cu₂+ need 2 electrons, while Ag+ need only 1 electron. When you calculate the moles of electrons wey deposit 3.0 g of copper, use am multiply by the molar mass of silver to get 10.13 g.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes an electrolyte?
o: A substance that conducts electricity without undergoing any chemical change
A substance that dissolves in water to form a non-conducting solution
A substance whose molten or aqueous solution conducts electricity and is decomposed in the process
A substance that conducts electricity only in the solid state
questions.e: An electrolyte conducts electricity in molten or dissolved form and undergoes chemical decomposition during the process, unlike metallic conductors which conduct without chemical change.
questions.p: Electrolyte dey conduct electricity wen e dey molten or dissolve for water. As e dey conduct, chemical change dey happen inside am, unlike metal wey no dey change.

questions.q: During the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide using inert electrodes, which species migrates to the cathode and what happens to it there?
o: Pb₂+ ions migrate to the cathode and are oxidised to lead metal
Pb₂+ ions migrate to the cathode and are reduced to lead metal
Br- ions migrate to the cathode and are oxidised to bromine gas
Br- ions migrate to the cathode and are reduced to bromine gas
questions.e: The cathode is the negative electrode, so positively charged Pb₂+ ions are attracted there and gain electrons (reduction) to form lead metal.
questions.p: Cathode na negative electrode, so positive Pb₂+ ions go rush go there. As dem reach there, dem go collect electrons to turn to lead metal.

questions.q: A town council wants to electroplate iron gates with zinc to prevent rusting. In setting up the electrolytic cell for this process, which arrangement is correct?
o: The zinc is made the cathode and the iron gate is dipped in molten zinc chloride without a power source
The iron gate is made the anode and zinc is made the cathode, using a zinc salt solution as electrolyte
The iron gate is made the cathode and a carbon rod is used as the anode, using dilute sulphuric acid
The iron gate is made the cathode and zinc is made the anode, using a zinc salt solution as electrolyte
questions.e: In electroplating, the object to be plated (iron gate) is the cathode where the metal ion is deposited, while the plating metal (zinc) is the anode which dissolves to replenish the metal ions in solution.
questions.p: To plate iron gate, you must put am for cathode side. Zinc go dey for anode so e go dissolve and replace the metal ions wey dey inside the solution.

questions.q: In an experiment, the same quantity of electricity liberated 0.20 mole of a metal M from a solution of its trivalent salt. How many moles of electrons were involved in depositing this metal?
questions.e: A trivalent metal ion M₃+ requires 3 electrons to be reduced to M, so moles of electrons = 3 x 0.20 = 0.60 mole.
questions.p: Because the metal M na trivalent, e need 3 electrons to turn to metal. If you get 0.20 mole of the metal, you go multiply am by 3 to get 0.60 mole of electrons.

questions.q: Two electrolytic cells are connected in series: the first contains molten magnesium chloride and the second contains molten aluminium oxide. If 0.30 mole of magnesium is deposited in the first cell, how many moles of aluminium will be deposited in the second cell by the same quantity of electricity?
questions.e: Mg₂+ requires 2 electrons while Al₃+ requires 3 electrons, so moles of electrons = 2 x 0.30 = 0.60. Moles of Al deposited = 0.60/3 = 0.20 mole, since the same charge passes through cells connected in series.
questions.p: Mg₂+ need 2 electrons, so 0.30 mole of Mg use 0.60 mole of electrons. Since Al₃+ need 3 electrons, you go divide that 0.60 by 3 to get 0.20 mole of aluminium.

questions.q: Energy changes in chemical reactions are usually classified using which term for the energy content of a system at constant pressure?
questions.e: Enthalpy (H) is the heat content of a system measured at constant pressure. It is the quantity whose change (delta H) is reported for reactions.
questions.p: Enthalpy na di heat content of system when pressure dey constant. Na di quantity wey dem dey measure di change for when reaction happen.

questions.q: A student mixes dilute hydrochloric acid with sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution in a plastic cup and notices the cup becomes cold to touch. This observation shows that the reaction is
o: Exothermic, releasing heat to the surroundings
Endothermic, absorbing heat from the surroundings
questions.e: A drop in temperature means the reaction absorbed heat energy from the surroundings, which is the definition of an endothermic reaction. The surroundings cool because energy flows into the reacting system.
questions.p: If cup come cold, e mean say di reaction don absorb heat energy from di environment. Dem dey call dis one endothermic reaction.

questions.q: In a potential energy diagram for an exothermic reaction, which labelled distance represents the activation energy of the forward reaction?
o: The gap between the reactants' energy level and the products' energy level
The gap between the reactants' energy level and the peak of the curve
The gap between the products' energy level and the peak of the curve
The horizontal distance along the reaction coordinate axis
questions.e: Activation energy is the minimum extra energy reactants must gain to reach the transition state (the peak). It is measured from the reactants' energy level up to the maximum of the curve, not down to the products.
questions.p: Activation energy na di extra energy wey reactants need to reach di peak. E start from di reactants level go reach di top of di curve.

questions.q: Given the bond dissociation energies: C-H = 413 kJ/mol, O=O = 498 kJ/mol, C=O = 799 kJ/mol, O-H = 463 kJ/mol, estimate the enthalpy change for the complete combustion of methane: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) -> CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g), given methane has 4 C-H bonds, CO₂ has 2 C=O bonds, and water has 2 O-H bonds per molecule.
questions.e: Bonds broken: 4(C-H)+2(O=O) = 4(413)+2(498) = 1652+996 = 2648 kJ. Bonds formed: 2(C=O)+4(O-H) = 2(799)+4(463) = 1598+1852 = 3450 kJ. Enthalpy change = bonds broken minus bonds formed = 2648 - 3450 = -802 kJ/mol.
questions.p: If you calculate bonds broken and subtract bonds formed, you go get 2648 minus 3450. Dis one give -802 kJ/mol.

questions.q: A reaction mixture reaches equilibrium faster when a catalyst is added mainly because the catalyst
o: Provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy
Increases the average kinetic energy of the reacting molecules
Shifts the position of equilibrium towards the products
Increases the enthalpy change of the overall reaction
questions.e: A catalyst works by providing an alternative route for the reaction that needs less activation energy, so more molecules can react successfully per unit time. It does not change the equilibrium position or the overall enthalpy change.
questions.p: Catalyst dey make reaction fast by providing another road wey get lower activation energy. E no dey change di overall enthalpy.

questions.q: Using Hess's Law, calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction: C(graphite) + 1/2 O₂(g) -> CO(g), given that the enthalpy of combustion of carbon to CO₂ is -394 kJ/mol and the enthalpy of combustion of CO to CO₂ is -283 kJ/mol.
questions.e: Using Hess's cycle: C + O₂ -> CO₂ (-394 kJ) and CO + 1/2O₂ -> CO₂ (-283 kJ). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives C + 1/2O₂ -> CO with enthalpy = -394 - (-283) = -111 kJ/mol.
questions.p: If you apply Hess Law and minus di second equation from di first one, you go get -394 minus -283, wey give -111 kJ/mol.

questions.q: Which type of enthalpy change refers to the heat change when one mole of a solid ionic compound dissolves completely in a large excess of water, such that further dilution causes no further heat change?
questions.e: Enthalpy of solution is specifically defined as the heat change when one mole of a solute dissolves fully in enough water to prevent further heat change on dilution. The other terms describe different standard enthalpy changes.
questions.p: Enthalpy of solution na di heat change when one mole of substance dissolve well well inside water. Dem no dey mix am up with neutralisation.

questions.q: 70 g of water (specific heat capacity = 4.2 J/g°C) in a calorimeter rises in temperature from 25°C to 39°C when a small quantity of solid X is dissolved in it. Calculate the heat energy released during the dissolution process.
questions.e: Heat released, Q = mass x specific heat capacity x temperature change = 70 x 4.2 x (39-25) = 70 x 4.2 x 14 = 4116 J. This confirms the dissolution process is exothermic.
questions.p: To find heat energy, multiply mass, specific heat capacity and temperature change together. 70 times 4.2 times 14 go give you 4116 J.

questions.q: A reaction is said to be exothermic when
o: the enthalpy of the products is greater than that of the reactants and heat is absorbed
the activation energy of the forward reaction is greater than that of the reverse reaction only
the enthalpy of the reactants equals that of the products and no heat is exchanged
the enthalpy of the reactants is greater than that of the products and heat is released to the surroundings
questions.e: In an exothermic reaction, reactants have more stored energy than the products, so the extra energy is given off as heat to the surroundings. This makes delta H negative.
questions.p: For exothermic reaction, reactants get higher stored energy pass the products, so the extra energy dey commot as heat go surroundings. Dis one dey make delta H negative.

questions.q: When ammonium trioxonitrate(V) (NH₄NO₃) dissolves in water, the temperature of the solution drops noticeably, and the test tube feels cold to touch. This observation shows that the dissolution process is
o: exothermic, because energy is released to the surroundings
endothermic, because energy is absorbed from the surroundings
exothermic, because the lattice energy exceeds the hydration energy
neither exothermic nor endothermic since no new bonds are formed
questions.e: A fall in temperature means the surroundings lost heat to the system, so the process absorbed energy. This makes the dissolution endothermic, consistent with ammonium trioxonitrate(V) being a common example of a cooling salt.
questions.p: If temperature fall down, e mean say heat absorb from surroundings enter the system. Dis make the process endothermic as ammonium trioxonitrate(V) (NH₄NO₃) dey dissolve.

questions.q: In a potential energy diagram for a reversible reaction, the activation energy of the forward reaction is 80 kJ/mol while the activation energy of the reverse reaction is 55 kJ/mol. What is the enthalpy change, delta H, for the forward reaction?
questions.e: Delta H for the forward reaction equals the forward activation energy minus the reverse activation energy, that is 80 minus 55, giving +25 kJ/mol. The positive sign shows the forward reaction is endothermic.
questions.p: Delta H for forward reaction na forward activation energy minus reverse activation energy, wey be 80 minus 55 to give +25 kJ/mol. The positive sign show say the reaction na endothermic.

questions.q: 150 g of water (specific heat capacity = 4.2 J/g°C) in an insulated plastic calorimeter is heated by burning a small sample of fuel, raising its temperature from 28°C to 48°C. What is the quantity of heat absorbed by the water?
questions.e: Heat absorbed equals mass times specific heat capacity times change in temperature, that is 150 x 4.2 x 20, which gives 12,600 J. This shows direct use of the calorimetry formula Q = mc delta T.
questions.p: Heat absorbed na mass times specific heat capacity times temperature change, wey be 150 x 4.2 x 20 to give 12,600 J. Dis na direct application of the formula Q = mc delta T.

questions.q: A chemistry student plots a potential energy (enthalpy) diagram for an exothermic reaction, showing reactants, products and a transition state (activated complex) at the peak of the curve. Which statement correctly describes this diagram?
o: The reactants and products are at the same energy level, with the hump showing heat released
The products lie above the reactants, and the hump between them represents activation energy
The products lie below the reactants, and the hump between them represents activation energy
The products lie below the reactants, and the hump represents the heat of reaction only
questions.e: For an exothermic reaction, products have lower energy than reactants, since energy is released overall. The hump above both levels represents the activation energy needed to form the activated complex, not the overall heat of reaction.
questions.p: For exothermic reaction, products dey down pass reactants because energy release. The hump for middle na activation energy wey dey needed to form activated complex.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains, in terms of bond energies, why burning natural gas (methane) in excess oxygen releases energy overall, even though energy must first be supplied to break the bonds in methane and oxygen?
o: No bonds are actually broken during combustion, only new bonds are formed
Bond breaking and bond formation always require exactly the same amount of energy
The energy absorbed in breaking bonds in methane and oxygen is greater than the energy released in forming new bonds
The energy released in forming new bonds in carbon(IV) oxide and water is greater than the energy absorbed in breaking bonds in methane and oxygen
questions.e: Combustion is exothermic overall because forming the strong C=O and O-H bonds in the products releases more energy than is needed to break the weaker bonds in the reactants. This net release of energy explains why delta H is negative for combustion reactions.
questions.p: Combustion dey exothermic overall because the energy wey form new bonds for carbon(IV) oxide and water pass the energy wey we take break bonds for methane and oxygen.

questions.q: Tunde investigated the effect of surface area on reaction rate by reacting excess dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with (i) a single large marble chip and (ii) the same mass of marble broken into many small chips. Which observation would he most likely record?
o: The small chips react faster because they present a larger total surface area for collisions
The large chip reacts faster because it dissolves without breaking apart
Both reactions proceed at exactly the same rate since the mass of marble is the same
The small chips react slower because they absorb more acid before reacting
questions.e: Breaking the marble into smaller chips increases the total surface area exposed to the acid. More surface area means more frequent collisions between acid particles and marble, so the reaction is faster.
questions.p: If you break marble into small pieces, you go get more surface area for the acid to touch. More surface area mean say particles go collide well-well, so the reaction go fast pass when you use one big lump.

questions.q: A student plots a graph of volume of gas collected against time for the reaction of magnesium ribbon with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. Which feature of the graph represents the average rate of reaction over the first 30 seconds?
o: The value of volume where the curve becomes horizontal
The gradient (slope) of the curve between time zero and 30 seconds
The intercept of the curve on the volume axis at time zero
The total time taken for the curve to flatten out completely
questions.e: Rate of reaction is the change in a measurable quantity, such as volume of gas, per unit time. On a volume-time graph, this is given by the gradient (slope) over the chosen time interval.
questions.p: Rate of reaction na how fast the volume of gas dey change with time. For graph, you go calculate the gradient between the time you want, which be the slope of the curve.

questions.q: In a reaction between sodium thiosulphate solution and dilute hydrochloric acid, a yellow precipitate of sulphur forms and gradually blocks the view of a cross mark placed under the flask. Increasing the temperature of the reaction mixture, while keeping concentrations constant, causes the cross to disappear faster mainly because
o: the concentration of hydrochloric acid increases as temperature rises
the sulphur precipitate becomes less visible at higher temperature regardless of collisions
the activation energy of the reaction becomes permanently lower at higher temperature
the reacting particles gain more kinetic energy, so more of them collide with energy equal to or above the activation energy
questions.e: Raising temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, so a greater fraction of collisions have energy at or above the activation energy. This results in more effective collisions and a faster reaction.
questions.p: When you heat the mixture, the particles go get more kinetic energy. This one make more particles get energy wey reach the activation energy, so the reaction go fast pass.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a solid catalyst used in powdered form is generally more effective than the same mass of catalyst used as a single large lump?
o: Powdered catalysts raise the activation energy needed, making collisions more effective
Powdered catalysts change the enthalpy of the overall reaction more favourably
The powdered catalyst provides a greater surface area, allowing more reactant particles to be adsorbed and react at active sites
Powdered catalysts react chemically with the products to speed up their removal
questions.e: A catalyst works by providing active sites where reactant particles are adsorbed and react. Powdering the catalyst increases its exposed surface area, so more active sites are available at a given time.
questions.p: Catalyst dey work for surface where reactant particles go sit down. If you grind the catalyst to powder, you go get more surface area and more active sites for the reaction to happen.

questions.q: In an experiment, 0.2 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid reacts with excess calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) at 27°C, and the rate of carbon(IV) oxide gas production is measured. Which of the following changes would NOT increase the rate of this reaction?
o: Using powdered calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) instead of large lumps
Increasing the temperature of the acid to 40°C
Increasing the concentration of the hydrochloric acid to 0.5 mol dm⁻³
Diluting the acid with distilled water to 0.1 mol dm⁻³
questions.e: Diluting the acid lowers the concentration of hydrogen ions, which reduces the frequency of effective collisions and therefore decreases, not increases, the rate. The other three changes all raise the rate of reaction.
questions.p: If you add water to dilute the acid, the concentration of hydrogen ions go reduce. This one go make the reaction slow down instead of making am fast.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the effect of a catalyst on the activation energy and the equilibrium position of a reversible reaction?
o: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both forward and reverse reactions but does not shift the equilibrium position
A catalyst raises the activation energy to slow down unwanted side reactions while shifting equilibrium towards products
A catalyst lowers the activation energy only for the forward reaction, thereby shifting equilibrium towards products
A catalyst has no effect on activation energy but shifts equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas
questions.e: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy for both the forward and reverse reactions equally. It speeds up the rate of reaching equilibrium but does not change the position of equilibrium.
questions.p: Catalyst dey provide new road with lower activation energy for both forward and backward reaction. E no dey change the equilibrium position, e only make the reaction reach there quick.

questions.q: In the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve of molecular energies for a gas sample, what does the area under the curve to the right of the activation energy value represent?
o: The number of molecules that have already reacted
The average kinetic energy of all the molecules
The fraction of molecules with enough energy to react on collision
The total number of molecules in the sample
questions.e: The area beyond the activation energy mark on the energy distribution curve shows the proportion of molecules whose energy equals or exceeds the activation energy, meaning they can react upon collision. This is a key idea linking temperature, energy distribution and reaction rate.
questions.p: That area wey dey past activation energy for the curve dey show the amount of molecules wey get energy wey reach or pass activation energy to fit react. E dey connect temperature, energy distribution and reaction rate together.

questions.q: Chidinma carried out an experiment to study how temperature affects the rate of reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid and sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution by measuring the time for a fixed volume of carbon(IV) oxide gas to be collected. Which of the following best explains why raising the temperature increases the rate of this reaction?
o: Raising the temperature increases the concentration of the reacting particles
Raising the temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, so more collisions have energy equal to or above the activation energy
Raising the temperature reduces the number of collisions between particles
Raising the temperature increases the activation energy needed for the reaction
questions.e: A rise in temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so they move faster and collide more often with greater energy. This increases the fraction of collisions that reach or exceed the activation energy, speeding up the reaction.
questions.p: When you increase temperature, particles dey get more kinetic energy and dem dey move fast to collide well. This one mean say more collisions go reach activation energy make reaction fast.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes a homogeneous catalyst in a chemical reaction?
o: It exists in a different physical state from the reactants and acts only on the surface
It is always consumed completely by the end of the reaction
It exists in the same physical state as the reactants and forms part of the same reaction mixture
It only works for reactions involving gases, never solutions
questions.e: A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants, for example a dissolved catalyst in an aqueous reaction mixture, so it mixes uniformly with them. It speeds up the reaction without being used up, unlike heterogeneous catalysts which act at a surface between different phases.
questions.p: Homogeneous catalyst dey share the same physical state with reactants like solution. E dey help speed up the reaction without make dem consume am finish.

questions.q: A reaction between 1.0 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid and excess magnesium ribbon is studied at 25°C, and the volume of hydrogen gas is measured every 30 seconds. Which of the following changes to the experimental setup would NOT increase the initial rate of this reaction?
o: Using a larger flask while keeping all other quantities the same
Using powdered magnesium instead of magnesium ribbon
Increasing the concentration of the hydrochloric acid to 2.0 mol dm⁻³
Carrying out the reaction at 45°C instead of 25°C
questions.e: Changing only the size of the flask does not alter the concentration, surface area, or temperature of the reacting substances, so the rate stays the same. The other three options each directly raise the frequency or energy of effective collisions, increasing the rate.
questions.p: To just change flask size no dey affect concentration, surface area or temperature of reactants. Na why the rate no go change at all.

questions.q: For the reaction X + 2Y -> Z, the rate law was found experimentally to be Rate = k[X][Y]². If the concentration of X is tripled while the concentration of Y is kept constant, by what factor does the rate of reaction change?
questions.e: Since the rate depends on the first power of the concentration of X, tripling the concentration of X alone multiplies the rate by 3 to the power 1, which is 3. The concentration of Y does not change, so its contribution to the rate stays the same.
questions.p: Because the rate law show say power of X na one, if you triple X concentration, the rate go multiply by 3. Y no change, so e own contribution remain constant.

questions.q: In a study of the reaction between zinc granules and dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, a graph of volume of hydrogen gas produced against time was plotted. Which feature of this graph indicates that the reaction has gone to completion?
o: The curve showing a sudden drop in volume
The curve rising steeply from the origin
The curve passing through the origin at a constant slope
The curve becoming a horizontal straight line
questions.e: When the curve becomes flat and horizontal, it means no more gas is being produced, showing that one of the reactants has been fully used up and the reaction has stopped. A steep rise instead shows a fast ongoing reaction, not its completion.
questions.p: If the graph curve become horizontal line, e mean say gas no dey produce again. E show say reaction don finish because reactant don finish.

questions.q: In an experiment on the decomposition of aqueous hydrogen peroxide using manganese(IV) oxide as catalyst, a student recorded the following volumes of oxygen gas collected over time: at 20 seconds, 24 cm³; at 40 seconds, 40 cm³; at 60 seconds, 48 cm³. Between 20 seconds and 60 seconds, what is the average rate of the reaction in cm³ of gas per second?
questions.e: The change in volume from 20 to 60 seconds is 48 minus 24, which equals 24 cm³, over a time interval of 40 seconds. Dividing 24 cm³ by 40 seconds gives an average rate of 0.60 cm³ per second.
questions.p: To find average rate, you go minus 24 cm³ from 48 cm³ to get 24 cm³, then divide am by the time interval of 40 seconds. When you divide 24 by 40, you go get 0.60 cm³ per second.

questions.q: In a reversible chemical reaction that has attained a state of dynamic equilibrium, which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: The reaction can only proceed in the forward direction
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
The concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
The forward and reverse reactions have stopped completely
questions.e: At dynamic equilibrium, both forward and reverse reactions continue to occur but at equal rates, so the concentrations of species remain constant, not necessarily equal. The reaction does not stop.
questions.p: For dynamic equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction dey equal the rate of the reverse reaction. The reaction no dey stop, and the concentration of reactants and products no suppose equal, just say dem dey constant.

questions.q: For the equilibrium system: 2NO(g) + Cl₂(g) <=> 2NOCl(g), Delta H = -77 kJ/mol, which combination of changes will BOTH favour an increase in the yield of NOCl?
o: Increasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature
Increasing the pressure and increasing the temperature
Decreasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature
Decreasing the pressure and increasing the temperature
questions.e: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles, favouring NOCl. Since the reaction is exothermic, lowering temperature also favours the forward reaction and more NOCl.
questions.p: Because 3 moles of gas dey left and 2 moles dey right, increasing pressure go push equilibrium go the side wey get small moles. Since Delta H be -77 kJ/mol, cooling down the system go make the forward reaction produce more NOCl.

questions.q: Consider the equilibrium: 2A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g). If the total pressure on the system at equilibrium is suddenly doubled by reducing the volume, what will be the effect on the position of equilibrium and the value of Kc?
o: Equilibrium shifts towards C, and Kc remains unchanged
Equilibrium shifts towards A and B, and Kc increases
Equilibrium shifts towards C, and Kc increases
Equilibrium shifts towards A and B, and Kc remains unchanged
questions.e: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right, so increasing pressure by reducing volume shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gas moles, which is C. Kc depends only on temperature, so it stays the same even though the position of equilibrium changes.
questions.p: If you reduce volume to increase pressure, equilibrium go shift go C sake of say C get small gas moles. But remember say na only temperature fit change Kc, so Kc value no go change at all.

questions.q: A saturated solution of lead(II) chloride, PbCl₂, exists in equilibrium with undissolved solid according to: PbCl₂(s) <=> Pb₂+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq). What will happen if a soluble chloride salt, such as sodium chloride, is added to this saturated solution?
o: There will be no change in the position of equilibrium
The equilibrium will shift to the right, increasing Pb₂+ concentration
The equilibrium will shift to the left, and PbCl₂ will precipitate out
More PbCl₂ will dissolve to maintain equilibrium
questions.e: Adding sodium chloride increases the concentration of chloride ions, a common ion already present in the equilibrium. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts to the left to reduce the excess chloride ions, causing more solid PbCl₂ to form.
questions.p: When you put sodium chloride, Cl- ions go plenty inside water and cause common ion effect. Le Chatelier principle talk say the equilibrium go shift go left, so PbCl₂ go come out as precipitate.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why increasing the concentration of a reactant in a reversible reaction at equilibrium causes the equilibrium position to shift towards the products?
o: The activation energy of the forward reaction is lowered by the added reactant
The rate of the reverse reaction becomes zero immediately
The equilibrium constant, Kc, increases as reactant concentration increases
The system responds by consuming some of the added reactant to restore equilibrium conditions
questions.e: By Le Chatelier's principle, when a reactant is added, the system shifts in the direction that uses up some of the excess reactant, which is the forward direction, to re-establish equilibrium. The equilibrium constant itself does not change because temperature is unchanged.
questions.p: According to Le Chatelier principle, if you add reactant, the system go try to use am up by moving forward. This one mean say the equilibrium position go shift go products side.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant, Kc, for a reversible reaction depends on which of the following factors only?
questions.e: The value of an equilibrium constant changes only when temperature changes. Concentration, pressure and catalysts can shift the position of equilibrium but do not alter the numerical value of Kc at a given temperature.
questions.p: Na only temperature fit change the value of Kc. Other things like pressure or catalyst no dey change the value, dem only dey shift the equilibrium position.

questions.q: For the gaseous equilibrium: N₂O₄(g) <=> 2NO₂(g), at a certain temperature the equilibrium concentrations are [N₂O₄] = 0.50 mol/dm3 and [NO₂] = 0.20 mol/dm3. Calculate the value of Kc.
questions.e: Kc = [NO₂]² / [N₂O₄] = (0.20)² / 0.50 = 0.04/0.50 = 0.08. Only the correct squaring of the product concentration and correct substitution give this value.
questions.p: To get Kc, you go square the concentration of NO₂ and divide am by the concentration of N₂O₄. When you calculate (0.20)² divide by 0.50, you go get 0.08.

questions.q: A chemist studying the equilibrium A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g) finds that doubling the pressure of the system (by halving the volume) at constant temperature does not shift the position of equilibrium. What can be concluded about this reaction?
o: The number of gas moles is the same on both sides
The reaction involves a solid catalyst
questions.e: A change in pressure only shifts equilibrium when the number of moles of gas differs between reactants and products. Since here both sides have 2 moles of gas, pressure change has no effect on the position of equilibrium.
questions.p: Pressure no dey affect equilibrium if the number of gas moles for reactant and product side dey equal. For this reaction, both sides get 2 moles of gas, so pressure change no go do anything.

questions.q: Consider the equilibrium: H₂(g) + I₂(g) <=> 2HI(g), Delta H = +52 kJ/mol. A student wants to increase the yield of hydrogen iodide at equilibrium. Which single change would achieve this?
o: Increasing the total pressure of the system
Decreasing the temperature of the system
Adding an inert gas at constant volume
Increasing the temperature of the system
questions.e: Since the forward reaction is endothermic, raising the temperature favours the forward reaction, increasing HI yield. Pressure changes have no effect here since both sides have equal moles of gas, and an inert gas at constant volume does not change concentrations.
questions.p: Because the reaction na endothermic, if you increase the temperature, the reaction go move forward to produce more HI. Pressure no get effect here because the number of moles for both sides na the same.

questions.q: In the Haber process for ammonia production, nitrogen and hydrogen gases are passed over an iron catalyst at about 450°C and 200 atmospheres. Which statement correctly describes the role of the catalyst in this reversible process?
o: It shifts the position of equilibrium to favour more ammonia
It decreases the activation energy of only the forward reaction
It increases the rate at which equilibrium is attained without changing the equilibrium yield
It increases the equilibrium yield of ammonia
questions.e: A catalyst speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but the position of equilibrium and the yield of ammonia remain unchanged. It lowers the activation energy for both directions, not just one.
questions.p: Catalyst just dey make the reaction reach equilibrium fast, e no dey change the amount of ammonia wey you go get. E dey lower the activation energy for both forward and backward reactions.

questions.q: A sample of well water from Ikot Ekpene forms a lasting lather with soap only after it has been boiled. This observation shows that the water contains mainly dissolved
questions.e: Boiling removes hardness only when it is caused by calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), which decomposes on heating to form insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV). This is temporary hardness. The other salts listed cause permanent hardness that boiling cannot remove.
questions.p: Na only temporary hardness wey Calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) dey cause boiling dey remove. E dey breakdown to form insoluble Calcium trioxocarbonate(IV).

questions.q: Which property of the water molecule best explains its unusually high boiling point compared to hydrogen sulphide, H₂S?
o: Its ability to ionise completely in the liquid state
The presence of covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen
Extensive hydrogen bonding between water molecules
questions.e: Water molecules are held together by strong hydrogen bonds due to the high electronegativity of oxygen, requiring more energy to separate molecules during boiling. H₂S lacks significant hydrogen bonding, so it boils at a much lower temperature despite similar structure.
questions.p: Water molecules get strong hydrogen bonding because oxygen dey very electronegative, so e need plenty heat before e go boil. H₂S no get this strong bond, na why e dey boil quick quick.

questions.q: A water sample contains dissolved calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV). Which of the following correctly represents what happens when this water is boiled?
o: Ca(HCO₃)₂ remains dissolved and unreactive to heat
Ca(HCO₃)₂ decomposes to CaCO₃, H₂O and CO₂
Ca(HCO₃)₂ reacts with soap to form scum directly
Ca(HCO₃)₂ is converted to CaSO₄ which precipitates
questions.e: On boiling, calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) breaks down into insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), water and carbon(IV) oxide gas. The insoluble carbonate settles out, removing the hardness from the water.
questions.p: When you boil Ca(HCO₃)₂, e go break down give you CaCO₃ wey go precipitate, join with water and CO₂ gas. Dis one go comot the hardness.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most suitable method for softening water that is to be used in a steam boiler, where complete removal of both calcium and magnesium ions is required?
o: Passing the water through an ion-exchange resin
questions.e: Ion-exchange resins replace calcium and magnesium ions with sodium or hydrogen ions, removing both temporary and permanent hardness completely. Boiling only removes temporary hardness, and sand filtration does not remove dissolved ions.
questions.p: Na ion-exchange resin be the best method to comot both calcium and magnesium ions completely for boiler water. Boiling only dey remove temporary hardness.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the general effect of temperature on the solubility of most solid solutes and of gases in water?
o: Solubility of solids and gases both decrease as temperature rises
Solubility of solids generally increases while that of gases generally decreases as temperature rises
Solubility of solids generally decreases while that of gases generally increases as temperature rises
Solubility of solids and gases both increase as temperature rises
questions.e: Most solids dissolve better as temperature rises because the dissolving process absorbs heat. Gases, however, dissolve less as temperature rises because the dissolved gas molecules gain energy and escape more easily from the solution.
questions.p: As temperature dey high, solubility of most solid solutes dey increase because heat dey help them dissolve. But for gases, high temperature dey make them escape, so their solubility dey reduce.

questions.q: A student adds excess washing soda solution to a hard water sample containing dissolved magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI). What type of reaction occurs, and what happens to the hardness?
o: Hydrolysis occurs; magnesium ions are released into solution
Double decomposition occurs, forming insoluble magnesium trioxocarbonate(IV); hardness is removed
questions.e: Washing soda supplies trioxocarbonate(IV) ions which exchange with the sulphate ions in a double decomposition reaction, precipitating insoluble magnesium trioxocarbonate(IV). Removing the magnesium ions from solution eliminates the hardness caused by them.
questions.p: Washing soda dey do double decomposition reaction with magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) to precipitate insoluble magnesium trioxocarbonate(IV). Dis one go comot the hardness.

questions.q: A particular well water in Minna produces plenty of lather with soap without any prior treatment and no scum is formed. Which type of water best describes this sample?
questions.e: Soft water readily forms lather with soap and does not produce scum, unlike hard water which contains dissolved calcium or magnesium salts. Since the sample lathers easily without treatment, it is soft water.
questions.p: Soft water dey make lather quick-quick without any scum. Because this water no need treatment to lather, e mean say na soft water.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of ions, when present as dissolved salts in water, are mainly responsible for hardness of water?
questions.e: Hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium salts, which react with soap to form insoluble scum. Sodium and potassium salts of soap remain soluble, so they do not cause hardness.
questions.p: Na calcium and magnesium ions dey cause hardness for water. Dem dey react with soap to form scum, unlike sodium or potassium ions.

questions.q: 100 g of water at 20°C can dissolve a maximum of 32 g of ammonium chloride to form a saturated solution. What is the solubility of ammonium chloride at this temperature, expressed in mol/dm³? (Molar mass of NH₄Cl = 53.5 g/mol, density of solution assumed equal to 1 g/cm³, total solution mass = 132 g)
questions.e: Moles of NH₄Cl = 32/53.5 = 0.598 mol. Total solution mass is 132 g, and since density is 1 g/cm³, volume = 132 cm³ = 0.132 dm³. Solubility = 0.598/0.132 = 4.53 mol/dm³.
questions.p: We calculate moles as 32 divided by 53.5, which give 0.598 mol. Since volume na 0.132 dm³, we divide 0.598 by 0.132 to get 4.53 mol/dm³.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why ion-exchange resins are effective in softening hard water?
o: They add excess soap which binds permanently with calcium and magnesium ions
They convert dissolved calcium and magnesium ions into insoluble carbonates that are filtered off
They boil off the dissolved salts as steam, leaving pure water behind
They exchange sodium ions on the resin for calcium and magnesium ions in the water
questions.e: Ion-exchange resins contain sodium ions that are released into the water in exchange for calcium and magnesium ions, which become attached to the resin. This removes the hardness-causing ions from the water, softening it.
questions.p: Ion-exchange resin get sodium ions wey e dey swap with calcium and magnesium ions inside water. This one dey remove the hardness so the water go soft.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes why distillation is an effective method of removing hardness from water?
o: It converts calcium and magnesium ions into insoluble hydroxides that settle out
It precipitates calcium tetraoxosulphate(VI) as an insoluble solid
It vaporizes pure water and leaves behind all dissolved mineral salts in the residue
It passes the water through a bed of resin beads that trap the salts
questions.e: Distillation works by evaporating the water and condensing the vapour, leaving all non-volatile dissolved salts, including calcium and magnesium compounds, behind in the residue. The condensed water collected is therefore free of hardness-causing salts.
questions.p: Distillation dey boil water turn am to steam, then e condense am back to liquid. All the mineral salts wey cause hardness go remain for the bottom as residue.

questions.q: A solubility curve for a certain salt shows that its solubility increases steadily from 20 g per 100 g of water at 10°C to 80 g per 100 g of water at 90°C. A saturated solution prepared at 90°C using 250 g of water is slowly cooled to 10°C. What mass of salt crystallizes out on cooling?
questions.e: At 90°C, 250 g of water dissolves (80/100) x 250 = 200 g of salt. At 10°C, the same 250 g of water can only hold (20/100) x 250 = 50 g of salt. The difference, 200 - 50 = 150 g, crystallizes out as the solution cools.
questions.p: At 90°C, 250 g of water go hold 200 g of salt, but at 10°C, e go only hold 50 g. The difference of 150 g na the one wey go come out as crystals.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly explains why hard water is generally considered unsuitable for use in industrial steam boilers?
o: It forms a scale of insoluble calcium and magnesium salts that reduces heating efficiency and can cause pipe blockage
It reacts with the metal boiler to form a toxic gas that corrodes pipes
It increases the rate of evaporation of water, wasting energy
It lowers the boiling point of water, making the steam less effective
questions.e: When hard water is heated in boilers, dissolved calcium and magnesium salts decompose or precipitate to form a hard scale on the inner surfaces. This scale insulates the boiler, reduces heat transfer efficiency, and may eventually block pipes or cause boiler damage.
questions.p: Hard water dey form scale inside boiler when e heat up. This scale dey block pipe and make the boiler no dey heat well again.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major source of carbon(II) oxide (carbon monoxide) pollution in Nigerian cities?
o: Complete combustion of fuel in vehicle engines
Incomplete combustion of fuel in vehicle engines
Decomposition of plastic waste in landfills
Evaporation of petrol from storage tanks
questions.e: Carbon(II) oxide forms when carbon-based fuels burn without enough oxygen, which is common in vehicle engines especially in heavy traffic. Complete combustion instead produces carbon(IV) oxide, not carbon(II) oxide.
questions.p: Carbon(II) oxide dey form when motor engine burn fuel and oxygen no plenty well well, especially for hold-up. If combustion complete, na carbon(IV) oxide go come out instead.

questions.q: A greenhouse gas is best described as one that:
o: dissolves in rainwater to lower its pH
reacts with ozone to deplete the ozone layer
absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation, trapping heat in the atmosphere
reduces visibility by forming smog with sunlight
questions.e: Greenhouse gases like carbon(IV) oxide and methane trap infrared radiation reflected from the earth, warming the atmosphere. This is the greenhouse effect, different from ozone depletion or acid rain formation.
questions.p: Greenhouse gas like carbon(IV) oxide dey trap infrared radiation wey dey bounce from earth, and dis one dey make atmospheric temperature hot. Na im we dey call greenhouse effect, e no join with ozone depletion at all.

questions.q: Photochemical smog, common in cities with heavy traffic, is formed mainly through the reaction of nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons in the presence of:
questions.e: Sunlight provides the energy that drives photochemical reactions between nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust, producing ozone and other smog components near the ground. Without sunlight, these reactions do not proceed significantly.
questions.p: Sunlight na im dey give energy wey make nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from motor exhaust react to form photochemical smog. Without sun, dis kind reaction no dey happen well.

questions.q: Particulate matter from cement factories and bush burning is classified as a pollutant mainly because it:
o: causes respiratory diseases when inhaled and reduces visibility
lowers the boiling point of atmospheric water vapour
reacts with oxygen to form ozone in the stratosphere
increases the rate of photosynthesis in nearby plants
questions.e: Suspended solid particles can be breathed into the lungs, causing diseases such as asthma and bronchitis, and they also scatter light, reducing visibility (haze). The other effects listed are not associated with particulate pollution.
questions.p: Small small particles from cement factory and bush burning fit enter person chest and cause sickness like asthma, plus e dey make everywhere dim. E no get anything to do with photosynthesis.

questions.q: A gas sample of 800 cm³ collected near a refinery was found by analysis to contain 48 cm³ of sulphur(IV) oxide. What is the percentage by volume of sulphur(IV) oxide in the sample?
questions.e: Percentage by volume equals (48/800) x 100, which gives 6.0%. This shows how much of the air sample is made up of the pollutant gas.
questions.p: To find percentage by volume, you go divide 48 by 800 and multiply by 100, and your answer na 6.0%. Dis calculation show how much sulphur(IV) oxide dey inside the gas sample.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why acid rain damages buildings made of limestone (calcium trioxocarbonate(IV))?
o: The acid only discolours the surface without any chemical change
The acid changes the limestone into a stronger, more brittle material
The acid reacts with calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) to form soluble calcium salts that are washed away
The acid evaporates the limestone directly into carbon(IV) oxide gas
questions.e: Acid rain contains dilute sulphuric(VI) and nitric(V) acids that react with calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) in limestone, forming soluble calcium salts, water and carbon(IV) oxide. The soluble products are washed away, gradually eroding the structure.
questions.p: Acid rain get acid wey dey react with calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) for limestone to form salt wey water fit dissolve and wash away. As water dey wash am go, the building dey spoil small small.

questions.q: A factory burns a fuel containing sulphur impurities, releasing sulphur(IV) oxide at a steady rate. If the gas combines with atmospheric oxygen and water vapour over several hours before falling as rain, which transformation correctly represents what happens to the sulphur(IV) oxide in the atmosphere?
o: It evaporates completely and never returns to the earth's surface
It reacts with nitrogen gas in the air to form ammonia
It is reduced to elemental sulphur which settles as dust
It is oxidised to sulphur(VI) oxide, which then dissolves in rainwater to form sulphuric(VI) acid
questions.e: In the atmosphere, sulphur(IV) oxide is gradually oxidised by oxygen to sulphur(VI) oxide, which then combines with water to form sulphuric(VI) acid, a major component of acid rain. The other options do not reflect the actual atmospheric chemistry involved.
questions.p: For air, oxygen dey turn sulphur(IV) oxide to sulphur(VI) oxide, and when water join am, e dey form sulphuric(VI) acid. Na dis acid rain dey fall come ground to destroy property.

questions.q: Carbon(II) oxide (carbon monoxide) is considered a dangerous pollutant mainly because it:
o: Combines with haemoglobin in the blood to form carboxyhaemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport
Reacts with rainwater to form a strong acid that corrodes metals
Dissolves in water bodies and kills aquatic plants directly
Depletes the ozone layer by reacting with ozone molecules
questions.e: Carbon monoxide binds strongly to haemoglobin, forming carboxyhaemoglobin which prevents oxygen from being carried round the body. This makes it a poisonous gas even in small concentrations.
questions.p: Carbon monoxide dey join body with haemoglobin strong-strong to form carboxyhaemoglobin. Dis one dey stop oxygen make e no round the body, na why the gas poisonous.

questions.q: Eutrophication of a river near a farm settlement is best described as a process in which:
o: Excess nitrates and phosphates cause algal overgrowth, which later depletes dissolved oxygen as it decays
Heavy metals settle at the river bed and poison fish directly
Acidic rain lowers the pH of the river water below 4.0
Oil spillage forms a film that blocks sunlight from reaching the river bed
questions.e: Nutrient runoff from fertilizers causes algae to grow rapidly (algal bloom). When the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up dissolved oxygen, killing fish and other aquatic organisms.
questions.p: Wetin fertilizer dey carry enter river dey make algae plenty too much. When the algae die, bacteria dey chop them and use up all oxygen, na so fish dey die.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why particulate matter (soot and dust) from bush burning and cement production poses a serious health hazard to humans?
o: The particles increase the acidity of the air directly, burning the skin on contact
The particles combine with nitrogen in the air to form poisonous oxides of nitrogen
The particles react with oxygen in the lungs to form carbon(IV) oxide, which is toxic
The fine particles can be inhaled deep into the lungs, causing respiratory diseases and reduced visibility
questions.e: Fine solid particles suspended in air can be breathed into the lungs where they irritate airways and cause respiratory problems. They also reduce visibility by scattering light, which is why particulate pollution is a major concern.
questions.p: Small-small dirt particles fit enter person chest deep when e dey breathe air. Dis one dey cause cough, sickness for lungs, and make everywhere dim.

questions.q: An environmental science class in Minna measured the concentration of oxides of nitrogen, NOx, in air near a busy expressway and found it unusually high during rush hour. Which process in a car engine is mainly responsible for producing these oxides?
o: Evaporation of lead compounds originally added to petrol as anti-knock agents
Reaction between nitrogen and oxygen from the air at the high temperatures inside the engine cylinder
Combustion of unburnt hydrocarbons escaping from the fuel tank
Reaction between carbon(IV) oxide and water vapour in the exhaust pipe
questions.e: At the very high temperatures reached during fuel combustion in car engines, nitrogen and oxygen from the air combine to form oxides of nitrogen. These oxides are then released through the exhaust and contribute to photochemical smog.
questions.p: When engine hot well-well inside car, nitrogen and oxygen from air dey join body together to form oxides of nitrogen. Na through exhaust pipe them dey commot go air.

questions.q: Montreal-type international agreements on reducing chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) emissions were primarily introduced to address which environmental problem?
o: Acidification of lakes and rivers due to acid rain
Formation of photochemical smog in cities with heavy traffic
Depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer, which shields the earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation
Global warming caused by excess carbon(IV) oxide
questions.e: CFCs released chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that broke down ozone molecules, thinning the protective ozone layer. International agreements aimed to phase out CFC use to allow the ozone layer to recover and continue shielding living things from ultraviolet rays.
questions.p: CFC gas dey spoil ozone layer wey dey protect earth from sun radiation. Na why people come join hand make law make everybody stop to dey use CFC.

questions.q: Which practical measure would most effectively reduce the release of sulphur(IV) oxide into the atmosphere from a coal-burning power plant?
o: Increasing the height of the chimney stack so the gas disperses higher into the air
Burning the coal at a much lower temperature to slow down the reaction rate
Installing scrubbers that remove sulphur(IV) oxide from the flue gases before release
Mixing the coal with limestone powder before transporting it to the plant
questions.e: Flue-gas desulphurisation scrubbers chemically react with sulphur(IV) oxide in the exhaust gases, trapping it before it leaves the chimney, which directly reduces emissions. Increasing chimney height only spreads the pollutant over a wider area rather than removing it.
questions.p: To put scrubber for chimney na the best way to catch sulphur(IV) oxide before e escape enter air. If you just build tall chimney, pollution still dey.

questions.q: A sample of hydrogen gas is collected over water in the laboratory. Which of the following best explains why this method is suitable for hydrogen?
o: Hydrogen reacts with water to form a stable compound
Hydrogen is only slightly soluble in water
questions.e: Hydrogen does not dissolve appreciably in water, so it can be collected by downward displacement of water without much loss. It does not react with water under these conditions.
questions.p: Hydrogen no dey dissolve well inside water, so we fit collect am by pushing water comot. E no dey react with water too, so e dey safe.

questions.q: Chukwuemeka heated 9.8 g of pure potassium trioxochlorate(V), KClO₃, strongly in the presence of a manganese(IV) oxide catalyst until it fully decomposed to potassium chloride and oxygen gas. Calculate the volume of oxygen gas liberated at s.t.p. [K=39, Cl=35.5, O=16, molar volume of gas at s.t.p = 22400 cm³]
questions.e: Molar mass of KClO₃ is 122.5 g/mol, so 9.8 g is 0.08 mol. From 2KClO₃ -> 2KCl + 3O₂, moles of O₂ = 0.08 x 3/2 = 0.12 mol, giving volume = 0.12 x 22400 = 2688 cm³.
questions.p: Molar mass of KClO₃ na 122.5 g/mol, so 9.8 g give us 0.08 mol. From di equation, 0.08 mol of KClO₃ go give 0.12 mol of O₂, wey come give 2688 cm³.

questions.q: Which property of nitrogen gas makes it suitable for use as a protective atmosphere in sealed food packaging such as sachet water and biscuit wrappers in Nigerian factories?
o: It is chemically inert under ordinary conditions
It is denser than carbon(IV) oxide
It is highly reactive and bonds with oxygen
questions.e: Nitrogen has a strong triple covalent bond between its atoms, making it largely unreactive at room conditions. This inertness prevents spoilage reactions such as oxidation of packaged food.
questions.p: Nitrogen get strong triple bond wey make am no dey react anyhow. Because e no dey react, e dey stop food make e no spoil quick.

questions.q: In an experiment, excess dilute hydrochloric acid is added to 2.4 g of magnesium ribbon placed in a flask fitted with a delivery tube leading to an inverted measuring cylinder filled with water. What volume of hydrogen gas is expected at s.t.p.? [Mg=24, molar volume of gas at s.t.p = 22400 cm³]
questions.e: Moles of magnesium = 2.4/24 = 0.1 mol. From Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl₂ + H₂, one mole of magnesium gives one mole of hydrogen, so 0.1 mol of H₂ occupies 0.1 x 22400 = 2240 cm³.
questions.p: 2.4 g of magnesium na 0.1 mol. Since one mole of magnesium dey produce one mole of hydrogen gas, 0.1 mol go give us 2240 cm³.

questions.q: A gas jar of dry sulphur(IV) oxide is tested with a piece of moist blue litmus paper, and separately a gas jar of the same gas is tested with moist starch-iodide paper. What result would correctly distinguish sulphur(IV) oxide from chlorine gas in this pair of tests?
o: Both gases turn moist blue litmus red and turn starch-iodide paper blue-black
Sulphur(IV) oxide turns moist blue litmus red but does not turn starch-iodide paper blue-black, while chlorine turns starch-iodide paper blue-black
Sulphur(IV) oxide bleaches moist litmus paper permanently while chlorine has no effect on it
Chlorine turns moist blue litmus red only, with no bleaching action at all
questions.e: Sulphur(IV) oxide is acidic and turns moist blue litmus red but is not a strong enough oxidising agent to liberate iodine from starch-iodide paper. Chlorine, being a strong oxidising agent, displaces iodine from the iodide ions, turning starch-iodide paper blue-black, which distinguishes the two gases.
questions.p: Sulphur(IV) oxide na acid, so e go turn blue litmus red but e no fit change starch-iodide paper. Chlorine na strong oxidising agent, so e go turn starch-iodide paper blue-black.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the laboratory preparation of chlorine gas by the oxidation of concentrated hydrochloric acid with manganese(IV) oxide?
questions.e: Manganese(IV) oxide oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid to chlorine gas while it is itself reduced to manganese(II) chloride, with water as the other product. The equation must balance atoms and charge, which only the first option does correctly.
questions.p: Manganese(IV) oxide dey oxidize conc hydrochloric acid make e produce chlorine gas, water, and manganese(II) chloride. Na only the first equation balance well well for atoms and charge.

questions.q: 0.80 g of a metal M reacts completely with excess dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to liberate 0.02 mol of hydrogen gas according to the equation: M + H₂SO₄ -> MSO₄ + H₂. What is the relative atomic mass of M?
questions.e: From the equation, 1 mole of M produces 1 mole of hydrogen gas, so 0.02 mol of M reacted. Relative atomic mass equals mass divided by moles: 0.80 g divided by 0.02 mol gives 40.
questions.p: From the equation, 1 mole of M dey produce 1 mole of hydrogen gas, meaning 0.02 mol of M react. If you divide 0.80 g by 0.02 mol, you go get 40 as the relative atomic mass.

questions.q: A gaseous mixture contains nitrogen and hydrogen in the mole ratio 1:3, the exact ratio required for the Haber process. If 5 moles of nitrogen react completely with the available hydrogen and the reaction proceeds at 40% yield, how many moles of ammonia are formed? (N₂ + 3H₂ -> 2NH₃)
questions.e: At complete reaction, 5 moles of nitrogen would give 10 moles of ammonia based on the mole ratio in the equation. At 40% yield, the actual amount formed is 40% of 10, which is 4.0 moles.
questions.p: If the reaction go 100%, 5 moles of nitrogen suppose produce 10 moles of ammonia. But as the yield na 40%, you go multiply 10 by 0.4 to get 4.0 moles.

questions.q: In the blast furnace extraction of iron, the hot waste gases escaping from the top of the furnace are mainly used to
o: preheat the incoming blast of air
questions.e: The hot waste gases leaving the top of the blast furnace are passed through the Cowper stoves to preheat the incoming air blast, which improves fuel efficiency. This recycling of heat is a key economic feature of the process.
questions.p: Dem hot waste gas wey dey comot for top of blast furnace dey pass through Cowper stoves to preheat the incoming air blast. Dis one dey help save fuel and make the process work well well.

questions.q: Duralumin is an important light alloy used in building aircraft bodies mainly because it combines low density with
questions.e: Duralumin (an alloy of aluminium with copper, magnesium and manganese) is valued because it is light yet strong enough to withstand the mechanical stresses experienced by aircraft, unlike pure aluminium which is softer.
questions.p: Duralumin light well well and e get strong resistance to mechanical stress. Na why dem dey use am build aircraft body instead of ordinary soft aluminium.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the structure of an alloy such as bronze?
o: It is a homogeneous mixture formed when atoms of one metal replace or fit into the lattice of another metal
It is a layered compound joined only by covalent bonds
It is a pure compound formed by strong ionic bonds between the metals
It is a solution of a metal dissolved completely in water
questions.e: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and a nonmetal) in which atoms of one element occupy positions in, or substitute for atoms in, the crystal lattice of the other metal. This is different from a true chemical compound.
questions.p: Alloy like bronze na mixture wey dey uniform, where atoms of one metal fit enter or replace the crystal lattice of another metal. E no be ordinary chemical compound.

questions.q: In the extraction of aluminium, bauxite ore is first purified to obtain pure alumina before electrolysis. What is the main reason for this purification step?
o: Purification increases the amount of cryolite required
Impurities such as iron(III) oxide would otherwise be deposited at the cathode along with aluminium
Impure bauxite cannot conduct electricity at all
Pure alumina has a much lower melting point than bauxite
questions.e: Bauxite contains impurities like iron(III) oxide and silica, which if not removed, would also be reduced during electrolysis and contaminate the aluminium produced. Purifying bauxite to alumina first ensures a high purity metal is obtained.
questions.p: Bauxite get impurities like iron(III) oxide inside am. If dem no remove am, the impurities go reduce during electrolysis and spoil the purity of the aluminium.

questions.q: Which property of iron makes it necessary to convert it into steel by removing most of its carbon content and other impurities before large-scale structural use?
o: Cast iron containing high carbon is brittle and cannot withstand sudden shock
Pure cast iron is too soft and ductile for construction work
Cast iron does not conduct heat or electricity
Cast iron reacts explosively with atmospheric oxygen
questions.e: Cast iron from the blast furnace contains about 2 to 4 percent carbon, which makes it hard but brittle, so it cannot withstand sudden shocks or stress. Converting it to steel by reducing the carbon content improves its strength and toughness for construction purposes.
questions.p: Cast iron get too much carbon inside am, wey dey make am brittle so e fit break easily under shock. Na why dem must reduce the carbon to make am steel for building work.

questions.q: During the purification of blister copper by electrolytic refining, impurities such as silver and gold are not oxidised at the anode but instead collect below it. What is this valuable residue called?
questions.e: In electrolytic refining of copper, less reactive metals like silver and gold present in impure copper do not dissolve into solution; they fall to the bottom of the cell as a solid residue called anode mud, which is later collected and sold for its precious metal content.
questions.p: When dem dey refine copper, precious metals like silver and gold no dey dissolve; dem dey fall down for bottom as anode mud. Dem dey pack dis residue later because e valuable.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct general molecular formula for the homologous series of alkynes?
questions.e: Alkynes contain one triple bond, which removes two more hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbons. This gives the general formula CnH2n-2.
questions.p: Alkynes get one triple bond, so dem get two hydrogen atoms less pass alkanes. Na why di formula be CnH2n-2.

questions.q: A sample of an alkene decolourises bromine water rapidly. When 0.2 mol of this alkene is completely combusted, it produces 0.8 mol of carbon(IV) oxide. What is the molecular formula of the alkene?
questions.e: Moles of carbon = 0.8 mol, so carbon atoms per molecule = 0.8/0.2 = 4. An alkene with 4 carbons has formula C₄H₈, following CnH2n.
questions.p: If 0.2 mol of alkene give 0.8 mol of CO₂, e mean say one molecule get 4 carbon atoms. Since alkene formula na CnH2n, di answer na C₄H₈.

questions.q: In the laboratory preparation of ethyne gas, calcium carbide (CaC₂) is reacted with water. What is the other product formed alongside ethyne in this reaction?
questions.e: Calcium carbide reacts with water as CaC₂ + 2H₂O to form C₂H₂ and Ca(OH)₂. Calcium hydroxide is the common laboratory product used to generate ethyne gas.
questions.p: When CaC₂ react with water, e dey produce C₂H₂ and Ca(OH)₂. Na calcium hydroxide be di other product wey dey form.

questions.q: Which type of hybridization is exhibited by each carbon atom in an alkane molecule such as propane?
questions.e: In alkanes, every carbon atom forms four single sigma bonds arranged tetrahedrally. This arrangement corresponds to sp3 hybridization.
questions.p: For alkanes, every carbon atom dey form four single sigma bonds. Dis kain arrangement dey make dem get sp3 hybridization.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why benzene does not easily undergo addition reactions like typical alkenes?
o: Benzene has no double bonds at all, only single bonds
Benzene molecules are too large for addition reactions to occur
Benzene contains only sp3 hybridised carbon atoms
The delocalised π electron cloud in benzene gives it extra stability, making addition less favourable
questions.e: Benzene has a ring of six carbon atoms with delocalised π electrons spread evenly above and below the ring. This delocalisation lowers the energy of the molecule, making it more stable and favouring substitution over addition.
questions.p: Benzene get delocalised π electrons wey dey make am very stable. Dis stability dey make am prefer substitution reaction pass addition reaction.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon X has the molecular formula C₆H₆ and undergoes nitration with a mixture of concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulphuric acid at about 50°C to form a yellow oily liquid. What is the likely identity and class of X?
questions.e: The formula C₆H₆ with a high degree of unsaturation but resistance to the usual addition tests, combined with nitration using concentrated nitric and sulphuric acids to form nitrobenzene (a yellow oily liquid), identifies X as benzene. This nitration is a classic electrophilic substitution reaction typical of aromatic compounds.
questions.p: Di formula C₆H₆ plus di way e take dey react with concentrated nitric and sulphuric acid show say na benzene. Dis reaction na classic electrophilic substitution for aromatic compounds.

questions.q: A gaseous alkane has a vapour density of 29. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1). What is the molecular formula of the alkane?
questions.e: Molar mass = 2 x vapour density = 2 x 29 = 58. For alkanes CnH2n+2, C₄H₁₀ has mass 4(12)+10(1) = 58, which matches.
questions.p: Molar mass na two times vapour density, wey come give us 58. If you check alkane formula CnH2n+2, na C₄H₁₀ get that molar mass.

questions.q: A straight-chain alkyne contains 5 carbon atoms with the triple bond located between the second and third carbon atoms. What is the IUPAC name of this compound?
questions.e: A five-carbon chain is named pentane as the parent, and yne shows the triple bond. Numbering from the end nearer the triple bond gives the lowest locant, which is 2, so the name is pent-2-yne.
questions.p: Five carbon chain dey use pent, and yne mean say triple bond dey. When you count from the side wey near the triple bond, na number 2 e go carry, so na pent-2-yne.

questions.q: 0.5 mol of an alkene, CnH2n, was completely burnt in excess oxygen and produced 56.0 dm3 of carbon(IV) oxide gas measured at S.T.P. (Molar volume of a gas at S.T.P = 22.4 dm3/mol). What is the value of n in the alkene?
questions.e: Moles of CO₂ produced = 56.0 / 22.4 = 2.5 mol. Since each mole of alkene CnH2n gives n moles of CO₂, n = 2.5 mol CO₂ / 0.5 mol alkene = 5.
questions.p: Divide 56.0 dm3 by 22.4 dm3/mol to get 2.5 mol of CO₂. When you divide 2.5 mol of CO₂ by 0.5 mol of the alkene, you go get 5.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the industrial process by which benzene is converted to cyclohexane for use in the manufacture of nylon?
o: Electrophilic substitution with chlorine gas in the presence of sunlight
Oxidation with hot, concentrated potassium permanganate solution
Friedel-Crafts alkylation with an alkyl halide and aluminium chloride catalyst
Catalytic hydrogenation using hydrogen gas and a nickel catalyst under pressure
questions.e: Benzene reacts with hydrogen gas under high pressure in the presence of a nickel catalyst to saturate the ring, forming cyclohexane. This is an addition (hydrogenation) reaction, unusual for benzene because the ring must first be broken down by forceful conditions.
questions.p: Benzene dey join with hydrogen gas under pressure plus nickel catalyst to turn to cyclohexane. Na hydrogenation reaction be that.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon sample on analysis was found to contain 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass, and its molar mass was determined to be 42 g/mol. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1). What is the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon?
questions.e: Dividing percentages by atomic masses gives C: 85.7/12 = 7.14, H: 14.3/1 = 14.3, a ratio of about 1:2, giving empirical formula CH₂ (mass 14). Since 42/14 = 3, the molecular formula is C₃H₆.
questions.p: When you divide the percentage by molar mass, you go get ratio CH₂ wey get mass of 14. Divide the molar mass 42 by 14, you go get 3, wey mean say the molecular formula na C₃H₆.

questions.q: Ethanol can be produced industrially by two main routes: fermentation of carbohydrates using yeast, and catalytic hydration of ethene with steam. Which of the following is a correct advantage of the fermentation method over the hydration method?
o: It operates at a much higher temperature and pressure
It gives a much higher percentage yield of pure ethanol
It uses a renewable raw material obtained from plants
It produces ethanol free from water without further purification
questions.e: Fermentation uses sugars from crops such as cassava or sugarcane, which are renewable, unlike ethene from petroleum. The hydration process actually gives a higher yield and purer product, and needs high temperature and pressure with a catalyst.
questions.p: Fermentation dey use crops like cassava or sugarcane wey dey renewable, unlike ethene wey come from petroleum. Ethene hydration dey give higher yield and purer product, but fermentation better because e dey use renewable raw material.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between ethanoic acid and methanoic acid in terms of acid strength, and the reason for it?
o: Methanoic acid is a stronger acid because it lacks an electron-donating alkyl group that would destabilise the carboxylate ion
Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid because it ionises completely in water like a strong acid
Methanoic acid is a weaker acid because it has a longer carbon chain that stabilises the carboxylate ion
Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid because the methyl group withdraws electrons strongly from the carboxyl group
questions.e: The methyl group in ethanoic acid is electron-donating, which destabilises the negative charge on the carboxylate ion and makes ethanoic acid a weaker acid than methanoic acid. Methanoic acid, having only hydrogen attached, does not have this destabilising effect, so it ionises more readily.
questions.p: Methanoic acid strong pass ethanoic acid because di hydrogen wey dey am no get electron-donating alkyl group like methyl group. Di methyl group for ethanoic acid dey push electron to destabilise di carboxylate ion, wey make am weaker acid.

questions.q: A fat molecule is a triester formed from glycerol and three long-chain fatty acids. When this fat is hydrolysed with water in the presence of a strong acid catalyst (acid hydrolysis), what are the two types of products obtained?
o: Glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids
questions.e: Acid hydrolysis of a fat breaks the ester linkages using water and acid catalyst to give back glycerol and the free fatty acids. Sodium salts (soap) are only formed when the hydrolysis is done with sodium hydroxide, which is saponification, not acid hydrolysis.
questions.p: Acid hydrolysis of fat dey break di ester bond to give glycerol and free fatty acids back. Na when you use sodium hydroxide you go get soap, but acid hydrolysis dey give free fatty acids instead.

questions.q: Soft soaps are generally produced by reacting fats or oils with a particular hydroxide, while hard soaps are produced using a different hydroxide. Which pair correctly matches the hydroxides used for soft soap and hard soap respectively?
questions.e: Soft soaps, which are more soluble and often used in liquid soaps, are made using potassium hydroxide, while hard soaps used as bar soaps are made using sodium hydroxide. This difference in the cation affects the physical form of the soap produced.
questions.p: Soft soap dey use potassium hydroxide because e dey make am more soluble, like liquid soaps. Hard soap dey use sodium hydroxide to make am strong bar soap.

questions.q: A synthetic detergent molecule has a long hydrocarbon chain attached to a sulphonate head group, unlike soap which has a carboxylate head group. What is the main advantage of this detergent over ordinary soap when used in hard water?
o: Detergents do not lower the surface tension of water, so they clean more gently
Detergents react completely with hard water ions to form a harmless precipitate that softens the water permanently
The sulphonate salts of calcium and magnesium remain soluble in water, so no scum is formed
The sulphonate group forms an insoluble scum with calcium and magnesium ions, which helps remove dirt faster
questions.e: Unlike the carboxylate salts in soap, the calcium and magnesium salts of sulphonate detergents are soluble in water, so they do not form the insoluble scum that ordinary soap forms in hard water. This makes synthetic detergents more effective for washing in hard water areas.
questions.p: Detergent better pass ordinary soap for hard water because calcium and magnesium sulphonate salts no dey form scum, dem dey dissolve well. Ordinary soap go form insoluble scum with hard water ions.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes nuclear fission from nuclear fusion?
o: Fission combines two light nuclei, while fusion splits a heavy nucleus
Fission releases no energy, while fusion releases large amounts of energy
Fission occurs only in the sun, while fusion occurs only in nuclear reactors
Fission involves splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei, while fusion involves combining light nuclei into a heavier one
