questions.e: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy, unstable nucleus into two or more lighter nuclei with release of energy. Nuclear fusion is the combination of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, also releasing energy. This is the correct distinction.
questions.p: Nuclear fission na when heavy nucleus break into small ones. Fusion na when two small nuclei join together to form one heavy one, and both dey release energy.

questions.q: A sample of a radioactive element has an initial activity of 800 counts per minute. After some time, the activity drops to 100 counts per minute. If the half-life of the element is 4 hours, how many hours have elapsed?
questions.e: 800 to 100 is a reduction by a factor of 8, which is 2³, meaning 3 half-lives have passed. Since one half-life is 4 hours, 3 half-lives equal 3 x 4 = 12 hours.
questions.p: If activity drop from 800 to 100, e mean say e don reduce by 8 times, which be 2 power 3. Since 3 half-lives don pass and one half-life na 4 hours, total time na 12 hours.

questions.q: In the nuclear equation: 94Pu-239 + 0n-1 -> 95Am-240 + X, what particle does X represent?
questions.e: Balancing mass numbers: 239 + 1 = 240 + mass of X, so mass of X is 0. Balancing atomic numbers: 94 + 0 = 95 + charge of X, so charge of X is -1, which matches a beta particle (0 charge... wait, beta has charge -1 and mass 0).
questions.p: If you balance the mass number, you go get 0. If you balance the atomic number, you go get -1. Na beta particle get 0 mass and -1 charge.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why nuclear reactions release far more energy than ordinary chemical reactions involving the same mass of material?
o: Nuclear reactions convert a measurable amount of mass directly into energy according to Einstein's equation
Nuclear reactions always occur at much higher temperatures than chemical reactions
Nuclear reactions involve rearrangement of electrons in the outer shell
Nuclear reactions require a catalyst while chemical reactions do not
questions.e: In nuclear reactions, a small amount of mass is converted directly into a large amount of energy, as described by Einstein's equation E = mc². Chemical reactions only involve electron rearrangement, which releases far less energy per unit mass.
questions.p: Nuclear reaction dey convert small mass to plenty energy using Einstein equation E = mc². Chemical reaction only dey move electrons around, so e no fit give that kain energy.

questions.q: A radioactive nuclide has a decay constant of 0.0231 per year. Calculate the half-life of the nuclide, in years. (Take ln 2 = 0.693)
questions.e: Half-life is calculated using the formula t(1/2) = ln2 / decay constant. Substituting values gives 0.693 / 0.0231 = 30 years.
questions.p: To find half-life, you divide 0.693 by the decay constant. If you divide 0.693 by 0.0231, you go get 30 years.

questions.q: A certain radioisotope used in carbon dating has a half-life of 5730 years. A wooden artifact found in an archaeological site in Benin shows that only 1/8 of the original Carbon-14 remains. What is the approximate age of the artifact?
questions.e: A remaining fraction of 1/8 equals (1/2)³, meaning 3 half-lives have passed. The age is therefore 3 x 5730 = 17190 years.
questions.p: If 1/8 of the carbon remain, e mean say 3 half-lives don pass. You just multiply 3 by 5730 years to get 17190 years.

questions.q: Which property is common to alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays emitted during radioactive decay?
o: They all have the same penetrating power
They can all ionize matter and affect a photographic plate
They all have the same mass
They all carry the same electric charge
questions.e: Although alpha, beta, and gamma radiations differ in mass, charge, and penetrating power, they share the common properties of being able to ionize matter and darken a photographic plate. This is why photographic film is used to detect radioactivity.
questions.p: Even though alpha, beta, and gamma get different power, all of them fit ionize matter. Dem all dey affect photographic plate too.

questions.q: A scientist is designing a device to generate electricity from the heat released by controlled splitting of heavy uranium nuclei in a power station. Which term correctly describes the type of nuclear process being harnessed, and what is the main hazard associated with its waste products?
o: Fission; the waste remains radioactive and harmful for a long time
Fusion; the waste produces excess oxygen gas
Fusion; the waste quickly turns into stable, non radioactive lead
Fission; the waste is completely harmless immediately after use
questions.e: Splitting heavy uranium nuclei to release energy is nuclear fission, as used in nuclear power stations. The main hazard of fission is that the waste products remain radioactive for long periods, requiring careful storage and disposal.
questions.p: Splitting uranium na nuclear fission. The waste wey come out from there dey radioactive for long time, so e dangerous for human being.

questions.q: Diamond and graphite are both allotropes of carbon but differ greatly in their physical properties. Which of the following correctly explains why graphite conducts electricity while diamond does not?
o: Graphite atoms are ionically bonded while diamond atoms are covalently bonded
Graphite contains metallic impurities that conduct electricity
Diamond has a lower density than graphite, which prevents electron flow
Graphite has free mobile electrons due to delocalised π electrons, while all four electrons of each carbon atom in diamond are used in covalent bonding
questions.e: In graphite, each carbon atom uses only three of its four valence electrons for covalent bonding within its layer, leaving one delocalised electron free to move and conduct electricity. In diamond, all four valence electrons of each carbon atom are involved in strong covalent bonds, so there are no free electrons.
questions.p: For graphite, each carbon atom dey use three electrons for bonding and leave one free to move and carry current. But for diamond, all four electrons tight well well for strong covalent bonds, so free electron no dey.

questions.q: A student heated 25.0 g of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), CaCO₃, strongly until it was completely decomposed. [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]. What mass of calcium oxide, CaO, was produced?
questions.e: CaCO₃ decomposes as CaCO₃ -> CaO + CO₂. Molar mass of CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol and CaO = 56 g/mol, so 25.0 g of CaCO₃ gives (56/100) x 25.0 = 14.0 g of CaO.
questions.p: As CaCO₃ dey break down to CaO and CO₂, we see say 100 g of CaCO₃ dey produce 56 g of CaO. When you calculate am for 25.0 g of CaCO₃, na 14.0 g of CaO you go get.

questions.q: Sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), NaHCO₃, is commonly used in baking and as an antacid. Which property of this compound makes it suitable as an antacid for treating excess stomach acid?
o: It is strongly alkaline and corrosive, so it destroys the acid completely on contact
It is insoluble in water and coats the stomach lining to block acid
It is a weak base that reacts with hydrochloric acid in the stomach to form a soluble neutral salt, water and carbon(IV) oxide gas
It reacts with stomach acid to form an insoluble precipitate that is excreted
questions.e: Sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) is mildly basic and reacts with hydrochloric acid in gastric juice: NaHCO₃ + HCl -> NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. This neutralises the excess acid gently without being too corrosive, relieving discomfort.
questions.p: NaHCO₃ na mild base wey dey help neutralize excess stomach acid sake of say e dey react with hydrochloric acid to form NaCl, water and CO₂ gas. E dey calm down belle pain without strong corrosion.

questions.q: A sample of water was suspected to contain dissolved calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), Ca(HCO₃)₂, which causes temporary hardness. Which of the following methods would effectively remove this type of hardness by decomposing the compound?
o: Boiling the water to decompose the hydrogencarbonate into insoluble carbonate
Passing the water through a charcoal filter
Adding dilute trioxonitrate(V) acid to the water
Adding excess sodium chloride to the water
questions.e: Temporary hardness is caused by calcium or magnesium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) dissolved in water. On boiling, Ca(HCO₃)₂ decomposes to insoluble CaCO₃, water and CO₂, which removes the hardness: Ca(HCO₃)₂ -> CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.
questions.p: Temporary hardness dey happen because of dissolved Ca(HCO₃)₂ inside water. When you boil am, e go break down to form insoluble CaCO₃, water and CO₂ gas, and this one go clear the hardness comot.

questions.q: In the industrial manufacture of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) (washing soda) by the Solvay process, which raw material provides the carbon(IV) oxide gas needed for the reaction?
questions.e: In the Solvay process, limestone (CaCO₃) is heated in a kiln to produce calcium oxide and carbon(IV) oxide gas: CaCO₃ -> CaO + CO₂. The CO₂ produced is passed into brine saturated with ammonia to form sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), which is later converted to washing soda.
questions.p: For Solvay process, dem dey heat limestone, wey be CaCO₃, make e produce carbon(IV) oxide gas and calcium oxide. Na that CO₂ dem dey use inside the process to make washing soda.

questions.q: Soap is produced industrially by boiling fats or oils with concentrated sodium hydroxide solution. This process is known as:
questions.e: The hydrolysis of fats and oils by an alkali such as sodium hydroxide to produce soap and glycerol is called saponification. Esterification is the reverse reaction that forms esters.
questions.p: When you boil fat or oil with alkali like sodium hydroxide, e dey produce soap and glycerol; we dey call dis process saponification. Esterification na di opposite reaction wey dey form esters.

questions.q: Hard water forms scum with ordinary soap but not with synthetic detergents. This is mainly because detergents:
o: are made from petroleum instead of animal fat
form soluble calcium and magnesium salts instead of insoluble ones
have a lower molecular mass than soap
contain long hydrocarbon chains that dissolve grease faster
questions.e: Soap reacts with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ ions in hard water to form insoluble scum, but the sulphonate or sulphate groups in detergents form soluble calcium and magnesium salts that do not precipitate. This is the key chemical advantage of detergents over soap in hard water.
questions.p: Soap dey react with Ca₂+ and Mg₂+ for hard water to form scum, but detergents get sulphonate or sulphate groups wey dey form soluble salts. Dis one make detergent better pass soap for hard water.

questions.q: A tablespoon of palm oil used by Mama Chidinma in her kitchen is best described chemically as a:
o: simple ester of a monohydric alcohol
triester of glycerol with fatty acids
questions.e: Fats and oils are triglycerides, formed when glycerol (a trihydric alcohol with three OH groups) reacts with three fatty acid molecules to form three ester linkages. This is why they are called triesters of glycerol.
questions.p: Fats and oils na triglycerides. Dem dey form when glycerol react with three fatty acid molecules to create three ester linkages, so we dey call dem triesters of glycerol.

questions.q: Which of the following tests is used to distinguish a reducing sugar such as glucose from a non-reducing sugar such as sucrose?
questions.e: Fehling's solution is reduced by reducing sugars like glucose, giving a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide on heating, while non-reducing sugars like sucrose give no colour change. The biuret test is for proteins and the iodine test detects starch.
questions.p: If you heat reducing sugar like glucose with Fehling's solution, e go give brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide. Non-reducing sugar like sucrose no go change colour at all.

questions.q: A 500 g sample of a vegetable oil requires 0.75 mol of potassium hydroxide for complete saponification. If the reaction produces glycerol and the potassium salts of fatty acids, how many moles of the triglyceride were present in the sample? (Each triglyceride molecule reacts with 3 moles of KOH.)
questions.e: Since each triglyceride needs 3 moles of KOH for complete saponification, the moles of triglyceride equal 0.75 divided by 3, which gives 0.25 mol.
questions.p: Because one mole of triglyceride need 3 moles of KOH to saponify, you go divide 0.75 by 3. Dis one give you 0.25 mol of di triglyceride.

questions.q: Proteins are polymers formed by the condensation of amino acid monomers through a specific bond. The linkage joining amino acid units together in a protein chain is called the:
questions.e: Amino acids join together by losing water between the carboxyl group of one molecule and the amino group of the next, forming a peptide (amide) bond. Glycosidic bonds instead link sugar units in carbohydrates.
questions.p: Amino acids dey join together when dem lose water between di carboxyl group and di amino group to form peptide bond. Glycosidic bond na for sugar units for carbohydrate.

questions.q: A student heats egg albumen solution strongly and observes that it becomes an insoluble solid mass that does not redissolve on cooling. This change is best explained as:
o: denaturation caused by disruption of the protein's native structure
formation of a new glycosidic linkage between protein molecules
hydrolysis of peptide bonds breaking the protein into amino acids
saponification of the protein's fatty acid side chains
questions.e: Heat disrupts the hydrogen bonds and other weak interactions holding a protein's three-dimensional shape, causing denaturation, which is irreversible coagulation as seen when egg white turns solid on cooking. Hydrolysis would require more than just heat and would break the chain into smaller units, not form a solid mass.
questions.p: Heat dey scatter di hydrogen bonds wey dey hold protein shape, and dis one dey cause denaturation. Na why egg white dey turn solid and e no fit go back to liquid again.

questions.q: Carbohydrates are generally defined as polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones (or compounds that yield them on hydrolysis) with the general formula Cx(H₂O)y. Which of the following is classified as a monosaccharide?
questions.e: Glucose is a simple sugar that cannot be hydrolysed into smaller sugar units, making it a monosaccharide. Sucrose is a disaccharide, while starch and cellulose are polysaccharides made of many glucose units.
questions.p: Glucose na simple sugar wey dem no fit break down again into another sugar, na im make am monosaccharide. Sucrose na disaccharide, while starch and cellulose na polysaccharides wey get plenty glucose inside.

questions.q: A fat molecule is formed when glycerol reacts with three fatty acid molecules. What is the name given to the type of bond formed between glycerol and each fatty acid during this reaction?
questions.e: Fats and oils are esters formed from the condensation reaction between glycerol (an alcohol) and fatty acids (carboxylic acids). This reaction produces an ester linkage and releases water.
questions.p: Fats and oils na esters wey dey form when glycerol and fatty acids join together. E dey produce ester bond and release water for the process.

questions.q: Ordinary soap, sodium octadecanoate, forms a scum when used with hard water. This scum is best described as:
o: An emulsified droplet of oil surrounded by water molecules
An insoluble calcium or magnesium salt of a fatty acid
A mixture of glycerol and sodium hydroxide
A soluble sodium salt of a fatty acid
questions.e: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions, which react with soap to form insoluble calcium or magnesium salts of the fatty acid. This insoluble precipitate is the scum, and it wastes soap before useful lather can form.
questions.p: Hard water get calcium and magnesium inside, wey dey react with soap to form insoluble salt wey be scum. Na this scum dey waste soap before foam fit show.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon chain of a soap molecule, such as in sodium hexadecanoate, dissolves grease and oil stains, while the ionic head dissolves in water. What term describes the non-polar hydrocarbon tail of the soap molecule with respect to water?
questions.e: The long hydrocarbon tail of a soap molecule repels water and dissolves in oily or greasy substances, so it is described as hydrophobic (water-hating). The ionic carboxylate head is hydrophilic and dissolves in water.
questions.p: The long tail of soap dey fear water and na oil e dey like, na im we dey call am hydrophobic. The head na hydrophilic because e dey dissolve for water.

questions.q: Starch and cellulose are both natural polysaccharides built entirely from glucose units, yet they differ greatly in properties; for instance, humans can digest starch but not cellulose. What mainly accounts for this difference?
o: Starch is a monosaccharide while cellulose is a disaccharide
Cellulose has a higher molecular mass than starch
Starch contains nitrogen atoms absent in cellulose
The glucose units in starch and cellulose are joined by different types of glycosidic linkages
questions.e: Starch and cellulose are both polymers of glucose, but the glucose units are linked by different glycosidic bonds (alpha-linkages in starch and beta-linkages in cellulose). Human digestive enzymes can break alpha-linkages but not beta-linkages, so cellulose passes through undigested.
questions.p: Starch and cellulose na both glucose polymers, but the way dem join different. Human body get enzyme wey fit break starch bond, but e no fit break cellulose bond.

questions.q: A 200 g sample of groundnut oil, assumed to be a simple triglyceride of relative molecular mass 884, is completely hydrolysed by boiling with excess sodium hydroxide solution. Calculate the number of moles of fatty acid salt (soap) produced, assuming complete saponification. (Relative molecular mass of oil = 884)
questions.e: Moles of oil = 200/884 = 0.226 mol. Each triglyceride molecule produces 3 moles of soap on hydrolysis, so moles of soap = 0.226 x 3 = 0.679 mol.
questions.p: First find mole of oil by dividing 200 by 884, wey give 0.226 mol. Because one oil molecule dey produce 3 moles of soap, multiply 0.226 by 3 to get 0.679 mol.

questions.q: Which property of synthetic detergents makes them more suitable than ordinary soap for use in areas with hard water, such as some parts of Nigeria where borehole water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts?
o: They lower the surface tension of water more than soap does
They are cheaper to manufacture on an industrial scale
They contain glycerol which prevents precipitate formation
They form soluble salts with calcium and magnesium ions instead of insoluble scum
questions.e: Synthetic detergents have sulphonate or sulphate groups whose calcium and magnesium salts remain soluble in water, unlike soap whose calcium and magnesium salts are insoluble and form scum. This allows detergents to lather well even in hard water.
questions.p: Synthetic detergents better pass ordinary soap for hard water because dia calcium and magnesium salts dey dissolve. E no dey form scum, so foam dey show well well.
